# Bosco Labs data APIs

> Bosco Labs publishes data tools for AI agents and analysts (HTTP API, remote MCP, x402 and Apify Actors) that return clean, typed JSON from official sources: SEC filings, insider trades, 13F holdings and XBRL financials, US House STOCK Act trades, European ESEF annual reports, UK/Danish/Norwegian company accounts and registries, sanctions lists, EU, UK and Dutch law and case law, EU tenders, US federal and Pentagon contract awards, ECB rates and euro inflation, clinical trials, drug safety, recalls, tariffs, package vulnerabilities and Dutch addresses. 30 tools are live: all 29 HTTP API tools are plain HTTPS endpoints and remote MCP tools that an agent can call with a key (prepaid credits) or without an account, paying per call in USDC via x402 (https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/<tool>, see API below); 30 of them are also Apify Actors on the Apify Store (pay per event). Data rows carry a source link.

Apify Store profile: https://apify.com/bosco_labs
Contact: support@boscolabs.dev

## Start here (free, no key)

- Plan a question: `curl -s -X POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/plan -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"question": "Is Rosneft on the EU sanctions list?"}'` returns the exact call, its input and its maximum price; a question it cannot answer is refused with `not_covered` instead of guessed
- Compact catalogue (one line per tool, ~10 KB): https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/tools?compact=true
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http bosco-labs https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp/free` (planner, tool descriptions, free LEI and SEC lookups); the paid tools are on https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp with your key
- Cursor: `{"mcpServers": {"bosco-labs": {"url": "https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp/free"}}}` in `.cursor/mcp.json`
- Paid tools: a key with $5.00 free credit (once per verified e-mail, no card): `curl -s -X POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/keys/request -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email": "you@example.com"}'` e-mails a one-time link; the page shows the key once. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` to the HTTP API or to https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp

## Finance & SEC

- [SEC Insider Trading API (Form 4): stock transactions since 2006](https://boscolabs.dev/sec-insider-trades.html): Every insider purchase and sale reported on SEC Form 4 (directors, officers, 10% owners), from official EDGAR filings, 2006 to today, with cluster-buy and cluster-sell signals; filter by ticker, CIK, transaction code, role, value and date. Price: Apify Store $0.0018 per transaction row and $0.02 per cluster signal; HTTP API $0.0002 per unit: a Form 4 transaction = 9 units ($0.0018), a cluster signal = 100 ($0.02). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-insider-trades))
- [SEC EDGAR Filings API: 8-K, 10-K, 10-Q feed since 1994](https://boscolabs.dev/sec-filings-feed.html): SEC EDGAR filings (8-K, 10-K, 10-Q, S-1, 13D, 13G, Form 4 and every other form) for any company or the whole market, live or back to 1994, from the SEC's own feeds; 8-K item codes and earnings releases (Item 2.02); links to each filing, not its text. Price: Apify Store $0.001 per filing; HTTP API $0.001 per filing. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-filings-feed))
- [Congress Stock Trades API: US House STOCK Act since 2014](https://boscolabs.dev/us-house-trades.html): Congress stock trades: stock, option, fund and bond trades that US House members disclose in STOCK Act Periodic Transaction Reports, from the Clerk of the House's official filings since January 2014 (no Senate); ticker, amount range, owner, days to disclose. Price: Apify Store $0.0018 per trade; HTTP API $0.0018 per PTR transaction. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/us-house-trades))
- [SEC 13F Holdings API: fund & ETF holdings, 13D/13G, Form 144](https://boscolabs.dev/sec-ownership.html): 13F institutional holdings and who owns a stock, from official SEC filings: a fund manager's 13F positions (new, increased, decreased or closed vs last quarter), mutual fund/ETF N-PORT holdings, funds holding a ticker, 5%+ stakes (13D/13G) and Form 144 planned insider sales. One ticker or fund in. Price: Apify Store $0.0018 per row, plus $0.01 per "who holds this stock" search (13F or N-PORT data set); HTTP API $0.0018 per holding, holder or filing row (one fund or company per call). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-ownership))
- [SEC Financial Statements API: income, balance sheet, cash flow](https://boscolabs.dev/sec-company-financials.html): Company financial statements from SEC EDGAR XBRL (10-K, 10-Q, 20-F): income statement (revenue, profit, EPS), balance sheet, cash flow, free cash flow and margins per fiscal year or quarter, 2009 to date, by stock ticker or CIK. Each value cites its XBRL tag and filing. Q4 derived if not reported. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per company-period row; HTTP API $0.005 per company-period row. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-company-financials))
- [SEC Company Screener API: filter all US filers by financials](https://boscolabs.dev/sec-company-screen.html): Stock screener on SEC EDGAR data. US companies matching your filters for one calendar year or quarter: revenue, net income, margins, cash flow, assets and 30 more metrics from SEC XBRL frames, sorted and capped. Each value cites its XBRL tag and SEC filing. Same metrics as SEC Company Financials. Price: Apify Store $0.002 per company returned; HTTP API $0.002 per company returned. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-company-screen))
- [EU Annual Reports API (ESEF): XBRL financial statements](https://boscolabs.dev/esef-annual-reports.html): Normalized key financials (revenue, EBIT, EBITDA, net income, EPS, assets, equity, cash flows, margins, growth) of European listed companies from official ESEF annual reports via filings.xbrl.org; 28 countries; every value linked to its XBRL fact. Price: Apify Store $0.01 per run plus $0.05 per annual report; raw XBRL fact rows, if switched on, $0.0005 each; HTTP API $0.05 per annual report. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/esef-annual-reports))
- [ISIN, LEI, CIK, FIGI & Ticker Resolver API (crosswalk)](https://boscolabs.dev/identifier-resolver.html): Issuer legal name, LEI, CIK, tickers, ISINs, FIGIs, CFI code and EU trading venues for one ISIN, LEI, CIK, ticker, FIGI or company name. Check digits validated first; a source URL per value. Data from GLEIF, OpenFIGI, SEC and ESMA FIRDS. Price: Apify Store $0.002 per resolved identifier; HTTP API $0.002 per identifier resolved. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/identifier-resolver))

## Companies

- [Counterparty Check API: KYB checklist from official registers](https://boscolabs.dev/counterparty-check.html): KYB checklist per company: register status, LEI, insolvency, recent accounts, sanctions (OFAC, UN, UK, EU) on company and officers, VAT (VIES), IBAN; pass, fail, review or unverified, sourced. Officers: UK, PL, NO, FR only. Insolvency: UK, PL, FR, DE, NL, NO, FI, EE, IE, CZ, LV; else unverified. Price: Apify Store $0.05 per company checked; HTTP API $0.05 per company checked; an ambiguous name (candidates) is free. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/counterparty-check))
- [Company Check API: due diligence, LEI, financials & SEC filings](https://boscolabs.dev/company-check.html): Company due diligence in one call: legal entity name, LEI, number, status, address, officers and owners, years of financials (revenue, profit, equity), SEC filings; UK Companies House charges, appointments and Gazette insolvency. By name, LEI, UK/DK/NO/FR/FI/EE/PL/IE/CZ/LV number, ticker or CIK. Price: Apify Store $0.03 per report; HTTP API $0.03 per company report. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/company-check))
- [VAT Number & IBAN Check API: EU VIES + IBAN validation](https://boscolabs.dev/vat-iban-check.html): Valid or not for EU VAT numbers (live from the official EU VIES service, with registered name, address and a name match) and IBANs (ISO 13616 check digits, length, bank code, country match). Pass, fail or unverified per check, with the source; unverified and malformed input are free. Price: Apify Store $0.002 per check with a definite answer; HTTP API $0.002 per definite check (VAT number answered by VIES, or a valid IBAN); malformed, failed and unverified are free. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/vat-iban-check))
- [Company Financials API: UK, Denmark (CVR), Norway accounts](https://boscolabs.dev/company-accounts.html): Financials (revenue, profit, equity, assets, cash, employees) of private and public companies from official accounts: UK Companies House, Denmark Erhvervsstyrelsen, Norway Brønnøysund; adds the LEI from GLEIF and a source per value. Price: Apify Store $0.04 per company-year; HTTP API $0.04 per company-year. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/company-accounts))
- [UK New Companies API: daily Companies House incorporations](https://boscolabs.dev/uk-new-companies.html): New UK companies incorporated on any day (default: yesterday) from the official Companies House API: number, name, type, status, SIC codes with descriptions, registered office address and a register link. Filter by SIC prefix, location and type. No director data. Price: Apify Store $0.002 per company; HTTP API $0.002 per company returned. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/uk-new-companies))
- [Company Hiring Signals API: open roles, departments, locations](https://boscolabs.dev/company-hiring-signals.html): Is a company hiring? Open roles by department, location and remote share, newest and oldest posting dates and top titles, plus job rows with a link each. Read from the company's public Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby job board. Look up by name, domain or board URL. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per company found plus $0.001 per job row; HTTP API $0.001 per unit: a company summary = 5 units ($0.005), a job row = 1 ($0.001); companies without a public job board are free. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/company-hiring-signals))

## Compliance & law

- [Sanctions List Screening API: OFAC, UK, EU, UN & US lists](https://boscolabs.dev/sanctions-screening.html): Sanctions list screening and search: is this company, vessel, person or crypto wallet sanctioned? Per name or address (fuzzy, alias-aware): yes/no, the listed entry, aliases, programs, source link, from OFAC SDN and non-SDN, the US Consolidated Screening List, UK, EU and UN Security Council lists. Price: Apify Store $0.01 per name or wallet address screened; HTTP API $0.01 per name or wallet address screened (an address no list could be checked against is free). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sanctions-screening))
- [EU Law Lookup API (EUR-Lex): article text, in force, amendments](https://boscolabs.dev/eu-law-lookup.html): The text of an EU law article as in force today (or on a date), whether the act is in force, what amended it, plus new Official Journal acts. Ask by name (GDPR, AI Act), citation, CELEX or ELI; 24 languages. Official EUR-Lex/Cellar data with a source link per row. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per act or article returned; HTTP API $0.005 per act or article returned. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/eu-law-lookup))
- [UK & Dutch Law Lookup API: article text by date, in force](https://boscolabs.dev/national-law-lookup.html): The text of a UK section or Dutch article as in force today (or on a date), whether it is in force and what changed it. Ask by citation: "Companies Act 2006 s 172", "BW 7:658", "artikel 13 Wet Vpb 1969". Official legislation.gov.uk and Dutch BWB data with a source link per row. Price: Apify Store $0.01 per article or act returned; HTTP API $0.005 per article or act returned. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/national-law-lookup))
- [Dutch Case Law API (Rechtspraak): court rulings by ECLI](https://boscolabs.dev/dutch-case-law.html): Dutch court rulings (uitspraken) by ECLI or by keyword, court and date: case numbers, legal area, summary (inhoudsindicatie), appeal/cassation links, law references, full text on request. Hoge Raad (Supreme Court), Raad van State, appeal and district courts. Official Rechtspraak Open Data, sourced. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per decision returned; HTTP API $0.005 per court decision returned. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/dutch-case-law))
- [Federal Register & eCFR API: CFR text as of a date, changes](https://boscolabs.dev/us-federal-rules.html): Federal Register documents and Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) text: a CFR section as in force today or on any date, its amendment history and the rules that changed it; what changed in a CFR part since a date; Federal Register search by agency or number. Official data, a source link per row. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per section, $0.002 per document; HTTP API $0.001 per unit: a CFR section with text = 5 units ($0.005), a Federal Register document = 2 ($0.002); rows without text are free. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/us-federal-rules))
- [Product Recall Check API: CPSC, NHTSA, FDA & EU Safety Gate](https://boscolabs.dev/product-recalls.html): Recalled yes/no, with each recall's date, hazard, remedy and official link, for a product name, brand, model, UPC/EAN or VIN. Checks US CPSC, NHTSA vehicle recalls, FDA enforcement reports (food, drugs, devices) and EU Safety Gate in one call. Lists every source checked. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per product checked; HTTP API $0.005 per product checked (every source answered). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/product-recalls))
- [HS Tariff Code & Duty Lookup API: US HTS and UK Tariff](https://boscolabs.dev/tariff-lookup.html): Import duty for an HS-based tariff code, US Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) or UK commodity code: description hierarchy, general (MFN), special (preferential) and column 2 rates, US Chapter 99 references, UK VAT, source link. Or a product description in, 5 candidate codes out. No binding ruling. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per lookup or search; HTTP API $0.005 per code lookup or code search (US or UK). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/tariff-lookup))

## Government & procurement

- [EU Tenders API (TED): public procurement & contract awards](https://boscolabs.dev/eu-tenders.html): EU public procurement notices from TED (Tenders Electronic Daily), the EU's official tenders journal: open calls with deadlines, contract awards with winners and values, prior information; EU, EEA and more, since 2016; filter by keyword, country, CPV code, notice type, date, EUR value. Price: Apify Store $0.002 per notice; HTTP API $0.002 per TED notice. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/eu-tenders))
- [Pentagon / DoD Contract Awards API: winners, amounts, tickers](https://boscolabs.dev/dod-contract-awards.html): US Department of Defense contract awards of $7.5M or more the same evening they are announced, plus USAspending.gov history since FY2008 (any federal agency); winner, amount, service, NAICS/PSC, matched to a US stock ticker with SEC shares outstanding. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per award row; HTTP API $0.005 per award row (USAspending history). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/dod-contract-awards))
- [US Federal Awards API: contracts & grants, all agencies](https://boscolabs.dev/us-federal-awards.html): US federal contract, grant and loan awards from every agency (USAspending.gov): winner, UEI, parent company, stock ticker, agency, amounts, dates, NAICS/PSC/assistance listing, place of performance and a source link. Filter by company, ticker, agency, keyword, state, date. Price: Apify Store $0.004 per award row; HTTP API $0.004 per award row. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/us-federal-awards))

## Macro, health & places

- [ECB Rates & Euro Inflation API: policy rates, FX, €STR, HICP](https://boscolabs.dev/eu-rates-inflation.html): Latest value, previous value, change and recent history of ECB policy rates, euro reference FX rates, €STR, euro-area and national bond yields, and Eurostat HICP inflation. Ask by plain name (ecb_deposit_rate, eur_fx:USD, hicp:NL), no SDMX keys. Official data, a source link per series. Price: Apify Store $0.002 per series returned; HTTP API $0.002 per series returned (catalogue free). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/eu-rates-inflation))
- [ClinicalTrials.gov API: trial search & NCT dossier](https://boscolabs.dev/clinical-trials.html): Clinical trials as compact JSON rows: status, phase, sponsor, conditions, interventions, enrollment, start and primary completion dates, countries, outcomes and results. Look up NCT numbers or search by condition, drug, sponsor, phase, status, country and dates. Sourced, no contact data. Price: Apify Store $0.004 per trial; HTTP API $0.004 per trial. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/clinical-trials))
- [Drug Safety API: FDA adverse events, label, recalls, EMA status](https://boscolabs.dev/drug-safety.html): Drug safety dossier for one drug name as one sourced JSON row: FDA adverse events (top FAERS reaction counts), boxed warning, indications, US recalls and shortages (openFDA), EU authorisation, EPAR and EU shortages (EMA). Dossier (default) $0.02 = 5 queries; one section $0.004. Not medical advice. Price: Apify Store $0.02 per dossier or $0.004 per single-section query; HTTP API $0.004 per sub-query; a full dossier = 5 units ($0.02); partial answers are free. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/drug-safety))
- [Dutch Address Lookup API: BAG postcode, geocode & building data](https://boscolabs.dev/dutch-address-lookup.html): Validates and geocodes Dutch addresses against the official BAG register (via PDOK): postcode, BAG ids, WGS84 + RD coordinates, construction year, use, floor area and building status. Free text, postcode + house number (or range) or BAG ids; up to 100 per run. Unmatched inputs are free. Price: Apify Store $0.002 per resolved address; HTTP API $0.002 per address resolved (unresolved inputs are free). ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/dutch-address-lookup))
- [Weather Forecast API: hourly + daily by city or lat/lon](https://boscolabs.dev/weather-forecast.html): Weather forecast for up to 50 places or coordinates, up to 10 days: hourly temperature, rain, wind, gusts, clouds and humidity plus a daily summary in local time. Source MET Norway (CC BY 4.0), cached per its terms. Unknown places are free. Price: Apify Store $0.0015 per location forecast. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/weather-forecast))

## Software security

- [Package Vulnerability Check API: CVEs, CISA KEV, safe upgrade](https://boscolabs.dev/package-vulns.html): Known vulnerabilities in a package version (npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist) or one CVE/GHSA id: severity, CVSS, fixed versions, CISA KEV exploited status and the lowest safe upgrade; for a CVE also the affected packages. From OSV.dev and CISA, a source link per advisory. Price: Apify Store $0.005 per answer; HTTP API $0.005 per package version or CVE answered. ([Apify Store](https://apify.com/bosco_labs/package-vulns))

## Blog

- [All posts](https://boscolabs.dev/blog/index.html), Atom feed: https://boscolabs.dev/blog/feed.xml
- [How to check if a company is sanctioned, with an API](https://boscolabs.dev/blog/check-if-company-is-sanctioned-api.html) (2026-11-09): Screen a company name against the OFAC, UK, EU and UN sanctions lists from code, read a match properly, and know what a name check can't catch.
- [Check UK company insolvency with the Companies House API](https://boscolabs.dev/blog/companies-house-api-insolvency-check.html) (2026-11-09): Which Companies House API fields show liquidation or administration, why has_insolvency_history is deprecated, and what the register misses. With Python.
- [We lost our own benchmark: web search vs. one API call](https://boscolabs.dev/blog/counterparty-check-benchmark.html) (2026-11-09): Web search vs. one counterparty-check API call on 25 companies: we lost the first run, found four bugs and reran it. Scores, cost, time and limits.
- [A KYB MCP server for AI agents: setup and limits](https://boscolabs.dev/blog/kyb-mcp-server-ai-agents.html) (2026-11-09): Connect a remote MCP server that checks register status, insolvency and sanctions in one tool call, and teach your agent what 'unverified' means.
- [Validate EU VAT numbers with the VIES API in Python](https://boscolabs.dev/blog/vies-vat-check-api-python.html) (2026-11-09): The official VIES REST endpoint, a small Python function around it, the errors you'll hit, and what a valid VAT number does and doesn't prove.

## How to call

- Apify API (synchronous): POST `https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/bosco_labs~<actor>/run-sync-get-dataset-items` with header `Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>` and the Actor input as the JSON body; the response is the dataset items.
- Apify hosted MCP server: add `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/<actor>` to your MCP client (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ...). It loads the Actor as a tool plus `get-actor-run` and `get-dataset-items`, and signs you in with OAuth or `Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>`. On the default server (`https://mcp.apify.com`) agents can also find the Actors with `search-actors` and run them with `call-actor`.
- Pricing: pay per event, billed to your own Apify account: you pay for rows delivered at the prices listed per Actor, and runs stop at your max charge limit.
- Bosco Labs HTTP API: `POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/<tool>` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` for every tool listed with an API price (same input and rows as the Actors), prepaid credits, $5 free trial, or no key and pay per call in USDC via x402; remote MCP at `https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp`. Keys, prices and limits: https://boscolabs.dev/api.html
- Contact: support@boscolabs.dev (questions, data issues, custom data requests).
- Bosco Labs MCP server: `bosco-labs-data-mcp` on PyPI (https://pypi.org/project/bosco-labs-data-mcp/) and the official MCP Registry (`io.github.Bosco-Labs/bosco-labs-data`): one MCP server for 7 of the data Actors (company-accounts, dod-contract-awards, esef-annual-reports, eu-tenders, sec-filings-feed, sec-insider-trades, us-house-trades) plus free LEI and SEC company lookups. Run it with `uvx bosco-labs-data-mcp` and set `APIFY_TOKEN`; source in https://github.com/Bosco-Labs/bosco-labs-data/tree/main/mcp.

## API (beta)

- Base URL: https://api.boscolabs.dev; `POST /v1/<tool>` with header `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (or `X-API-Key`) and the Actor's input object as JSON body; the response holds the Actor's rows plus `charged_usd` and `balance_usd`.
- OpenAPI: https://api.boscolabs.dev/openapi.json; interactive docs: https://api.boscolabs.dev/docs; catalogue with prices and input schemas: https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/tools (free)
- Not sure which tool? `POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/plan` with `{"question": "..."}` (free, no key) returns the exact calls with their input and maximum price; `GET https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/tools/<tool>` describes one tool (free); `POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/run` with the plan_id and a required `max_usd` runs the plan on your key (each step charged like a direct call). On MCP: plan_official_records_query, describe_official_records_tool, run_official_records_plan.
- Remote MCP (streamable HTTP, same key header): https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp lists counterparty_check, plan_official_records_query and run_official_records_plan (runs any tool by name); every tool as its own MCP tool: https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp?tools=all
- In Claude (custom connector with sign-in, links your key by OAuth): https://api.boscolabs.dev/mcp/claude
- [Get a key, prices and limits](https://boscolabs.dev/api.html): prepaid credits, packs $10 = 100,000 credits, $50 = 550,000 credits (+10% bonus), $200 = 2,400,000 credits (+20% bonus); optional automatic top-up (`"auto_topup": true` at checkout); one-time $5.00 free trial per verified e-mail; prices include VAT
- x402, no account (https://boscolabs.dev/api.html#x402): call `POST /v1/<tool>` without a key to get `402 Payment Required` (x402 v2) and pay per call in USDC on Base mainnet (eip155:8453); schemes `upto` (settles only what was delivered: rows x price, min $0.005) and `exact` (settles the quote: bound it with maxResults; keyless calls default to 10 rows) are offered; with `upto` a wallet needs only USDC on Base (gasless permit, no ETH). Nothing is settled on an error or empty result (`404 no_results`). Prices = https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/tools. Example agent: https://github.com/Bosco-Labs/bosco-labs-data/tree/main/examples/x402-agent
- x402 payment details: payTo 0x7bcb52707d5C4f334ad0D2548f96a0419fa6203F (USDC on Base); facilitator: Coinbase CDP. The `facilitatorAddress` in a 402 rotates within CDP's own set of addresses, so it can differ from a Bazaar listing; every address CDP hands out is valid.
- [Account](https://boscolabs.dev/account.html): a key's balance, today's spend against its daily cap and its last 20 ledger rows (`GET /v1/me`, `GET /v1/me/usage`), credit top-ups, and a new key for a lost one (same e-mail: a link that issues a new key and revokes the old one; balance kept)
- [Privacy](https://boscolabs.dev/privacy.html): request bodies (names screened, queries) are never logged or stored
- [Terms](https://boscolabs.dev/terms.html): prepaid credits, 14-day refunds, data is information with a source link, not advice
- [Trust](https://boscolabs.dev/security.html): read-only tools, sources and licences, sanctions screening limits, untrusted text in results
- [Status](https://boscolabs.dev/status.html): daily check of every tool against its source and the version date of every sanctions list (JSON: https://s1uqkufag2x3nhpu.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/status/status.json)
- [Benchmark](https://boscolabs.dev/benchmark.html): counterparty-check against a model with web search on 25 companies (status, sanctions, insolvency), with limits
- `counterparty-check`: $0.05 per company checked; an ambiguous name (candidates) is free (max 10 companies (companies)).
- `company-check`: $0.03 per company report (max 1 report).
- `vat-iban-check`: $0.002 per definite check (VAT number answered by VIES, or a valid IBAN); malformed, failed and unverified are free (max 10 VAT numbers and 50 IBANs). VAT answers: EU VIES (European Commission); IBAN layouts: SWIFT IBAN Registry.
- `sec-company-financials`: $0.005 per company-period row (max 10 tickers/CIKs x 20 years).
- `sec-company-screen`: $0.002 per company returned (max 200 companies (maxResults)).
- `sec-filings-feed`: $0.001 per filing (max 200 filings (maxResults)).
- `sanctions-screening`: $0.01 per name or wallet address screened (an address no list could be checked against is free) (max 50 names and 50 addresses). This product uses the International Trade Administration's Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the International Trade Administration. OFAC and CSL data are US government works. UK Sanctions List: contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. EU list: European Commission, names as published. No endorsement by any publisher is implied.
- `eu-law-lookup`: $0.005 per act or article returned (max 50 results (maxResults)). Consolidated texts from EUR-Lex (© European Union) are a documentation tool with no legal effect; only the acts published in the Official Journal of the European Union are authentic.
- `national-law-lookup`: $0.005 per article or act returned (max 5 articles). UK: contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (© Crown and database right, legislation.gov.uk).
- `eu-rates-inflation`: $0.002 per series returned (catalogue free) (max 20 series). Source: ECB statistics (data.ecb.europa.eu). The data are free of charge from the ECB; we charge for processing and delivery, not for the data. Eurostat HICP: © European Union, free of charge from Eurostat. The change field is computed by Bosco Labs.
- `us-federal-rules`: $0.001 per unit: a CFR section with text = 5 units ($0.005), a Federal Register document = 2 ($0.002); rows without text are free (max 10 CFR units or 50 documents).
- `drug-safety`: $0.004 per sub-query; a full dossier = 5 units ($0.02); partial answers are free (max 1 drug).
- `product-recalls`: $0.005 per product checked (every source answered) (max 20 products).
- `package-vulns`: $0.005 per package version or CVE answered (max 1 check).
- `identifier-resolver`: $0.002 per identifier resolved (max 1 identifier).
- `clinical-trials`: $0.004 per trial (max 100 trials (maxResults) or 100 NCT numbers).
- `company-hiring-signals`: $0.001 per unit: a company summary = 5 units ($0.005), a job row = 1 ($0.001); companies without a public job board are free (max 5 companies x 200 jobs).
- `dutch-address-lookup`: $0.002 per address resolved (unresolved inputs are free) (max 50 addresses/BAG ids or 1 postcode (100 addresses)). BAG data (Kadaster, via PDOK): Public Domain Mark 1.0. No endorsement by Kadaster or PDOK implied.
- `dutch-case-law`: $0.005 per court decision returned (max 25 ECLIs + 25 search results (maxResults)). Rechtspraak Open Data; no copyright on court decisions (art. 11 Auteurswet). The published decision on rechtspraak.nl is the reference text; not legal advice.
- `uk-new-companies`: $0.002 per company returned (max 200 companies (maxResults)). UK: contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (Companies House).
- `eu-tenders`: $0.002 per TED notice (max 200 notices (maxResults)).
- `us-federal-awards`: $0.004 per award row (max 100 awards (maxResults)).
- `dod-contract-awards`: $0.005 per award row (USAspending history) (max 100 awards (maxResults)).
- `us-house-trades`: $0.0018 per PTR transaction (max 200 trades (maxResults)).
- `sec-insider-trades`: $0.0002 per unit: a Form 4 transaction = 9 units ($0.0018), a cluster signal = 100 ($0.02) (max 5 tickers/CIKs x 183 days, 200 rows (maxResults)).
- `company-accounts`: $0.04 per company-year (max 5 companies, 10 years per country (maxResults)).
- `esef-annual-reports`: $0.05 per annual report (max 10 reports (maxFilings)).
- `sec-ownership`: $0.0018 per holding, holder or filing row (one fund or company per call) (max 200 rows (maxResults)).
- `tariff-lookup`: $0.005 per code lookup or code search (US or UK) (max 1 code or 5 candidates).

## SEC Insider Trading API (Form 4): stock transactions since 2006

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/sec-insider-trades.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-insider-trades
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/sec-insider-trades
Price: Apify Store $0.0018 per transaction row and $0.02 per cluster signal; HTTP API $0.0002 per unit: a Form 4 transaction = 9 units ($0.0018), a cluster signal = 100 ($0.02)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/sec-insider-trades, $0.0002 per unit: a Form 4 transaction = 9 units ($0.0018), a cluster signal = 100 ($0.02) (max 5 tickers/CIKs x 183 days, 200 rows (maxResults))

Insider trading data from SEC Form 4: every insider stock transaction (buy or sell) by directors, officers and 10% owners, from official EDGAR filings, 2006 to today. Filter by ticker, CIK, transaction code, role, value and date; adds cluster-buy and cluster-sell signals.

Coverage: Today's filings from the EDGAR live feed, minutes after the SEC accepts them; recent quarters from the EDGAR indexes and Form 4 XML; history from 2006 from the SEC's quarterly Insider Transactions Data Sets. Non-derivative table only: options and other derivatives are not included.

Example questions:

- Did any Tesla insiders buy shares in the last 90 days?
- Show insider cluster buys across the US market this month.
- List Nvidia insider sales over $1 million filed in 2024, with links to the Form 4s.

### Input fields

- `lookbackDays` (integer): Used only when `dateFrom` is empty: read filings from this many days back until today, e.g. 30. Empty = 90 days when `tickers` or `ciks` are set, 7 days for the whole market. Handy for schedules.
- `dateFrom` (string): Earliest filing date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2024-01-01". Data starts 2006-01-01. Empty = `lookbackDays` days before today (90 for tickers/CIKs, 7 for the whole market).
- `dateTo` (string): Latest filing date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2024-12-31". Empty = today, including today's filings from the live EDGAR feed.
- `clusterBuysOnly` (boolean): true = only open-market purchases that are part of a cluster: at least 2 different directors or officers of the same company buying, filed within `clusterWindowDays`, together worth at least $100,000. Default false. Also reads the window before the date range.
- `clusterSellsOnly` (boolean): true = only open-market sales that are part of a cluster (same rule as cluster buys, for sales). Pre-planned 10b5-1 plan sales are left out (filings flag them since April 2023). Default false. Can be combined with `clusterBuysOnly`.
- `includeClusterSignals` (boolean): true (default) = also output one row per cluster signal (record_type = "cluster"): the day a company's insider buying or selling first met the cluster rule, with the insiders and total value. Charged as a separate, higher-priced event. false = transaction rows only.
- `clusterWindowDays` (integer): How many days of filings count as one cluster of insider buying or selling, e.g. 14. Default 30.
- `transactionCodes` (array): Form 4 transaction codes to return, e.g. ["P"] for open-market purchases only. Default ["P", "S"] (open-market purchases and sales). Pass [] for all codes, including awards (A), tax withholding (F) and option exercises (M).
- `insiderRoles` (array): Only insiders with one of these roles: director, officer, ten_percent_owner, other, e.g. ["director", "officer"]. Empty = all roles.
- `minValueUsd` (integer): Minimum transaction value in USD (shares x price), e.g. 100000. Default 0 = no minimum. Transactions without a price count as 0.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum transaction rows, newest first, e.g. 500. Default 100, up to 200,000 per run (split bigger exports by date range). The run stops reading once it has this many, and returns at most this many cluster signals.
- `onlyNewSinceLastRun` (boolean): true = skip (and don't charge for) transactions and signals an earlier run with the same filters already delivered. For scheduled runs. Default false. Remembered in a named key-value store in your account. E.g. `true` for a daily scheduled run.
- `tickers` (array): Optional: issuer stock tickers, e.g. ["AAPL", "TSLA"]. Leave empty to scan the whole market (the usual use: insider buying anywhere). Mapped to the company's CIK with the SEC's ticker list; history is also matched on the ticker as written in the filing.
- `ciks` (array): Issuer SEC Central Index Keys as digits, leading zeros optional, e.g. ["320193"] for Apple. Use for delisted or renamed companies the SEC's ticker list no longer has. Empty = no CIK filter.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `record_type` (string): transaction = one Form 4 transaction; cluster = one cluster-buy or cluster-sell signal.
- `cluster_side` (string | null): Cluster rows only: buy = insiders buying together, sell = insiders selling together (10b5-1 plan sales excluded).
- `accession_number` (string): SEC accession number of the Form 4 filing.
- `form` (string): 4, or 4/A for an amendment.
- `issuer_name` (string): Company whose shares were traded, as filed.
- `issuer_cik` (string): SEC CIK of the issuer (10 digits).
- `ticker` (string | null): Trading symbol as filed, or the listed ticker of the row's share class (BRK.B for Class B shares filed as BRK.A); null if that class has none.
- `insider_name` (string): Reporting person (the first one in a joint filing).
- `insider_cik` (string | null): SEC CIK of the reporting person.
- `insider_roles` (array): director, officer, ten_percent_owner, other (combined over all joint filers).
- `officer_title` (string | null): Officer title, e.g. Chief Executive Officer.
- `owner_count` (integer): Number of reporting persons on the filing (joint filings > 1).
- `transaction_date` (string | null): Date of the transaction (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `filing_date` (string): Date the SEC received the filing (YYYY-MM-DD). For cluster rows: the day the cluster rule was first met.
- `usable_from` (string): First weekday after filing_date: the earliest day a backtest may act on this row (Form 4s can be filed until 22:00 New York time, after the close). Trade at the first market open on or after this date.
- `accepted_at` (string | null): EDGAR acceptance time with New York offset (live EDGAR rows only).
- `transaction_code` (string): Form 4 code: P purchase, S sale, A award, M option exercise, F tax withholding, G gift, ...
- `transaction_type` (string | null): Plain-English meaning of the transaction code.
- `acquired_disposed` (string | null): A = acquired, D = disposed.
- `shares` (number | null): Number of shares.
- `price` (number | null): Price per share in USD (null when the filing gives none).
- `value_usd` (number | null): shares x price.
- `shares_owned_after` (number | null): Shares owned after the transaction.
- `ownership` (string | null): direct or indirect (e.g. through a trust or fund).
- `plan_10b5_1` (boolean | null): Made under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan: true/false from the Form 4 checkbox (filings from 2023-04-01), true when a footnote says so, null when the filing predates the checkbox and no footnote mentions a plan (unknown, not 'no plan'). The box is optional for plans adopted before 2023-02-27, so false can still be such a plan.
- `security_title` (string | null): Security, e.g. Common Stock.
- `cluster_insiders` (integer | null): Transactions: distinct directors/officers buying this issuer in the cluster window up to this filing date (null for non-buys or when the window reaches before the data read). Clusters: insiders in the cluster.
- `cluster_value_usd` (number | null): Total open-market purchase value of those insiders in the window.
- `in_cluster` (boolean | null): Purchases only: part of a cluster signal.
- `cluster_date` (string | null): Purchases in a cluster: the date of that cluster signal.
- `first_filing_date` (string | null): Cluster rows: filing date of the first buy in the cluster.
- `cluster_window_days` (integer | null): Cluster rows: the window used.
- `insider_names` (array | null): Cluster rows: the buying insiders.
- `accession_numbers` (array | null): Cluster rows: the Form 4 filings in the cluster.
- `filing_url` (string): EDGAR filing index page.
- `source` (string): edgar-xml (parsed Form 4 XML), dera (SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets) or derived (cluster).
- `source_url` (string | null): The SEC page to cite: the Form 4 filing (edgar-xml rows: the filing text; dera rows: the filing index page; see `source`).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the row was produced.

### Example input

```json
{ "tickers": ["NVDA", "AAPL"], "transactionCodes": ["P", "S"], "minValueUsd": 100000,
  "dateFrom": "2025-01-01", "maxResults": 100 }
```

## SEC EDGAR Filings API: 8-K, 10-K, 10-Q feed since 1994

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/sec-filings-feed.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-filings-feed
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/sec-filings-feed
Price: Apify Store $0.001 per filing; HTTP API $0.001 per filing
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/sec-filings-feed, $0.001 per filing (max 200 filings (maxResults))

SEC EDGAR filings (8-K, 10-K, 10-Q, S-1, 13D, 13G, Form 4, any form) for any company or the whole market, latest filings live or back to 1994, from the SEC's own feeds: no scraper to maintain. Filter by ticker, CIK, form, 8-K item and date; flags earnings releases. Returns filing links, not text.

Coverage: All EDGAR forms. Companies: the SEC submissions API, complete history back to 1994. Whole market: the live feed, then the EDGAR daily and quarterly indexes back to 1993. 8-K item codes exist since August 2004. Rows hold links to the filing and its main document, not the document text.

Example questions:

- When did Nvidia release its last four quarterly results, and was it before or after the market closed?
- Which companies filed a 13D in the last 7 days, and who filed it?
- Give me links to Apple's 10-K annual reports since 2015.

### Input fields

- `formTypes` (array): EDGAR form types, exact match, e.g. ["8-K", "10-K", "10-Q"]; also S-1, 13D, 13G, 4, DEF 14A, 20-F, 6-K and any other form. Add "10-K/A" etc. for amendments. 13D and 13G also match the SC 13D and SCHEDULE 13D names. Empty = every form.
- `tickers` (array): Company tickers, e.g. ["AAPL", "MSFT"]. Mapped to the CIK with the SEC's own company_tickers.json. Empty (and `ciks` empty) = the whole market.
- `ciks` (array): SEC Central Index Keys as digits, leading zeros optional, e.g. ["320193"] for Apple. Use for delisted companies, funds and filers without a ticker. Empty = no CIK filter.
- `earningsReleasesOnly` (boolean): true = only 8-Ks with Item 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition): the dates and exact times companies released earnings. Overrides `formTypes` and `itemCodes`. Default false.
- `itemCodes` (array): Only 8-Ks reporting at least one of these items, as strings, e.g. ["5.02"] (director/officer change), "1.01" (material agreement), "2.01" (acquisition), "1.05" (cybersecurity incident). Without `formTypes`, reads 8-K and 8-K/A. Empty = no item filter.
- `dateFrom` (string): Earliest filing date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2020-01-01". EDGAR's index goes back to 1993. Empty = `lookbackDays` days before today (or, for tickers/CIKs without `lookbackDays`, the company's newest filings).
- `dateTo` (string): Latest filing date, YYYY-MM-DD. Empty = today, including filings accepted minutes ago (live EDGAR feed). E.g. "2026-03-31".
- `lookbackDays` (integer): Used only when `dateFrom` is empty: read filings from this many days back until today, e.g. 365. Empty = 7 days for the whole market; for `tickers`/`ciks`, empty = each company's newest filings (its last 1,000), so "latest 10-K of AAPL" needs no dates.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum filings, newest first, e.g. 10 for a company's latest 10 filings. Default 100. The run stops once it has this many; you pay per filing returned.
- `onlyNewSinceLastRun` (boolean): true = skip (and don't charge for) filings an earlier run with the same filters already delivered. For scheduled runs. Default false. Remembered in a named key-value store in your account. E.g. `true` for a daily scheduled run.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `accession_number` (string): SEC accession number (unique per filing).
- `form` (string): EDGAR form type as filed, e.g. 8-K, 10-K, SC 13D.
- `company_name` (string): Company the filing is about (issuer or subject; the filer otherwise).
- `cik` (string): SEC CIK of that company (10 digits).
- `ticker` (string | null): Its main ticker in the SEC's current ticker list (null if none).
- `filing_date` (string): Filing date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `accepted_at` (string | null): EDGAR acceptance time, New York time with offset.
- `market_timing` (string | null): before_open, market_hours or after_close (New York regular session), closed on weekends.
- `report_date` (string | null): Period of report (YYYY-MM-DD), e.g. the quarter end of a 10-Q or the event date of an 8-K.
- `items` (array): 8-K item codes, e.g. ["2.02", "9.01"]. Empty for other forms.
- `item_descriptions` (array): Names of those items, same order.
- `parties` (array | null): All companies and people on the filing with their role (Filer, Issuer, Subject, Filed by, Reporting). Null for company searches.
- `filing_index_url` (string): EDGAR filing index page (all documents and exhibits).
- `primary_document_url` (string | null): The main document (HTML/iXBRL, text or XML).
- `source` (string): submissions-api, full-index, daily-index or live-feed.
- `source_url` (string): The SEC page or file the row was read from.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the row was produced.

### Example input

```json
{ "tickers": ["AAPL", "MSFT", "NVDA"], "formTypes": ["8-K", "10-Q", "10-K"], "dateFrom": "2020-01-01", "maxResults": 1000 }
```

## Congress Stock Trades API: US House STOCK Act since 2014

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/us-house-trades.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/us-house-trades
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/us-house-trades
Price: Apify Store $0.0018 per trade; HTTP API $0.0018 per PTR transaction
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/us-house-trades, $0.0018 per PTR transaction (max 200 trades (maxResults))

Congress stock trades: congressional stock trading disclosures by US House members (politicians' Periodic Transaction Reports under the STOCK Act), from the House Clerk since 2014 (no Senate). Each row: ticker, amount range, owner, disclosure delay. Filter by member, ticker, type, amount, date.

Coverage: Periodic Transaction Reports of House members filed online, from January 2014 to the latest update of the Clerk's index. Scanned paper PTRs are skipped (their PDF links are listed in the run's SUMMARY record). The Senate and annual financial disclosure reports are not included.

Example questions:

- Which options did Nancy Pelosi's household trade in 2025, and how many days after the trade were they disclosed?
- Which House members disclosed NVDA trades in the last 30 days?
- List House trades over $1 million filed in 2024.

### Input fields

- `members` (array): Case-insensitive part of the member's name as listed by the Clerk, e.g. ["Pelosi"] or ["Josh Gottheimer"]. Empty = all House members.
- `tickers` (array): Only trades whose filing names one of these tickers, e.g. ["NVDA", "MSFT", "BRK.B"]. Trades without a ticker in the filing are left out when this is set. Empty = all.
- `transactionTypes` (array): Any of purchase, sale (full or partial), exchange, e.g. ["purchase"]. Default all three.
- `filedFrom` (string): Earliest filing date (when the trade became public), YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2025-01-01". Empty = 365 days ago when `members` is set, else 30 days ago; ignored when `years` is set without dates.
- `filedTo` (string): Latest filing date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2025-12-31". Empty = today.
- `years` (array): Whole filing years to load, as strings, e.g. ["2024", "2025"] (one Clerk index per year; online PTRs start in 2014). Without dates, returns those whole years. Use this or `filedFrom` for history.
- `minAmountUsd` (integer): Only trades whose reported range starts at or above this USD amount, e.g. 15001 leaves out the smallest $1,001 - $15,000 range, 1000001 keeps trades over $1 million. Empty = no minimum.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum trades, newest filings first, e.g. 500. Default 100. You pay per trade returned.
- `onlyNewSinceLastRun` (boolean): true = skip (and don't charge for) trades an earlier run with the same filters already delivered. For scheduled runs. Default false. Remembered in a named key-value store in your account. E.g. `true` for a daily scheduled run.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `transaction_id` (string): doc_id + position of the transaction in the PTR, e.g. 20035553-1. Stable across runs.
- `member_name` (string): First name, last name and suffix as listed in the Clerk's index.
- `first_name` (string): First name as listed in the Clerk's index.
- `last_name` (string): Last name as listed in the Clerk's index.
- `state_district` (string | null): State and district as listed in the index, e.g. CA11.
- `state` (string | null): Two-letter state code, the first two characters of state_district.
- `filing_date` (string): Date the PTR was filed (YYYY-MM-DD): when the trade became public.
- `transaction_date` (string): Trade date as reported (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `notification_date` (string): Date the member was notified of the trade, as reported (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `days_to_disclose` (integer): filing_date - transaction_date in days. For amendments this counts to the amendment, not the first filing.
- `owner` (string | null): Owner code as filed: SP = spouse, JT = joint, DC = dependent child, null = the member.
- `account` (string | null): Account the trade was in, as filed (Subholding Of), e.g. UBS IRA Account; null when not given.
- `ticker` (string | null): Ticker as filed in parentheses in the asset text, upper-cased; null when the filing gives none.
- `asset_description` (string): Asset text as filed (older PDFs garble upper/lower case).
- `asset_type` (string | null): From asset_type_code: ST = stock, OP = option, EF/MF = fund, GS/CS = bond, other codes = other. Filings before ~2018 have no code: option if the description says so, else null.
- `asset_type_code` (string | null): The Clerk's asset type code in square brackets, e.g. ST, OP, EF, GS (see fd.house.gov/reference/asset-type-codes.aspx).
- `option_type` (string | null): call or put, from the transaction description, for options only.
- `transaction_type` (string): P = purchase, S / S (partial) = sale, E = exchange.
- `is_partial` (boolean): True for a partial sale (S (partial)).
- `amount_min` (number | null): Lower bound of the reported value range in USD, e.g. 15001; the value itself when the filer reported an exact amount (e.g. 318.74).
- `amount_max` (number | null): Upper bound of the reported value range in USD; null for 'Over $50,000,000' and 'Spouse/DC Over $1,000,000'.
- `amount_text` (string): The value range (or exact value) as filed, e.g. $15,001 - $50,000.
- `is_amendment` (boolean): True when the transaction's filing status is Amended: the filing date is then not when the trade first became public.
- `doc_id` (string): The Clerk's document (filing) ID.
- `pdf_url` (string): The PTR PDF on disclosures-clerk.house.gov.
- `source_url` (string): Where the row was extracted from (the PTR PDF).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the PDF was fetched and parsed.

### Example input

```json
{ "members": ["Pelosi"], "years": ["2024", "2025"], "transactionTypes": ["purchase"], "maxResults": 500 }
```

## SEC 13F Holdings API: fund & ETF holdings, 13D/13G, Form 144

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/sec-ownership.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-ownership
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/sec-ownership
Price: Apify Store $0.0018 per row, plus $0.01 per "who holds this stock" search (13F or N-PORT data set); HTTP API $0.0018 per holding, holder or filing row (one fund or company per call)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/sec-ownership, $0.0018 per holding, holder or filing row (one fund or company per call) (max 200 rows (maxResults))

13F institutional holdings and who owns a stock, from official SEC filings: a fund manager's 13F positions (new, increased, decreased or closed vs last quarter), mutual fund/ETF N-PORT holdings, funds holding a ticker, 5%+ stakes (13D/13G) and Form 144 planned insider sales. One ticker or fund in.

Example questions:

- What did Berkshire Hathaway buy and sell last quarter?
- Which funds hold the most Nvidia stock?
- What are ARKK's top holdings and what did it add last quarter?
- Which ETFs and mutual funds hold Palantir?
- Has anyone filed an activist 13D on Peraso?
- Which insiders filed to sell more than $1 million of stock this week?

### Input fields

- `mode` (string): holdings13f = Form 13F: pass `filer` for a fund manager's holdings (with changes vs the previous quarter), or `ticker`/`cusip` for the managers holding a stock. holdingsNport = Form N-PORT: pass `fund` (a mutual fund or ETF ticker) for its holdings (with changes vs its previous report), or `ticker`/`cusip` for the mutual funds and ETFs holding a stock. stakes13dg = Schedule 13D/13G filings about `ticker`, or new 13D filings market-wide. planned144 = Form 144 notices of planned insider sales for `ticker`, or market-wide. Default holdings13f.
- `filer` (string): holdings13f only: the fund manager's name or SEC CIK, e.g. "Berkshire Hathaway" or "1067983". A name is matched with EDGAR's company search (the first match that files 13F reports); a CIK is exact. Empty = look up the holders of `ticker`/`cusip` instead.
- `fund` (string): holdingsNport only: the fund's ticker (any share class), e.g. "VOO" or "ARKK"; its SEC series ID, e.g. "S000002839"; or its name, e.g. "Vanguard 500 Index Fund" (matched with the SEC's series and class list; the fund picked and up to 3 close alternatives are named in the status message). Letters, digits, spaces and . , & ' ( ) / + -, up to 100 characters. Empty = look up the funds holding `ticker`/`cusip` instead.
- `ticker` (string): The company the shares are in, as a current US ticker, e.g. "AAPL". holdings13f/holdingsNport: the managers or funds holding it (or, with `filer`/`fund`, only that position). stakes13dg / planned144: filings about it. Empty = whole market (stakes13dg, planned144).
- `issuerCik` (string): Instead of `ticker`: the company's SEC CIK as digits, e.g. "320193" for Apple. Use for delisted or renamed companies. Empty = use `ticker`.
- `cusip` (string): holdings13f/holdingsNport only: the 9-character CUSIP of one share class, e.g. "037833100" (Apple common stock). Most precise way to ask which managers or funds hold a security. Empty = CUSIPs found in the company's recent Schedule 13D/13G filings (all its share classes).
- `quarter` (string): holdings13f/holdingsNport only: the quarter of the holdings, as "2026Q2" or the quarter end "2026-06-30". Empty = the newest: the filer's or fund's latest report, or for holders of a stock the newest SEC data set (13F reports are due 45 days after quarter end; N-PORT reports are public 60 days after a fund's fiscal quarter end, so a fund's report can fall in any month of the quarter).
- `stakeForms` (array): stakes13dg only: which forms, e.g. ["13D"] for new activist stakes only. Empty = all four for a ticker; 13D and 13D/A for the whole market (activist alerts).
- `minValueUsd` (integer): Minimum value in US dollars, e.g. 1000000. planned144: the notice's aggregate market value; holdings13f/holdingsNport: the position value. Default 0 = no minimum. Not used by stakes13dg.
- `dateFrom` (string): stakes13dg / planned144: earliest filing date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-10-01". Structured 13D/13G start 2024-12-18. Empty = `lookbackDays` before today.
- `dateTo` (string): stakes13dg / planned144: latest filing date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-10-31". Empty = today, including today's filings from the EDGAR live feed.
- `lookbackDays` (integer): stakes13dg / planned144, used when `dateFrom` is empty: filings from this many days back until today, e.g. 30. Empty = 365 days for a ticker's 13D/13G, 90 for a ticker's Form 144, 7 for the whole market.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum rows (one charged event each), e.g. 200. Default 50: a fund's largest positions, a stock's largest holders, or the newest filings.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `record_type` (string): holding = a position in one 13F filer's portfolio; holder = one 13F filer holding the asked stock (SEC Form 13F data set); fund_holding = a position in one mutual fund's or ETF's portfolio (Form N-PORT); fund_holder = one fund holding the asked stock (SEC Form N-PORT data set); stake = one Schedule 13D/13G filing; form144 = one Form 144 notice.
- `form` (string): Form as filed: 13F-HR or 13F-HR/A; 13D, 13D/A, 13G or 13G/A (Schedule); 144 or 144/A.
- `filer_name` (string | null): holding/holder: the 13F manager. fund_holding/fund_holder: the fund (series) name. stake: the first reporting person on the filing.
- `filer_cik` (string | null): SEC CIK (10 digits) of the 13F manager, of the fund's registrant (trust), of the 13D/13G filer, or of the person filing the Form 144.
- `period_of_report` (string): 13F rows: the quarter end the holdings are reported for (YYYY-MM-DD). N-PORT rows: the date the fund's holdings are reported as of (a fund's fiscal quarter end, YYYY-MM-DD).
- `accession_number` (string): SEC accession number of the filing the row comes from.
- `filing_date` (string): Date the SEC received the filing (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `issuer_name` (string | null): Company whose securities are held, owned or to be sold, as written in the filing (13F names are often abbreviated).
- `issuer_cik` (string | null): stake/form144: SEC CIK (10 digits) of the issuer.
- `title_of_class` (string | null): 13F rows: class of the security as filed, e.g. COM, CL A, CAP STK CL C.
- `cusip` (string | null): 13F rows: 9-character CUSIP of the security.
- `cusips` (array): stake: the issuer CUSIP(s) on the cover page.
- `ticker` (string | null): Ticker of this security from the SEC's ticker list: the issuer by CIK or name, the share class by CUSIP or the class in title_of_class (GOOG for Alphabet class C). Null when unknown, or when the issuer has several share classes and the class can't be told (see ticker_candidates).
- `ticker_candidates` (array): When ticker is null because the issuer has several listed share classes: the issuer's tickers, main first (e.g. ["BRK-B", "BRK-A"]). Empty otherwise. Ticker filters match these too.
- `put_call` (string | null): 13F rows: PUT or CALL for option positions (value = the underlying), null for shares and bonds.
- `shares` (number | null): 13F rows: shares (or principal amount when share_type is PRN) held at quarter end, summed over the filing's lines; 0 for a closed position. stake: shares beneficially owned by the reporting person with the highest percent.
- `share_type` (string | null): 13F and N-PORT rows: SH (shares) or PRN (principal amount); N-PORT also NC (contracts) or OU (other units).
- `value_usd` (number | null): 13F rows: market value in US dollars at quarter end as reported (filings before 2023-01-03 reported $1,000s and are multiplied by 1,000).
- `portfolio_pct` (number | null): holding: value as a percentage of the filing's total reported value. fund_holding/fund_holder: value as a percentage of the fund's net assets, as filed (closed positions 0).
- `previous_period` (string | null): holding: the previous quarter end the change is measured against.
- `previous_shares` (number | null): holding: shares at the previous quarter end (0 = not held then, null = no 13F for that quarter).
- `previous_value_usd` (number | null): holding: value at the previous quarter end, in US dollars.
- `shares_change` (number | null): holding: shares minus previous_shares.
- `shares_change_pct` (number | null): holding: shares_change as a percentage of previous_shares (null when not held before).
- `change` (string | null): holding: new, increased, decreased, unchanged or closed (sold out) vs the previous quarter; null when unknown.
- `series_id` (string | null): N-PORT rows: the fund's SEC series ID, e.g. S000002839 (Vanguard 500 Index Fund).
- `registrant_name` (string | null): N-PORT rows: the registered investment company (trust) the fund belongs to, e.g. VANGUARD INDEX FUNDS.
- `fund_net_assets_usd` (number | null): N-PORT rows: the fund's net assets in US dollars at period_of_report.
- `payoff_profile` (string | null): N-PORT rows: Long, Short or N/A as filed.
- `isin` (string | null): fund_holding: the security's ISIN when the fund reported one, e.g. US0378331005.
- `issuer_lei` (string | null): fund_holding: the issuer's LEI when the fund reported one.
- `asset_category` (string | null): fund_holding: the N-PORT asset category, e.g. EC (common equity), EP (preferred), DBT (debt), STIV (short-term investment vehicle), DE/DIR/DCR (derivatives).
- `currency` (string | null): fund_holding: the currency the security is denominated in (ISO 4217); value_usd is always in US dollars.
- `country` (string | null): fund_holding: the investment's country (ISO 3166 alpha-2) as filed.
- `stake_type` (string | null): stake: activist (Schedule 13D: may seek to influence control) or passive (Schedule 13G).
- `amendment_no` (integer | null): stake: amendment number on the cover page (null for an original filing).
- `security_class` (string | null): stake/form144: class of securities as filed, e.g. Common Stock.
- `percent_of_class` (number | null): stake: percent of the class beneficially owned, the highest among the reporting persons (group members usually report the same aggregate).
- `reporting_persons` (array): stake: every reporting person on the cover pages: name, cik (null if none), percent_of_class, shares, person_type (SEC codes like IA, IN, PN, CO).
- `event_date` (string | null): stake: date of the event that required the filing (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `seller_name` (string | null): form144: the person for whose account the securities are to be sold, as filed.
- `relationships` (array): form144: relationship to the issuer as filed, e.g. Director, Officer, 10% Securityholder.
- `shares_to_be_sold` (number | null): form144: number of shares (units) to be sold, summed over the notice's lines.
- `aggregate_market_value_usd` (number | null): form144: aggregate market value of the shares to be sold, in US dollars, as filed.
- `shares_outstanding` (number | null): form144: shares of the class outstanding, as filed.
- `approx_sale_date` (string | null): form144: approximate date of sale (YYYY-MM-DD; the earliest if several).
- `exchanges` (array): form144: exchange(s) where the shares are to be sold.
- `broker_names` (array): form144: broker(s) or market maker(s) handling the sale.
- `plan_adoption_dates` (array): form144: adoption dates of the Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, if the sale is under one (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `notice_date` (string | null): form144: date of the notice (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `filing_url` (string): EDGAR index page of the filing.
- `source` (string): edgar-13f (the filing's information table), sec-13f-data-set (SEC Form 13F data set), edgar-nport (the fund's N-PORT-P XML), sec-nport-data-set (SEC Form N-PORT data set) or edgar-xml (the filing's XML).
- `source_url` (string): The exact SEC file the row was read from.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the row was produced.

### Example input

```json
{"mode": "holdings13f", "filer": "Berkshire Hathaway"}
```

## SEC Financial Statements API: income, balance sheet, cash flow

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/sec-company-financials.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-company-financials
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/sec-company-financials
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per company-period row; HTTP API $0.005 per company-period row
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/sec-company-financials, $0.005 per company-period row (max 10 tickers/CIKs x 20 years)

Company financial statements from SEC EDGAR XBRL (10-K, 10-Q, 20-F): income statement (revenue, profit, EPS), balance sheet, cash flow, free cash flow and margins per fiscal year or quarter, 2009 to date, by stock ticker or CIK. Each value cites its XBRL tag and filing. Q4 derived if not reported.

Example questions:

- How did Microsoft's revenue, net income and free cash flow develop over the last 8 quarters?
- Compare Nvidia, AMD and Intel on operating margin for the last 5 fiscal years.
- What was JPMorgan's net income in 2024, and which filing is it from?

### Input fields

- `tickers` (array): US tickers as listed by the SEC, e.g. ["AAPL", "MSFT"]; share classes with a dash or dot, e.g. "BRK-B". Foreign companies filing 20-F/40-F work too, e.g. "NVO". Mapped to the CIK with the SEC's company_tickers.json; an unknown ticker is skipped with suggestions in the status message. Empty = use `ciks`.
- `ciks` (array): SEC Central Index Keys as digits, leading zeros optional, e.g. ["320193"] for Apple. Use for delisted companies and filers without a ticker. Empty = use `tickers`; at least one of the two is required.
- `period` (string): "annual" = one row per fiscal year (FY). "quarterly" = one row per fiscal quarter, Q1-Q4, each a discrete 3-month period (Q4 and year-to-date-only cash flows are derived, see `warnings`). Companies without quarterly XBRL data (most 20-F filers) return fiscal years instead. Default "annual".
- `years` (integer): How many of the latest fiscal years to return per company, e.g. 5 (5 rows annual, up to 20 rows quarterly; 2 with quarterly = the last 8 quarters). XBRL data starts in 2009-2011. Default 5, max 20.
- `metrics` (array): Only these output fields, e.g. ["revenue", "net_income", "free_cash_flow", "operating_margin"]. Valid: revenue, cost_of_revenue, gross_profit, research_and_development, selling_general_and_administrative, operating_profit, profit_before_tax, net_income, net_income_attributable_to_parent, eps_basic, eps_diluted, weighted_average_shares_basic, weighted_average_shares_diluted, depreciation_amortisation, total_assets, current_assets, cash_and_equivalents, total_liabilities, current_liabilities, noncurrent_liabilities, long_term_debt, total_equity, equity_attributable_to_parent, shares_outstanding, operating_cash_flow, investing_cash_flow, financing_cash_flow, capex, dividends_paid, free_cash_flow, ebitda, gross_margin, operating_margin, net_margin, return_on_equity, equity_ratio, revenue_growth. Empty = all of them.
- `includeSources` (boolean): true = each row has `sources` (per value: the XBRL tag and the SEC accession number it came from, plus how it was derived) and `filings` (form, filing date and URL of each filing cited). false = values only, about 3x smaller rows. Default true.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `ticker` (string | null): Main ticker in the SEC's current ticker list (null if none).
- `cik` (string): SEC CIK, 10 digits.
- `company_name` (string): Company name as in SEC companyfacts.
- `fiscal_year` (integer): Fiscal year as the company names it (Apple's year ending September 2025 = 2025).
- `fiscal_period` (string): FY for a fiscal year, Q1-Q4 for a discrete 3-month fiscal quarter.
- `period_start` (string | null): First day of the period (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `period_end` (string): Last day of the period = balance-sheet date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `form` (string | null): Form of the main filing for this period: 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F, 40-F, 6-K or an /A amendment.
- `filed` (string | null): Filing date of that filing (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `accession_number` (string | null): SEC accession number of the filing most values come from.
- `source_url` (string | null): EDGAR index page of that filing.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `currency` (string): Reporting currency of all money values (ISO 4217, e.g. USD, EUR, DKK). Values are in full units, not thousands.
- `revenue` (number | null): Total revenue / net sales (for banks: total net revenue). In `currency`.
- `cost_of_revenue` (number | null): Cost of revenue / cost of goods and services sold. In `currency`.
- `gross_profit` (number | null): Gross profit; when not tagged, revenue - cost_of_revenue (sources says derived). In `currency`.
- `research_and_development` (number | null): Research and development expense. In `currency`.
- `selling_general_and_administrative` (number | null): Selling, general and administrative expense (null when the company reports sales/marketing and G&A separately). In `currency`.
- `operating_profit` (number | null): Operating income (loss). Null for most banks and insurers. In `currency`.
- `profit_before_tax` (number | null): Income from continuing operations before income taxes. In `currency`.
- `net_income` (number | null): Net income including noncontrolling interests (ProfitLoss), else net income attributable to the parent; as in the esef-annual-reports Actor. In `currency`.
- `net_income_attributable_to_parent` (number | null): Net income attributable to the parent's shareholders (the US 'net income' headline). In `currency`.
- `eps_basic` (number | null): Basic earnings per share, in currency per share. Never derived (null for Q4 unless reported).
- `eps_diluted` (number | null): Diluted earnings per share, in currency per share. Never derived.
- `weighted_average_shares_basic` (number | null): Weighted average shares outstanding, basic. Never derived.
- `weighted_average_shares_diluted` (number | null): Weighted average shares outstanding, diluted. Never derived.
- `depreciation_amortisation` (number | null): Depreciation, depletion and amortization (cash flow statement). In `currency`.
- `total_assets` (number | null): Total assets at period end. In `currency`.
- `current_assets` (number | null): Total current assets at period end. Null for banks and insurers (unclassified balance sheet). In `currency`.
- `cash_and_equivalents` (number | null): Cash and cash equivalents at period end (banks: cash and due from banks). In `currency`.
- `total_liabilities` (number | null): Total liabilities; when not tagged, total_assets - total_equity (sources says derived). In `currency`.
- `current_liabilities` (number | null): Total current liabilities. Null for banks and insurers. In `currency`.
- `noncurrent_liabilities` (number | null): Total non-current liabilities, when tagged. In `currency`.
- `long_term_debt` (number | null): Long-term debt, non-current portion where tagged, else total long-term debt; sources shows the tag. In `currency`.
- `total_equity` (number | null): Total equity including noncontrolling interests, else stockholders' equity. In `currency`.
- `equity_attributable_to_parent` (number | null): Stockholders' equity attributable to the parent. In `currency`.
- `shares_outstanding` (number | null): Common shares outstanding at the balance-sheet date.
- `operating_cash_flow` (number | null): Net cash from operating activities. In `currency`.
- `investing_cash_flow` (number | null): Net cash from investing activities. In `currency`.
- `financing_cash_flow` (number | null): Net cash from financing activities. In `currency`.
- `capex` (number | null): Capital expenditure: payments for property, plant and equipment, as a positive number. Null for most banks. In `currency`.
- `dividends_paid` (number | null): Dividends paid in cash, as a positive number. In `currency`.
- `free_cash_flow` (number | null): Derived: operating_cash_flow - capex.
- `ebitda` (number | null): Derived: operating_profit + depreciation_amortisation.
- `gross_margin` (number | null): Derived: gross_profit / revenue (0.25 = 25%).
- `operating_margin` (number | null): Derived: operating_profit / revenue.
- `net_margin` (number | null): Derived: net_income / revenue.
- `return_on_equity` (number | null): Derived: net_income / total_equity, fiscal-year rows only.
- `equity_ratio` (number | null): Derived: total_equity / total_assets.
- `revenue_growth` (number | null): Derived: revenue / revenue of the same fiscal period one year earlier - 1 (year over year, also for quarters).
- `metrics_found` (integer): How many of the reported metrics (not the derived ones) have a value.
- `sources` (object): Only with includeSources: per metric {tag: XBRL concept used, accession: filing it came from, derived: how a quarter value was computed (e.g. 'fiscal year - 9-month YTD') or the formula for gross_profit/total_liabilities fallbacks}.
- `filings` (object): Only with includeSources: per accession number cited in sources, its form, filing date and EDGAR URL.
- `warnings` (array): Notes on this row: quarter values derived from year-to-date figures, restated values (latest filing used), quarterly data missing.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the row was produced.

### Example input

```json
{ "tickers": ["AAPL", "MSFT"], "period": "quarterly", "years": 2, "metrics": ["revenue", "net_income", "free_cash_flow"] }
```

## SEC Company Screener API: filter all US filers by financials

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/sec-company-screen.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sec-company-screen
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/sec-company-screen
Price: Apify Store $0.002 per company returned; HTTP API $0.002 per company returned
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/sec-company-screen, $0.002 per company returned (max 200 companies (maxResults))

Stock screener on SEC EDGAR data. US companies matching your filters for one calendar year or quarter: revenue, net income, margins, cash flow, assets and 30 more metrics from SEC XBRL frames, sorted and capped. Each value cites its XBRL tag and SEC filing. Same metrics as SEC Company Financials.

Example questions:

- Which US companies had revenue over $10B and net margin above 20% in fiscal 2025?
- Top 20 US companies by operating cash flow in 2025.
- Which companies with a ticker had an operating margin above 30% in Q3 2025?

### Input fields

- `period` (string, required): Calendar period in SEC frames format: "CY2025" = annual figures, "CY2025Q3" = 3-month quarter figures. Required, 2009 to the current year. Calendar-aligned: each company comes with its own fiscal period that best fits it (e.g. CY2025 holds Apple's fiscal year to Sep 2025, Microsoft's to Jun 2025, Walmart's to Jan 2026), shown in period_start/period_end. Balance-sheet metrics are taken at each company's period end.
- `filters` (array): Conditions every company must meet, as a list of {metric, min, max} (either bound optional, both inclusive), e.g. [{"metric": "revenue", "min": 10000000000}, {"metric": "net_margin", "min": 0.2}] = revenue of at least $10B and net margin of at least 20%. Money in full USD (10000000000 = $10B), ratios as fractions (0.2 = 20%), EPS in USD per share. A company without a value for a filter metric is left out. Metrics: see sortBy. Empty = no filter (all companies with a sortBy value).
- `sortBy` (string): Metric to rank by, e.g. "operating_cash_flow". Same names as the SEC Company Financials Actor; the last seven (free_cash_flow to equity_ratio) are derived from two reported metrics. Companies without a value for it are left out. Empty = the first filter's metric, else revenue.
- `sortOrder` (string): "desc" = largest first (top N), "asc" = smallest first (e.g. the lowest net margin). Default "desc".
- `maxResults` (integer): Most companies to return (and charge for), e.g. 20 for a top 20. The status message says how many matched in total. Default 50, max 1000.
- `metrics` (array): More fields to show per company besides the sortBy and filter metrics, e.g. ["operating_cash_flow", "total_assets"]. Same names as sortBy. Each adds a few SEC requests. Empty = only the sortBy and filter metrics (plus the inputs of derived ones).
- `tickersOnly` (boolean): true = skip companies without a ticker in the SEC's company_tickers.json (delisted companies, private issuers of public debt, subsidiaries). Default false. E.g. `true`.
- `includeSources` (boolean): true = each row has `sources`: per value the XBRL tag, the SEC accession number and the filing URL (or the formula for derived values). false = values only, about 3x smaller rows. Default true.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `ticker` (string | null): Main ticker in the SEC's current ticker list (null if the company has none, e.g. delisted or private debt issuers).
- `cik` (string): SEC CIK, 10 digits.
- `company_name` (string | null): Company name as in the SEC frame.
- `period` (string): The calendar period screened, e.g. CY2025 or CY2025Q3. SEC frames are calendar-aligned: each company appears with its own fiscal period that best fits this calendar period (Apple's year to 27 Sep 2025, Microsoft's to 30 Jun 2025 and Walmart's to 31 Jan 2026 are all in CY2025). See period_start/period_end.
- `period_start` (string | null): First day of the company's own fiscal period that SEC assigned to this calendar period (YYYY-MM-DD); null when the company reported no duration value (income, cash flow or EPS) for it.
- `period_end` (string | null): Last day of that fiscal period (YYYY-MM-DD); balance-sheet values are as of this date (when period_start is null: the balance-sheet date nearest the calendar period's end).
- `currency` (string): Always USD: frames are screened in USD (companies reporting in other currencies are not included). Values are in full dollars, not thousands.
- `revenue` (number | null): Total revenue / net sales (for banks: total net revenue). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `cost_of_revenue` (number | null): Cost of revenue / cost of goods and services sold. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `gross_profit` (number | null): Gross profit; when not tagged, revenue - cost_of_revenue (sources says derived). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `research_and_development` (number | null): Research and development expense. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `selling_general_and_administrative` (number | null): Selling, general and administrative expense (null when the company reports sales/marketing and G&A separately). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `operating_profit` (number | null): Operating income (loss). Null for most banks and insurers. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `profit_before_tax` (number | null): Income from continuing operations before income taxes. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `net_income` (number | null): Net income including noncontrolling interests (ProfitLoss), else net income attributable to the parent; as in the esef-annual-reports Actor. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `net_income_attributable_to_parent` (number | null): Net income attributable to the parent's shareholders (the US 'net income' headline). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `eps_basic` (number | null): Basic earnings per share, in USD per share. Never derived (null for Q4 unless reported). Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `eps_diluted` (number | null): Diluted earnings per share, in USD per share. Never derived. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `weighted_average_shares_basic` (number | null): Weighted average shares outstanding, basic. Never derived. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `weighted_average_shares_diluted` (number | null): Weighted average shares outstanding, diluted. Never derived. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `depreciation_amortisation` (number | null): Depreciation, depletion and amortization (cash flow statement). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `total_assets` (number | null): Total assets at period end. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `current_assets` (number | null): Total current assets at period end. Null for banks and insurers (unclassified balance sheet). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `cash_and_equivalents` (number | null): Cash and cash equivalents at period end (banks: cash and due from banks). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `total_liabilities` (number | null): Total liabilities; when not tagged, total_assets - total_equity (sources says derived). In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
