- `current_liabilities` (number | null): Total current liabilities. Null for banks and insurers. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `noncurrent_liabilities` (number | null): Total non-current liabilities, when tagged. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `long_term_debt` (number | null): Long-term debt, non-current portion where tagged, else total long-term debt; sources shows the tag. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `total_equity` (number | null): Total equity including noncontrolling interests, else stockholders' equity. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `equity_attributable_to_parent` (number | null): Stockholders' equity attributable to the parent. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `shares_outstanding` (number | null): Common shares outstanding at the balance-sheet date. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `operating_cash_flow` (number | null): Net cash from operating activities. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `investing_cash_flow` (number | null): Net cash from investing activities. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `financing_cash_flow` (number | null): Net cash from financing activities. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `capex` (number | null): Capital expenditure: payments for property, plant and equipment, as a positive number. Null for most banks. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `dividends_paid` (number | null): Dividends paid in cash, as a positive number. In USD. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `free_cash_flow` (number | null): Derived: operating_cash_flow - capex. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `ebitda` (number | null): Derived: operating_profit + depreciation_amortisation. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `gross_margin` (number | null): Derived: gross_profit / revenue (0.25 = 25%). Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `operating_margin` (number | null): Derived: operating_profit / revenue (0.25 = 25%). Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `net_margin` (number | null): Derived: net_income / revenue (0.25 = 25%). Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `return_on_equity` (number | null): Derived: net_income / total_equity (0.25 = 25%). Calendar-year periods only. Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `equity_ratio` (number | null): Derived: total_equity / total_assets (0.25 = 25%). Only present when asked (sortBy, filters, metrics) or needed for a derived field.
- `source_url` (string): EDGAR index page of the filing most of the row's values come from.
- `sources` (object): Only with includeSources: per metric {tag: XBRL concept used, accession: SEC filing the value comes from (the latest filing that reported it, or for re-checked values the first 10-K/10-Q that did), url: its EDGAR index page}, or {derived: formula} for derived values.
- `warnings` (array): Notes on this row: a value from a proxy statement replaced by the 10-K/10-Q figure, a value that could not be checked, or a metric left out because it was reported for a different period than the row's.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the row was produced.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.

### Example input

```json
{
  "period": "CY2025",
  "filters": [
    { "metric": "revenue", "min": 10000000000 },
    { "metric": "net_margin", "min": 0.2 }
  ],
  "sortBy": "revenue",
  "maxResults": 50
}
```

## EU Annual Reports API (ESEF): XBRL financial statements

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/esef-annual-reports.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/esef-annual-reports
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/esef-annual-reports
Price: Apify Store $0.01 per run plus $0.05 per annual report; raw XBRL fact rows, if switched on, $0.0005 each; HTTP API $0.05 per annual report
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/esef-annual-reports, $0.05 per annual report (max 10 reports (maxFilings))

Key financials (revenue, operating income/EBIT, net income, EPS, assets, equity, cash flows, margins, growth) from the ESEF annual reports of European listed companies in 28 countries, via filings.xbrl.org. Each value links to its XBRL fact. Filter by LEI, company name, country, fiscal year.

Coverage: ESEF annual reports collected by filings.xbrl.org: 27,626 reports from 28 countries (counted 2026-11-05; largest: UA, GB, DK, SE, NO, FR, FI). Germany is not in the index. Reports appear a few days to a few weeks after publication, once filings.xbrl.org has processed them. All values are in full currency units.

Example questions:

- Get Heineken's latest revenue growth and operating margin from its annual report.
- Compare net income and equity of Belgian listed companies for fiscal years ending in 2024.
- Which XBRL fact does ASML's reported revenue come from?

### Input fields

- `leis` (array): Legal Entity Identifiers (20 letters/digits), e.g. ["724500Y6DUVHQD6OXN27"] for ASML: the most precise lookup, any country. Empty = no LEI filter.
- `companyName` (string): Case-insensitive part of the registered company name, e.g. "heineken" or "lvmh"; can match several companies, so check `company_name` in the output. Empty = no name filter.
- `countries` (array): Filing countries as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes, e.g. ["NL", "BE", "FR"]; also SE, DK, FI, NO, IT, ES, GB and others. Empty = all 28 countries in the index (Germany is not in it).
- `periodFrom` (string): Fiscal year ending on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2024-01-01". Empty = no lower limit.
- `periodTo` (string): Fiscal year ending on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2024-12-31". Empty = no upper limit.
- `maxFilings` (integer): Maximum annual reports, newest fiscal period first, e.g. 1 for a company's latest report. Default 10. One report per company per fiscal year, with the prior year nested in each row.
- `includeRawFacts` (boolean): true = also output every tagged XBRL fact of each report as its own row (record_type = "fact"), charged per fact row. Default false (one summary row per report).
- `onlyNewSinceLastRun` (boolean): true = skip (and don't charge for) reports an earlier run with the same filters already delivered. For scheduled runs. Default false. Remembered in a named key-value store in your account. E.g. `true` for a daily scheduled run.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `record_type` (string): summary = one row per annual report; fact = one raw XBRL fact (only with includeRawFacts).
- `lei` (string | null): Legal Entity Identifier of the filer.
- `company_name` (string | null): Registered name (null when filings.xbrl.org has none).
- `country` (string): Filing country (ISO 3166 alpha-2).
- `period_end` (string): Fiscal year end (YYYY-MM-DD), taken from the report facts.
- `fiscal_year_start` (string | null): Fiscal year start (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `currency` (string | null): ISO 4217 currency of the monetary values.
- `revenue` (number | null): revenue for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:Revenue or ifrs-full:RevenueFromContractsWithCustomers
- `gross_profit` (number | null): gross_profit for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:GrossProfit
- `operating_profit` (number | null): operating_profit for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:ProfitLossFromOperatingActivities
- `profit_before_tax` (number | null): profit_before_tax for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:ProfitLossBeforeTax
- `net_income` (number | null): net_income for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:ProfitLoss
- `net_income_attributable_to_parent` (number | null): net_income_attributable_to_parent for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParent
- `eps_basic` (number | null): eps_basic for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:BasicEarningsLossPerShare
- `eps_diluted` (number | null): eps_diluted for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:DilutedEarningsLossPerShare
- `total_assets` (number | null): total_assets for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:Assets
- `current_assets` (number | null): current_assets for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:CurrentAssets
- `cash_and_equivalents` (number | null): cash_and_equivalents for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:CashAndCashEquivalents
- `total_equity` (number | null): total_equity for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:Equity
- `equity_attributable_to_parent` (number | null): equity_attributable_to_parent for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParent
- `total_liabilities` (number | null): total_liabilities for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:Liabilities
- `current_liabilities` (number | null): current_liabilities for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:CurrentLiabilities
- `noncurrent_liabilities` (number | null): noncurrent_liabilities for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:NoncurrentLiabilities
- `operating_cash_flow` (number | null): operating_cash_flow for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivities
- `investing_cash_flow` (number | null): investing_cash_flow for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInInvestingActivities
- `financing_cash_flow` (number | null): financing_cash_flow for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInFinancingActivities
- `depreciation_amortisation` (number | null): depreciation_amortisation for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:DepreciationAndAmortisationExpense or ifrs-full:AdjustmentsForDepreciationAndAmortisationExpense or ifrs-full:DepreciationAmortisationAndImpairmentLossReversalOfImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLoss or ifrs-full:AdjustmentsForDepreciationAndAmortisationExpenseAndImpairmentLossReversalOfImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLoss
- `employee_benefits_expense` (number | null): employee_benefits_expense for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:EmployeeBenefitsExpense
- `dividends_paid` (number | null): dividends_paid for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:DividendsPaidClassifiedAsFinancingActivities or ifrs-full:DividendsPaid
- `dividend_per_share` (number | null): dividend_per_share for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:DividendsRecognisedAsDistributionsToOwnersPerShare
- `dividend_proposed_per_share` (number | null): dividend_proposed_per_share for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:DividendsProposedOrDeclaredBeforeFinancialStatementsAuthorisedForIssueButNotRecognisedAsDistributionToOwnersPerShare
- `shares_outstanding` (number | null): shares_outstanding for the fiscal year; source concept: ifrs-full:NumberOfSharesOutstanding
- `metrics_found` (integer): How many of the reported metrics were found.
- `ebitda` (number | null): Derived: operating_profit + depreciation_amortisation.
- `operating_margin` (number | null): Derived: operating_profit / revenue.
- `net_margin` (number | null): Derived: net_income / revenue.
- `return_on_equity` (number | null): Derived: net_income / total_equity.
- `equity_ratio` (number | null): Derived: total_equity / total_assets.
- `revenue_growth` (number | null): Derived: revenue / prior_year.revenue - 1.
- `sources` (object): Per field: concept, fact_id, period, unit, decimals of the source fact, or {derived: formula}.
- `prior_year` (object | null): Comparative fiscal year from the same report: period_end, fiscal_year_start, currency, the same metrics and derived fields, metrics_found and sources.
- `fact_id` (string): XBRL fact id inside the report.
- `concept` (string): XBRL concept, e.g. ifrs-full:Revenue.
- `value` (string | null): Raw fact value as reported (canonical form).
- `unit` (string | null): XBRL unit, e.g. iso4217:EUR.
- `period` (string | null): XBRL period (instant or start/end).
- `decimals` (integer | null): XBRL decimals (precision).
- `dimensions` (object): Extra XBRL dimensions (axes/members) of the fact.
- `filing_id` (string): filings.xbrl.org filing id.
- `published` (string | null): Publication timestamp of the filing.
- `viewer_url` (string | null): Inline XBRL viewer of the annual report.
- `report_url` (string | null): The iXBRL (XHTML) annual report.
- `source_url` (string): xBRL-JSON the row was extracted from.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the source was fetched.

### Example input

```json
{ "countries": ["NL", "BE", "FR"], "periodFrom": "2025-01-01", "maxFilings": 50 }
```

## ISIN, LEI, CIK, FIGI & Ticker Resolver API (crosswalk)

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/identifier-resolver.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/identifier-resolver
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/identifier-resolver
Price: Apify Store $0.002 per resolved identifier; HTTP API $0.002 per identifier resolved
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/identifier-resolver, $0.002 per identifier resolved (max 1 identifier)

Issuer legal name, LEI, CIK, tickers, ISINs, FIGIs, CFI code and EU trading venues for one ISIN, LEI, CIK, ticker, FIGI or company name. Check digits validated first; a source URL per value. Data from GLEIF, OpenFIGI, SEC and ESMA FIRDS.

Example questions:

- What is the LEI, CIK and home-market FIGI of ISIN NL0010273215, and on how many EU venues does it trade? Cite the sources.

### Input fields

- `identifier` (string, required): ONE identifier of a security or company: an ISIN ("US0378331005"), an LEI ("HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394"), an SEC CIK ("320193"), a ticker ("AAPL", "BRK.B"; add exchange for non-US markets), a FIGI ("BBG000B9XRY4") or a company name ("Siemens AG"). The type is detected automatically; ISIN, LEI and FIGI check digits are verified before any lookup, and a bad one fails in seconds with the correct digit, at no charge. Required.
- `idType` (string): What the identifier is. Default "auto": digits only = CIK, 20 characters = LEI, 12 characters = ISIN or FIGI (by check digit), up to 6 characters without spaces = ticker (read as a name if no US ticker matches), anything else = company name. Set it for short names; numeric tickers just need exchange ("7203" with "JT").
- `exchange` (string): Only for a ticker outside the US: a Bloomberg exchange code ("LN" London, "GR" Germany, "NA" Amsterdam, "FP" Paris, "JT" Tokyo, "SW" Swiss) or a 4-letter MIC ("XLON", "XAMS"). Empty (default) = US tickers from the SEC's list. With an exchange, an all-digit identifier is read as a ticker ("7974" + "JT" = Nintendo), not a CIK.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query` (string): The identifier as given.
- `query_type` (string): How it was read: isin, lei, cik, ticker, figi or name.
- `exchange_filter` (string | null): The exchange given for a ticker, else null.
- `issuer_name` (string | null): Issuer legal name: GLEIF legal name, else SEC name, else OpenFIGI name.
- `issuer_name_latin` (string | null): English or transliterated GLEIF name when the legal name is not in Latin script (e.g. Japanese), else null.
- `lei` (string | null): Issuer Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), e.g. HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394.
- `lei_status` (string | null): GLEIF registration status: ISSUED, LAPSED, RETIRED, ...
- `issuer_country` (string | null): Country of the issuer's legal address (ISO 3166 alpha-2), from GLEIF.
- `issuer_jurisdiction` (string | null): Legal jurisdiction from GLEIF, e.g. US-CA or NL.
- `cik` (string | null): SEC Central Index Key (no leading zeros) if the issuer files with the SEC, else null.
- `tickers` (array): Tickers with exchange: source SEC (exchange = SEC name, e.g. Nasdaq) and source OpenFIGI (exchange = Bloomberg composite code, e.g. US, GR, LN; composite_figi set), up to 10 OpenFIGI listings.
- `isin` (string | null): The instrument ISIN: the one asked for, else the issuer's main share ISIN (equity shares on most EU venues in FIRDS).
- `issuer_isins` (array): Up to 20 ISINs GLEIF maps to the issuer's LEI (shares, bonds, other securities).
- `issuer_isin_count` (integer | null): Total ISINs GLEIF maps to the LEI (null if no LEI).
- `composite_figi` (string | null): Composite (country-level) FIGI of the instrument's home or US listing, e.g. BBG000B9XRY4.
- `share_class_figi` (string | null): Share-class FIGI (global across countries), e.g. BBG001S5N8V8.
- `security_type` (string | null): OpenFIGI security type, e.g. Common Stock, Depositary Receipt, Corp.
- `instrument_name` (string | null): Instrument name as most often reported to FIRDS, else OpenFIGI's name.
- `cfi_code` (string | null): ISO 10962 CFI code from FIRDS, e.g. ESVUFR (equity, common share).
- `currency` (string | null): Notional currency from FIRDS (ISO 4217).
- `eu_trading_venues` (array): EU/EEA trading venues (MIC and first trading date) where FIRDS lists the instrument as currently traded, by MIC, up to 100.
- `eu_venue_count` (integer | null): Number of current EU venues in FIRDS (null if FIRDS was not reached or no ISIN is known).
- `eu_venues_terminated_count` (integer | null): Venues where trading has ended, per FIRDS.
- `match_confidence` (number): 1.0 when every link is by identifier; lower when a link was made by name (0.9 exact name and jurisdiction, 0.6 ambiguous).
- `match_note` (string): How the identifiers were linked, in words.
- `alternatives` (array): Other candidate issuers (name, lei, isin, cik) when a name was matched.
- `sources` (object): Source URL per value: lei, cik, isin, issuer_isins, issuer_name, tickers, figi, instrument (FIRDS query).
- `source_url` (string | null): Main source: the GLEIF record, else SEC, FIRDS or OpenFIGI.
- `provided_by` (string): Bosco Labs (boscolabs.dev).
- `notices` (array): Licence and attribution notices (GLEIF CC0, OpenFIGI, ESMA free-of-charge notice).
- `warnings` (array): Sources that failed or were rate-limited, and ambiguous matches, in plain words.
- `retrieved_at` (string): ISO-8601 UTC time of the lookup.
- `duration_seconds` (number): Time the lookup took.

### Example input

```json
{ "identifier": "US0378331005" }
```

## Counterparty Check API: KYB checklist from official registers

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/counterparty-check.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/counterparty-check
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/counterparty-check
Price: Apify Store $0.05 per company checked; HTTP API $0.05 per company checked; an ambiguous name (candidates) is free
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/counterparty-check, $0.05 per company checked; an ambiguous name (candidates) is free (max 10 companies (companies))

KYB checklist per company: register status, LEI, insolvency, recent accounts, sanctions (OFAC, UN, UK, EU) on company and officers, VAT (VIES), IBAN; pass, fail, review or unverified, sourced. Officers: UK, PL, NO, FR only. Insolvency: UK, PL, FR, DE, NL, NO, FI, EE, IE, CZ, LV; else unverified.

Example questions:

- Before we pay them: check supplier Novo Nordisk A/S (CVR 24256790), their VAT number DK24256790 and IBAN DK5000400440116243.

### Input fields

- `query` (string): The counterparty to check: a name (e.g. "Novo Nordisk") or an identifier: LEI (20 characters, e.g. "724500Y6DUVHQD6OXN27"), UK company number ("00445790", "SC123456"), Danish CVR ("24256790"), Norwegian org number ("923609016"), French SIREN (9 digits, "552032534") or SIRET (14 digits, "55203253400703"), Finnish Business ID with its dash ("0112038-9"), Estonian registry code (8 digits, "12417834"), Irish CRO company number ("CRO 104547", or the digits with `country` IE), Czech IČO ("IČO 27074358", the company's VAT number "CZ27074358", or the digits with `country` CZ), Latvian registration number (11 digits, "40003032949"), US ticker in capitals or with $ ("AAPL", "$brk.b"; foreign companies listed in the US resolve to their home country), SEC CIK ("320193"). The type is detected from format and check digits; an 8-digit number valid in several registers (UK, Danish CVR, Estonian) is settled by asking them, and `country` decides when given. Required, unless you give a `companies` list instead.
- `country` (string): ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code to disambiguate, e.g. "DK", "GB", "NO", "FR", "FI", "EE", "IE", "CZ", "LV", "NL", "US". With a name it limits the search to that country and, for NO, FR, FI, EE, IE, CZ and LV, also searches the national register (most companies there have no LEI); with a number it says which register the number belongs to (e.g. "GB" for a UK number without a leading zero, "EE" for an Estonian registry code, "FI" for a Business ID typed without its dash, "IE" for an Irish CRO number, "CZ" for a Czech IČO). Empty = detect from the query.
- `vatNumber` (string): The VAT number the counterparty gave you, with its country prefix, e.g. "DK24256790". Checked live in VIES (valid or not, registered name) and matched against the register's name and country. Empty = the VAT number the register lists, if any (Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic); otherwise the VAT check is unverified.
- `iban` (string): The bank account the counterparty wants to be paid on, e.g. "DK5000400440116243". Checked offline: length, layout and ISO 13616 check digits, bank code, and whether its country matches the company's. No bank is contacted, so it does not prove who holds the account.
- `walletAddresses` (array): Wallet addresses the counterparty wants to be paid on, e.g. ["0x7FF9cFad3877F21d41Da833E2F775dB0569eE3D9"]. Each is matched exactly against the addresses OFAC lists. At most 10.
- `companies` (array): Check a list of companies in one run instead of `query`: up to 10 companies, each a name or number ("Tesco PLC") or an object with the fields above, e.g. ["Tesco PLC", {"query": "Novo Nordisk A/S", "country": "DK", "vatNumber": "DK24256790"}, {"query": "00445790", "country": "GB"}]. One row per company, priced like a single check ($0.05 per company checked); an ambiguous name, or a company no source knows or that does not answer in time, is a row that costs nothing. Leave `query` empty when you use this.

### Output fields

- `query` (string): The input as given.
- `status` (string): checked, or ambiguous (candidates returned, nothing charged).
- `company` (object | null): Identity from the register and GLEIF, with a source URL per value.
- `checks` (array): The checklist: check, status (pass, fail, review, unverified), detail, source, source_url, checked_at.
- `summary` (object): Counts per status, needs_attention (fail and review checks) and unverified_checks.
- `notice` (string): Screening aid, not a compliance, credit or legal determination.
- `latest_financials` (object | null): Newest fiscal year's key figures with basis and source.
- `people` (object | null): UK officers and PSCs, or Polish board, proxies and shareholders.
- `insolvency` (object | null): UK Gazette notices or Polish KRS proceedings.
- `us_listing` (object | null): SEC registrant data when the company files with the SEC.
- `sanctions` (object): entity (the company's screening row; `identifier_matches`: listings that carry the company's own registration number or LEI), people_with_matches, people_screened.
- `vat` (object | null): VIES result for the VAT number.
- `iban` (object | null): IBAN structure and country result.
- `wallets` (array): Wallet address screening rows.
- `candidates` (array): Only when status is ambiguous: companies that fit the name.
- `sanctions_hits` (array): Only when no single company was resolved (ambiguous or failed rows): sanctions listings matching the name asked for or a candidate's name (screened_name, listed_name, list_name, entry_id, score 0-100, source_url), screened free. Empty when none matched.
- `warnings` (array): Sources that failed or were partly read.
- `source_url` (string | null): The main identity source.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the check ran (UTC).

### Example input

```json
{ "query": "24256790", "country": "DK", "vatNumber": "DK24256790", "iban": "DK5000400440116243" }
```

## Company Check API: due diligence, LEI, financials & SEC filings

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/company-check.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/company-check
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/company-check
Price: Apify Store $0.03 per report; HTTP API $0.03 per company report
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/company-check, $0.03 per company report (max 1 report)

Company due diligence in one call: legal entity name, LEI, number, status, address, officers and owners, years of financials (revenue, profit, equity), SEC filings; UK Companies House charges, appointments and Gazette insolvency. By name, LEI, UK/DK/NO/FR/FI/EE/PL/IE/CZ/LV number, ticker or CIK.

Example questions:

- Who is Novo Nordisk legally, and what were its revenue and net income in the last three years? Cite your sources.

### Input fields

- `query` (string, required): The company to check: a name (e.g. "Novo Nordisk") or an identifier: LEI (20 characters, e.g. "724500Y6DUVHQD6OXN27"), UK company number ("00445790", "SC123456"), Danish CVR ("24256790"), Norwegian org number ("923609016"), French SIREN (9 digits, "552032534") or SIRET (14 digits, "55203253400703"), Finnish Business ID with its dash ("0112038-9"), Estonian registry code (8 digits, "12417834"), Irish CRO company number ("CRO 104547", or the digits with `country` IE), Czech IČO ("IČO 27074358", the company's VAT number "CZ27074358", or the digits with `country` CZ), Latvian registration number (11 digits, "40003032949"), US ticker in capitals or with $ ("AAPL", "$brk.b"; foreign companies listed in the US resolve to their home country), SEC CIK ("320193") or FDIC certificate of a US bank ("FDIC:628"). The type is detected from format and check digits; an 8-digit number valid in several registers (UK, Danish CVR, Estonian) is settled by asking them, and `country` decides when given. Required.
- `country` (string): ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code to disambiguate, e.g. "DK", "GB", "NO", "FR", "FI", "EE", "IE", "CZ", "LV", "NL", "US". With a name it limits the search to that country and, for NO, FR, FI, EE, IE, CZ and LV, also searches the national register (most companies there have no LEI); with a number it says which register the number belongs to (e.g. "GB" for a UK number without a leading zero, "EE" for an Estonian registry code, "FI" for a Business ID typed without its dash, "IE" for an Irish CRO number, "CZ" for a Czech IČO). Empty = detect from the query.
- `maxYears` (integer): How many fiscal years of key figures to return, newest first, e.g. 3. Default 3, maximum 10. Norway's open register holds the last 3 years only. The price is the same for any number of years.
- `include` (array): Which sections to fill: any of "identity", "financials", "us" (SEC filings of US issuers), "people" (UK officers and owners from Companies House; Polish board, proxies and shareholders from KRS), and the due-diligence sections "charges" (UK registered mortgages and secured debt), "appointments" (each current UK officer's other company appointments; also fills "people") and "insolvency" (UK: insolvency notices in The Gazette; Poland: bankruptcy, restructuring and liquidation entries from KRS), e.g. ["identity", "charges", "insolvency"]. Default (or empty) = identity, financials, us and people, plus insolvency for Polish companies (free from the KRS extract); the UK due-diligence sections only when listed. Fewer sections = fewer sources called, slightly faster; the price is the same.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query` (string): The query as given.
- `query_type` (string): How the query was read: lei, uk (UK company number), cvr, ee (Estonian registry code), orgnr (Norwegian org number), siren (French SIREN, also for a SIRET), ytunnus (Finnish Business ID), krs, nip or regon (Polish KRS number, tax ID or REGON), cro (Irish CRO company number), ico (Czech IČO), lv (Latvian registration number), fdic (FDIC certificate number), cik, ticker or name.
- `country` (string | null): ISO 3166 alpha-2 country of the company (its home country, also for a foreign company listed in the US). null when unknown.
- `identity` (object | null): Who the company is: from the national register, GLEIF, the SEC and (US banks) the FDIC (first source that has a value wins). null if no source had a record or the section was not requested.
- `financials` (object | null): Key figures of the last `maxYears` fiscal years, each with its source filing: a listed company's ESEF report first, else the national register, else the company's SEC XBRL filings (10-K, 20-F, 40-F). null when none were found (see not_found).
- `us` (object | null): The US listing: SEC EDGAR data for US issuers and for foreign companies listed in the US (by ticker, CIK, or a US company in GLEIF that the SEC lists). null otherwise.
- `bank` (object | null): US banks: the FDIC-insured bank of this company from the FDIC BankFind Suite (company level only). Filled for a US bank (found by FDIC certificate, LEI or name) and for a US bank holding company (its largest bank). Requested with the `us` section. null otherwise.
- `people` (object | null): UK companies: current officers (directors, secretaries) and persons with significant control (owners) from Companies House, with only the fields a KYB check needs (no addresses). Requested with the `people` section. null for other countries.
- `charges` (object | null): UK companies, with the `charges` section: charges (mortgages, debentures, other secured debt) registered at Companies House, newest first; an empty list means none registered. null when not requested or not UK.
- `insolvency` (object | null): With the `insolvency` section (default for Polish companies). UK: corporate insolvency notices in The Gazette (winding-up orders and petitions, administration, liquidation, creditors' meetings) from our nightly copy since 2020 (`covers_from`, `covers_to`), matched by the company number in the notice or, when the notice gives no number, the exact registered name (`matched_on`), newest first, in `notices`; notices under a former name without the number are not found; Open Government Licence v3.0. Poland: bankruptcy, restructuring, arrangement, liquidation, dissolution and receivership entries (KRS extract, Dział 6) in `proceedings` and enforced arrears (Dział 4) in `arrears`, read live; trustees and liquidators are not listed. An empty list means none found. null when not requested or for other countries.
- `candidates` (array): When a name (or a number valid in two registers) matches several companies: the top 3 (legal_name, country, lei, lei_status, registration_number, score 0-1). The report is for the first; re-run with its LEI or registration number (and country) to pick another. Empty when the match was clear.
- `not_found` (array): Requested sections without data, each {section, reason} in plain words an agent can relay.
- `warnings` (array): Sources that failed or timed out, and other caveats, in plain words. The rest of the report is still valid.
- `sources` (array): Every source used, each {section, name, url}.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the report was made (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): How long the lookup took.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.

### Example input

```json
{ "query": "Novo Nordisk", "country": "DK", "maxYears": 3 }
```

## VAT Number & IBAN Check API: EU VIES + IBAN validation

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/vat-iban-check.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/vat-iban-check
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/vat-iban-check
Price: Apify Store $0.002 per check with a definite answer; HTTP API $0.002 per definite check (VAT number answered by VIES, or a valid IBAN); malformed, failed and unverified are free
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/vat-iban-check, $0.002 per definite check (VAT number answered by VIES, or a valid IBAN); malformed, failed and unverified are free (max 10 VAT numbers and 50 IBANs)

Valid or not for EU VAT numbers (live from the official EU VIES service, with registered name, address and a name match) and IBANs (ISO 13616 check digits, length, bank code, country match). Pass, fail or unverified per check, with the source; unverified and malformed input are free.

Example questions:

- Check that supplier VAT number IE6388047V belongs to Google Ireland and that IBAN NL91ABNA0417164300 is valid.

### Input fields

- `vatNumbers` (array): EU VAT numbers to check live against VIES, each with its country prefix, e.g. ["IE6388047V", "NL004495445B01"]. Spaces, dots and dashes are ignored; GR is read as EL (Greece), XI is Northern Ireland. 0-10 numbers, checked one at a time (about 1-3 s each). Empty = no VAT check.
- `ibans` (array): IBANs to validate (check digits, length and layout per country, bank code), in electronic or print format, e.g. ["NL91ABNA0417164300", "DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00"]. 0-50 IBANs; no bank or third-party service is called. Empty = no IBAN check.
- `expectedName` (string): The company name you expect behind the VAT numbers, e.g. "Google Ireland Ltd". Compared with the name VIES returns after removing case, accents, punctuation and legal forms (Ltd = Limited, B.V., GmbH ...): name_match true or false; null when the member state shares no name (e.g. Germany). Empty = no name check.
- `expectedCountry` (string): ISO 3166 alpha-2 code of the country you expect, e.g. "NL". Compared with each IBAN's and VAT number's country (country_match; GB IBANs also match JE, GG and IM, FR IBANs the French overseas territories). Empty = no country check.
- `requesterVatNumber` (string): Your own EU VAT number, e.g. "NL123456789B01". VIES then returns a consultation number (consultation_number) that proves to a tax authority that you checked a number at a given time. Empty = no consultation number.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query` (string): The VAT number or IBAN as given.
- `check_type` (string): vat or iban.
- `number` (string | null): Normalised number: upper case without spaces, e.g. IE6388047V or NL91ABNA0417164300 (Greek VAT numbers with EL).
- `country_code` (string | null): Country of the number: VAT prefix (EL = Greece, XI = Northern Ireland) or IBAN country (ISO 3166 alpha-2); null if unreadable.
- `status` (string): pass = valid; fail = invalid (malformed, or VIES says not valid); unverified = VIES or the member state gave no answer (never means invalid; check again later).
- `valid` (boolean | null): true, false, or null when unverified.
- `reason` (string | null): Why the row failed or is unverified, in words an agent can act on. On a pass row: null, or which name or country check failed ("Valid, but country_match failed (...)").
- `registered_name` (string | null): Name registered with the VAT number, as VIES returns it; null when the member state does not share it (e.g. DE) or the number is not valid.
- `registered_address` (string | null): Registered address as VIES returns it (lines joined with commas); null when not shared.
- `request_date` (string | null): VIES request date-time (ISO 8601, UTC) of the answer; null for IBANs and unanswered requests.
- `consultation_number` (string | null): VIES consultation number, only when requesterVatNumber was given; keep it as proof of the check.
- `bank_code` (string | null): Bank identifier taken from a valid IBAN at the SWIFT IBAN Registry position, e.g. ABNA (NL) or 37040044 (DE).
- `sepa_country` (boolean | null): Whether the IBAN's country is in the SEPA scheme (SWIFT IBAN Registry).
- `expected_name` (string | null): expectedName from the input (VAT rows).
- `name_match` (boolean | null): expectedName equals the VIES name after removing case, accents, punctuation and legal forms; null when not asked or no name was shared.
- `expected_country` (string | null): expectedCountry from the input.
- `country_match` (boolean | null): The number's country equals expectedCountry (GB IBANs cover JE, GG, IM); null when not asked or not checked.
- `checks` (array): Every check made: {check (vat_format, vies_registration, name_match, iban_structure, country_match), status (pass/fail/unverified), detail, source}.
- `source` (string): Where the answer comes from: VIES (European Commission, answered by the national tax administration) or the ISO 13616 / SWIFT IBAN Registry rules.
- `source_url` (string): VIES page or the SWIFT IBAN Registry page.
- `provided_by` (string): Bosco Labs (boscolabs.dev).
- `checked_at` (string): ISO 8601 UTC time of the check.

### Example input

```json
{
  "vatNumbers": ["IE6388047V"],
  "ibans": ["NL91ABNA0417164300"],
  "expectedName": "Google Ireland Ltd",
  "expectedCountry": "IE",
  "requesterVatNumber": "NL123456789B01"
}
```

## Company Financials API: UK, Denmark (CVR), Norway accounts

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/company-accounts.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/company-accounts
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/company-accounts
Price: Apify Store $0.04 per company-year; HTTP API $0.04 per company-year
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/company-accounts, $0.04 per company-year (max 5 companies, 10 years per country (maxResults))

Company financials (revenue, profit, equity, cash, employees) from official annual reports, private companies included: UK Companies House (all digital years), Denmark by CVR number (all years), Norway Brønnøysund (3 years). Look up by company number, CVR or org number; adds LEI and sources.

Coverage: UK: accounts filed electronically with Companies House in the last ~60 days. Denmark: every annual report filed digitally with Erhvervsstyrelsen, all years. Norway: the last 3 fiscal years of every company that files accounts with the Brønnøysund Register (company accounts, not group accounts). Belgium only when the Actor owner has configured access. LEI looked up at GLEIF.

Example questions:

- What were Novo Nordisk's revenue and equity in its latest Danish annual report?
- Get the last three years of Equinor ASA's own accounts from the Norwegian register.
- What is the LEI and the latest net assets of UK company 03117531?

### Input fields

- `countries` (array): Registers to read, as codes: GB (Companies House), DK (Erhvervsstyrelsen), NO (Brønnøysund Regnskapsregisteret), BE (National Bank of Belgium; needs enterprise numbers and NBB access set up by the Actor owner). Default ["GB", "DK", "NO"]. Used only when no numbers are given (it then returns each country's newest filings); with numbers, the countries of those numbers are read and this is ignored.
- `companyNumbers` (array): UK Companies House numbers, e.g. ["03117531", "SC123456"] (shorter numbers are zero-padded to 8). Accounts of any year filed digitally (iXBRL), newest first; paper/PDF-only filings are skipped. Empty = the newest UK filings (last ~60 days).
- `cvrNumbers` (array): Danish CVR numbers, 8 digits, e.g. ["24256790"]. All years are available, newest first. Empty = the newest Danish filings.
- `orgNumbers` (array): Norwegian organisation numbers, 9 digits, e.g. ["923609016"]. The last 3 fiscal years are available, newest first. Empty = companies whose accounts were registered in the last 2 days.
- `enterpriseNumbers` (array): Belgian KBO/BCE enterprise numbers, 10 digits with or without dots, e.g. ["0403.170.701"]. Required for BE (there is no "newest filings" mode for Belgium), which works only when the Actor owner has set up NBB access.
- `enrichLei` (boolean): true (default) = look up each company's Legal Entity Identifier at GLEIF by its registration number and add `lei` and `lei_status` (null when the company has no LEI). false = skip the lookup.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum company-years per country, newest filings first, e.g. 1 for a company's latest accounts. Default 5. One row per company per fiscal year.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `country` (string): Country of the register (ISO 3166 alpha-2).
- `company_number` (string | null): UK Companies House company number (GB rows).
- `cvr` (string | null): Danish CVR number (DK rows).
- `org_number` (string | null): Norwegian organisation number (NO rows).
- `enterprise_number` (string | null): Belgian enterprise (KBO/BCE) number, 10 digits (BE rows).
- `company_name` (string | null): Registered name as tagged in the accounts (NO: from Enhetsregisteret; BE: from the filing reference).
- `lei` (string | null): Legal Entity Identifier found at GLEIF for this registration number; null when none is found or enrichLei is off.
- `lei_status` (string | null): GLEIF registration status of the LEI, e.g. ISSUED or LAPSED.
- `period_end` (string | null): Fiscal year end (YYYY-MM-DD), taken from the facts.
- `fiscal_year_start` (string | null): Fiscal year start (YYYY-MM-DD); null for balance-sheet-only accounts.
- `currency` (string | null): ISO 4217 currency of the monetary values.
- `revenue` (number | null): Turnover / revenue for the fiscal year. Small UK companies (filleted accounts) and Danish class B companies often don't publish it. NO: sales revenue (salgsinntekter), else total operating income.
- `gross_profit` (number | null): Gross profit (DK: bruttofortjeneste, often reported instead of revenue).
- `operating_profit` (number | null): Operating profit (EBIT).
- `profit_before_tax` (number | null): Profit before tax.
- `net_income` (number | null): Profit or loss for the year.
- `total_assets` (number | null): Total assets (DK; UK small-company balance sheets usually don't tag a total).
- `fixed_assets` (number | null): Fixed / non-current assets.
- `current_assets` (number | null): Current assets.
- `cash_and_equivalents` (number | null): Cash at bank and in hand / cash and cash equivalents.
- `total_equity` (number | null): Total equity (capital and reserves).
- `net_assets` (number | null): Net assets (UK balance sheet total).
- `net_current_assets` (number | null): Net current assets or liabilities (UK).
- `total_liabilities` (number | null): Total liabilities; when not tagged, total_assets - total_equity (sources says derived).
- `current_liabilities` (number | null): UK: creditors falling due within one year. DK: short-term liabilities other than provisions. NO: short-term debt. BE: amounts payable within one year.
- `noncurrent_liabilities` (number | null): UK: creditors falling due after more than one year. DK: long-term liabilities other than provisions. NO: long-term debt. BE: amounts payable after more than one year.
- `employees` (number | null): Average number of employees during the year (BE: full-time equivalents). Not in the Norwegian data.
- `metrics_found` (integer): How many of the normalized metrics were found.
- `sources` (object): Per metric: concept, fact_id, context_ref, period, unit, decimals of the source fact, or {derived: formula}. NO: concept is the JSON path in the record at source_data_url; BE: the NBB rubric code.
- `published` (string | null): GB: filing date (by company number) or date of the Companies House daily file (newest filings); DK: publication timestamp; BE: filing date; NO: null.
- `report_url` (string | null): GB (by company number): the accounts on the Companies House website; DK: the human-readable annual report (XHTML or PDF); NO: PDF copy of the filed accounts at Brønnøysund.
- `registry_url` (string | null): Company page in the official register (filing history / CVR).
- `source_document` (string | null): GB: Companies House filing transaction id (by company number) or file name of the accounts inside the daily bulk ZIP (newest filings).
- `source_url` (string): The page to cite: report_url when there is one, else registry_url.
- `source_data_url` (string): The machine-readable file the figures were read from. GB: the Companies House document (by company number, needs a key) or bulk ZIP (newest filings); DK: the XBRL file; NO: the Regnskapsregisteret JSON record; BE: the NBB accounting-data URL (needs a key).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the source was fetched.

### Example input

```json
{ "countries": ["GB", "DK", "NO"], "companyNumbers": ["03117531"], "cvrNumbers": ["24256790"], "orgNumbers": ["923609016"], "maxResults": 10 }
```

## UK New Companies API: daily Companies House incorporations

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/uk-new-companies.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/uk-new-companies
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/uk-new-companies
Price: Apify Store $0.002 per company; HTTP API $0.002 per company returned
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/uk-new-companies, $0.002 per company returned (max 200 companies (maxResults))

New UK companies incorporated on any day (default: yesterday) from the official Companies House API: number, name, type, status, SIC codes with descriptions, registered office address and a register link. Filter by SIC prefix, location and type. No director data.

Example questions:

- New UK companies incorporated yesterday in London with SIC 62 (IT).

### Input fields

- `incorporatedFrom` (string): Earliest incorporation date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-11-01". Empty = the same day as `incorporatedTo` (so both empty = yesterday, UTC).
- `incorporatedTo` (string): Latest incorporation date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-11-04". Empty = yesterday (UTC), or `incorporatedFrom` if that is later.
- `sicCodes` (array): UK SIC 2007 code prefixes (Companies House condensed list); a prefix matches every code below it, e.g. ["62"] = IT / software, "6201" = software development, "56101" = licensed restaurants, "68" = real estate. A company matches if any of its SIC codes matches. Empty = all sectors.
- `location` (string): Registered office location as free text, passed to Companies House's location filter: a town, county or postcode (area), e.g. "London", "Manchester" or "EC1". Empty = all of the UK.
- `companyTypes` (array): Companies House company types, e.g. ["ltd"] (private limited), "plc", "llp", "private-limited-guarant-nsc" (company limited by guarantee), "limited-partnership". Default ["ltd", "plc", "llp"]. Pass [] for all types.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum companies to return, e.g. 500. Default 100. You pay per company delivered.
- `onlyNewSinceLastRun` (boolean): true = skip (and don't charge for) companies an earlier run with the same filters already delivered. For scheduled runs. Default false. Remembered in a named key-value store in your account. E.g. `true` for a daily scheduled run.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `company_number` (string): Companies House company number, 8 characters, e.g. 16812345 or SC812345.
- `company_name` (string | null): Registered company name.
- `company_type` (string | null): Companies House company type code, e.g. ltd, plc, llp.
- `company_subtype` (string | null): Subtype when set: community-interest-company or private-fund-limited-partnership.
- `company_status` (string | null): Company status code, e.g. active.
- `incorporation_date` (string): Date of incorporation (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `sic_codes` (array): SIC 2007 codes the company declared (up to four, 5 digits).
- `sic_descriptions` (array): Description of each SIC code from the Companies House condensed SIC list, in the same order as sic_codes; null for a code not on that list.
- `registered_office_address` (string | null): Registered office address as one line.
- `address_line_1` (string | null): Registered office: first address line.
- `address_line_2` (string | null): Registered office: second address line.
- `locality` (string | null): Registered office: town or city.
- `region` (string | null): Registered office: region or county, as filed (often empty).
- `postal_code` (string | null): Registered office: postcode.
- `postcode_area` (string | null): Postcode area (leading letters of the postcode), e.g. EC, M, SW.
- `country` (string | null): Registered office: country, e.g. England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland.
- `source_url` (string): The company's page on the Companies House register (find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `api_url` (string): The company profile in the Companies House API (needs an API key).
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the data was fetched.

### Example input

```json
{
  "incorporatedFrom": "2026-11-04",
  "incorporatedTo": "2026-11-04",
  "sicCodes": ["62"],
  "location": "London",
  "companyTypes": ["ltd", "plc", "llp"],
  "maxResults": 100,
  "onlyNewSinceLastRun": false
}
```

## Company Hiring Signals API: open roles, departments, locations

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/company-hiring-signals.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/company-hiring-signals
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/company-hiring-signals
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per company found plus $0.001 per job row; HTTP API $0.001 per unit: a company summary = 5 units ($0.005), a job row = 1 ($0.001); companies without a public job board are free
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/company-hiring-signals, $0.001 per unit: a company summary = 5 units ($0.005), a job row = 1 ($0.001); companies without a public job board are free (max 5 companies x 200 jobs)

Is a company hiring? Open roles by department, location and remote share, newest and oldest posting dates and top titles, plus job rows with a link each. Read from the company's public Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby job board. Look up by name, domain or board URL.

Example questions:

- Is Notion hiring engineers? How many roles, where, and since when? Link the postings.

### Input fields

- `companies` (array, required): Companies to check, 1-50: a name ("Notion"), a website domain ("stripe.com"), a job board URL ("https://jobs.lever.co/spotify", "https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/airbnb", "https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/ramp") or provider:token ("greenhouse:stripe", "lever:spotify", "lever-eu:<token>", "ashby:notion"). Names and domains are matched to likely board names on Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby; a board URL is exact. Required.
- `departments` (array): Only count and return roles whose department or team has a word starting with one of these, case-insensitive, e.g. ["engineering", "data"]. Department names are each company's own (Stripe uses "Tech" and team codes), so `keywords` on the title is often more reliable. Empty = all departments.
- `locations` (array): Only roles whose location text, other locations or country contains one of these as whole words, case-insensitive ("US" does not match "Australia"), e.g. ["London", "Germany", "remote"]. Lever gives ISO country codes ("GB"), Ashby country names; Greenhouse has the location text only. Empty = all locations.
- `keywords` (array): Only roles whose job title has a word starting with one of these, case-insensitive ("engineer" matches "Engineering", "ai" not "Retail"), e.g. ["engineer", "data scientist"]. Empty = all titles.
- `postedSince` (string): Only roles first published on or after this date: an ISO date ("2026-10-01") or a number of days back ("30d"). Greenhouse: first published; Lever: created; Ashby: last published. Empty = any date.
- `maxJobsPerCompany` (integer): Most job rows to return per company, newest first, e.g. 20. Default 50, maximum 1000; 0 = summary only. The summary always counts all matching roles, whatever this limit. Each job row is charged.
- `summaryOnly` (boolean): true = one summary row per company and no job rows (cheapest; answers "is X hiring and where?"). Default false.
- `compareWithPrevious` (boolean): true = add a `trend` (change in open roles, new and closed jobs) versus the last run that also had this on, and save this run's job IDs for next time in the key-value store "company-hiring-signals-history" in your account. The first run has no trend. Default false.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `row_type` (string): company_summary (one per input company, found or not) or job (one per open role).
- `company` (string): The company as given in the input.
- `found` (boolean | null): Summary rows: true if a public job board was found. Not-found rows are free of charge.
- `provider` (string | null): Job board provider: greenhouse, lever, lever-eu (Lever's EU instance) or ashby.
- `board_token` (string | null): The company's board name at the provider, e.g. stripe. Pass it as provider:token for an exact lookup.
- `board_url` (string | null): Summary rows: the company's public job board page.
- `source_url` (string | null): Summary rows: the public API URL all counts were computed from. Job rows: the job's public posting page.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `total_open_roles` (integer | null): Summary rows: all open roles on the board, before filters.
- `matching_roles` (integer | null): Summary rows: open roles matching departments, locations, keywords and postedSince. All counts below are over these.
- `filters` (object | null): Summary rows: the filters applied (lower-cased), null if none.
- `by_department` (array): Summary rows: top 15 departments as {name, count}, largest first. Roles without a department are not listed.
- `by_location` (array): Summary rows: top 15 primary locations as {name, count}; spelling variants (US-Remote, US Remote) and a bare city with its City, Country form count as one.
- `by_country` (array): Summary rows: top 15 countries as {name, count}: ISO codes for Lever, country names for Ashby; for Greenhouse (no country field) names read from the location text.
- `remote_share` (number | null): Summary rows: share of matching roles marked remote, 0-1. Greenhouse: roles whose location text says remote. null when no roles match.
- `posted_last_30_days` (integer | null): Summary rows: matching roles posted in the 30 days before retrieved_at.
- `newest_posted_at` (string | null): Summary rows: newest posting date among matching roles (ISO 8601 UTC).
- `oldest_posted_at` (string | null): Summary rows: oldest posting date among matching roles: how long the company has been hiring for its open roles.
- `top_titles` (array): Summary rows: the 10 most common job titles as {title, count}.
- `trend` (object | null): Summary rows with compareWithPrevious: {previous_retrieved_at, previous_total_open_roles, change, new_jobs, closed_jobs} versus the last such run. null on the first run or when off.
- `jobs_returned` (integer | null): Summary rows: job rows returned for this company (at most maxJobsPerCompany, newest first).
- `other_boards` (array): Summary rows: other boards found for the same name (usually old, smaller ones). The board with most open roles is used.
- `not_found_reason` (string | null): Summary rows: why no board was found, and how to fix it. null when found.
- `warnings` (array): Summary rows: caveats in plain words, e.g. a provider that could not be read or several providers with a board under the same name.
- `job_id` (string | null): Job rows: the provider's job posting ID.
- `title` (string | null): Job rows: job title as published.
- `department` (string | null): Job rows: department (Greenhouse: top-level department).
- `team` (string | null): Job rows: team or sub-department, null if none or the same as department.
- `location` (string | null): Job rows: primary location as written by the company.
- `other_locations` (array): Job rows: further locations of the same posting (Lever, Ashby).
- `country` (string | null): Job rows: country: ISO 3166 alpha-2 for Lever, country name for Ashby, null for Greenhouse.
- `workplace_type` (string | null): Job rows: remote, hybrid or on-site (Lever, Ashby); null when not stated or on Greenhouse.
- `remote` (boolean | null): Job rows: true if remote; false if hybrid or on-site; null when unknown. Greenhouse: true when the location text says remote, else null.
- `employment_type` (string | null): Job rows: as the provider gives it, e.g. FullTime, Intern (Ashby) or Permanent (Lever commitment). null on Greenhouse.
- `posted_at` (string | null): Job rows: ISO 8601 UTC. Greenhouse: first published; Lever: created; Ashby: last published.
- `updated_at` (string | null): Job rows: last update (Greenhouse only), ISO 8601 UTC.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the board was read (ISO 8601 UTC).

### Example input

```json
{
  "companies": ["stripe.com", "Notion", "https://jobs.lever.co/spotify"],
  "departments": ["engineering"],
  "postedSince": "30d",
  "maxJobsPerCompany": 20
}
```

## Sanctions List Screening API: OFAC, UK, EU, UN & US lists

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/sanctions-screening.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/sanctions-screening
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/sanctions-screening
Price: Apify Store $0.01 per name or wallet address screened; HTTP API $0.01 per name or wallet address screened (an address no list could be checked against is free)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/sanctions-screening, $0.01 per name or wallet address screened (an address no list could be checked against is free) (max 50 names and 50 addresses)

Sanctions list screening and search: is this company, vessel, person or crypto wallet sanctioned? Per name or address (fuzzy, alias-aware): yes/no, the listed entry, aliases, programs, source link, from OFAC SDN and non-SDN, the US Consolidated Screening List, UK, EU and UN Security Council lists.

Example questions:

- Before we sign with these suppliers, check whether Sovcomflot or Novo Nordisk A/S are on any sanctions list, and cite the lists you checked.

### Input fields

- `names` (array): Company, vessel or person names to check, one per entry, as plain text, e.g. ["Sovcomflot", "Novo Nordisk A/S", "Vladimir Putin"]. Legal forms (Ltd, LLC, GmbH, PJSC), accents, punctuation and word order are ignored. Up to 200 names; each name gives one result row and one charge; repeats are screened once. Give names, addresses or both.
- `addresses` (array): Crypto wallet addresses to check, one per entry, e.g. ["0x7FF9cFad3877F21d41Da833E2F775dB0569eE3D9"]. Matched exactly against the wallet addresses the lists publish (OFAC SDN: XBT, ETH, USDT, TRX and more); EVM 0x and bech32 bc1 addresses ignore case, others must match as written. Up to 50; each checked address gives one result row and one charge, same price as a name (an address no selected list publishes wallets for is answered free). Give names, addresses or both.
- `country` (string): Country of the party you are screening, as an ISO 3166 alpha-2 code or English name, e.g. "RU" or "Russia". It never hides a match: listings that name other countries move to the end and get country_match false. Empty = no country ranking.
- `entityType` (string): Only return listings of this type, e.g. "organization". Default "any". Listings whose type the list does not state (the US Commerce and State lists) are always kept.
- `minScore` (integer): Lowest similarity score (0-100) that counts as a match, e.g. 85 (default). 100 = same name after normalisation; 90-99 = small spelling differences or the name inside a longer listed name; lower values find more variants and more false positives. Range 50-100.
- `lists` (array): Which lists to check, any of "ofac_sdn", "ofac_consolidated", "us_csl", "uk", "eu", "un", e.g. ["ofac_sdn", "uk"]. Default (or empty) = all six. The price is the same for any number of lists.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query` (string): The name or wallet address as given.
- `address` (string): Address rows only: the wallet address as given (trimmed).
- `chain` (string | null): Address rows only: currency code(s) the list gives for the matched address, e.g. ETH or USDT/USDC; for an unmatched address a guess from its format (EVM, TRX, XBT) or null.
- `match_found` (boolean): True when at least one listing scored >= min_score.
- `match_count` (integer): Number of listings at or above min_score (only the top 5 are in matches).
- `best_score` (integer | null): Highest score, null when nothing matched.
- `summary` (string): One sentence an agent can pass on: the best match, or 'No match >= N' with every list checked and its date; ends with 'INCOMPLETE: not checked: ...' when an asked list could not be loaded.
- `complete` (boolean): True when every asked list was checked. False: a no-match covers only lists_checked.
- `lists_not_checked` (array): Names of asked lists that could not be loaded for this run (empty when complete).
- `notice` (string): Screening aid on official lists only (no PEP or adverse media); neither a match nor no match is a compliance determination.
- `matches` (array): Top 5 listings, best first (listings in other countries than `country` last).
- `lists_checked` (array): Every list this answer covers, with its publish date (version_date), when it was downloaded (fetched_at), its number of entries and the official file URL. Address rows list only the lists that publish wallet addresses, with their number of addresses instead of entries.
- `warnings` (array): Lists that could not be downloaded (not checked, or checked from an older cached copy), in plain words.
- `min_score` (integer): Threshold used.
- `entity_type` (string): Entity type filter used.
- `country` (string | null): Country used for ranking (ISO-2), or null.
- `attribution` (string): Source notices for the lists checked (ITA non-endorsement, Open Government Licence v3.0, EU reuse; see LEGAL.md).
- `checked_at` (string): When the screening ran (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.

### Example input

```json
{ "names": ["Sovcomflot", "Huawei Technologies", "Petrel 8"], "entityType": "any", "minScore": 85 }
```

## EU Law Lookup API (EUR-Lex): article text, in force, amendments

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/eu-law-lookup.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/eu-law-lookup
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/eu-law-lookup
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per act or article returned; HTTP API $0.005 per act or article returned
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/eu-law-lookup, $0.005 per act or article returned (max 50 results (maxResults))

The text of an EU law article as in force today (or on a date), whether the act is in force, what amended it, plus new Official Journal acts. Ask by name (GDPR, AI Act), citation, CELEX or ELI; 24 languages. Official EUR-Lex/Cellar data with a source link per row.

Example questions:

- What does Article 50 of the AI Act require today, and has it been amended? Quote the text and link the source.

### Input fields

- `query` (string): The EU act to look up: a short name ("GDPR", "AI Act", "DSA", "NIS2", "DORA", "MiCA", "CSRD"...), a citation ("Regulation (EU) 2024/1689", "Directive 95/46/EC", "Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006"), a bare number ("2016/679"), a CELEX number ("32016R0679") or an ELI URI ("http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj"). "AI Act Article 50" also works. Leave empty only when using ojSince (new Official Journal acts). An unreadable citation fails in seconds, with examples, at no charge.
- `article` (string): Article number, optionally with a paragraph: "5", "6(1)", "4a"; several separated by commas ("5, 6(1)", up to 10). One row per article. Empty = one row for the whole act with its table of contents and recital count (no full text unless include has "text").
- `language` (string): EU language code of the text and titles: BG, CS, DA, DE, EL, EN, ES, ET, FI, FR, GA, HR, HU, IT, LT, LV, MT, NL, PL, PT, RO, SK, SL, SV. Default EN. If the text is missing in that language, English is returned with a warning. E.g. "DE".
- `asOf` (string): YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2025-01-01": return the consolidated version that applied on that date. Empty = today (the newest consolidated version in force now). Acts without consolidated versions return the Official Journal text.
- `include` (array): Any of "metadata" (always on), "amendments" (amended_by, corrected_by, repealed_by, amends, repeals), "citing" (acts and judgments that cite this act, newest first) and "text" (the whole act as plain text, cut at maxTextChars). Default ["metadata", "amendments"]. The price is the same.
- `maxTextChars` (integer): Cap on article_text and text, in characters, e.g. 30000 (default). Longer text is cut and flagged (article_text_truncated / text_truncated) with a warning.
- `maxCiting` (integer): With include "citing": how many citing acts to list, newest first, e.g. 20 (default). citing_acts_total always gives the full count.
- `ojSince` (string): Switches to Official Journal mode: list acts published in the OJ L series from this date (YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-11-03") until today, newest first, at most 31 days back. Leave query empty when you use this. Empty = normal lookup.
- `keywords` (string): OJ mode only: comma-separated words or phrases; an act is kept when its title (in the chosen language) contains any of them, case-insensitive, e.g. "artificial intelligence, data". Empty = all acts.
- `maxResults` (integer): OJ mode only: the most acts to return, newest first, e.g. 50 (default). One charge per act returned.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query` (string | null): The query as given (null in OJ mode).
- `celex` (string): CELEX number of the act, e.g. 32016R0679.
- `eli` (string | null): European Legislation Identifier URI of the act, e.g. http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj.
- `title` (string | null): Official title in the chosen language (null if Cellar has none in that language).
- `act_type` (string | null): Type of act, e.g. Regulation, Directive, Implementing regulation, Corrigendum.
- `act_type_code` (string | null): Publications Office resource-type code, e.g. REG, DIR, DEC_IMPL, CORRIGENDUM.
- `date_document` (string | null): Date of the document (signature/adoption), YYYY-MM-DD.
- `date_publication` (string | null): Date of publication in the Official Journal, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `oj_reference` (string | null): Official Journal reference for acts published act by act (since Oct 2023), e.g. "OJ L, 2024/1689".
- `date_entry_into_force` (string | null): Earliest date of entry into force, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `entry_into_force_dates` (array): All entry-into-force / effect dates EUR-Lex records (staged application), sorted.
- `date_end_of_validity` (string | null): End of validity, YYYY-MM-DD; null when open-ended.
- `in_force` (boolean | null): Whether EUR-Lex marks the act as in force today.
- `eur_lex_url` (string): EUR-Lex page of the original act.
- `summary_url` (string | null): EUR-Lex plain-language summary of the act, when one exists.
- `language` (string): Language of the text and titles returned (EN when the requested one was unavailable).
- `as_of` (string | null): The asOf date used (null = today).
- `latest_consolidated_version_date` (string | null): Date of the newest consolidated version EUR-Lex holds (may be later than asOf).
- `text_version` (string | null): "consolidated" (EUR-Lex consolidated version, documentation only) or "original" (OJ text); null if no text.
- `text_celex` (string | null): CELEX of the text the article was read from, e.g. 02024R1689-20260727 for a consolidated version.
- `consolidated_version_date` (string | null): Date of the consolidated version used, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `text_notice` (string | null): For consolidated texts: EUR-Lex's own disclaimer (no legal effect; the OJ text is authentic).
- `source_url` (string): EUR-Lex page of the exact text version used (consolidated version or OJ act).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `cellar_url` (string | null): The Cellar document the text was read from.
- `amended_by` (array): Acts that amend this act: {celex, title, date, url}, newest first (include amendments).
- `corrected_by` (array): Corrigenda to this act: {celex, title, date, url}.
- `repealed_by` (array): Acts that repeal this act: {celex, title, date, url}.
- `implicitly_repealed_by` (array): Acts that implicitly repeal this act.
- `amends` (array): Acts this act amends: {celex, title, date, url}.
- `repeals` (array): Acts this act repeals.
- `implicitly_repeals` (array): Acts this act implicitly repeals.
- `citing_acts` (array | null): Legislation and case-law citing this act, newest first, up to maxCiting: {celex, title, date, url} (include citing).
- `citing_acts_total` (integer | null): How many legislative acts and judgments cite this act.
- `article` (string | null): The article returned, e.g. "50"; null for an act-level row.
- `paragraph` (string | null): The paragraph returned, e.g. "1"; null = whole article.
- `article_title` (string | null): Heading of the article, e.g. "Principles relating to processing of personal data".
- `article_text` (string | null): Plain text of the article (or paragraph), one line per paragraph or point, numbering kept ("1.", "(a)").
- `article_text_truncated` (boolean | null): True when article_text was cut at maxTextChars.
- `article_amended_by` (array): In a consolidated text: acts that changed this article (from EUR-Lex's change markers), {celex, change}.
- `recitals_count` (integer | null): Act-level row: number of recitals in the OJ text.
- `articles_count` (integer | null): Act-level row: number of articles in the text used.
- `table_of_contents` (array): Act-level row: [{article, title}] for every article, to pick one for a follow-up call.
- `text` (string | null): Whole act as plain text, cut at maxTextChars (include text only).
- `text_truncated` (boolean | null): True when text was cut at maxTextChars.
- `warnings` (array): Caveats in plain words: fallbacks, not in force on asOf, truncation, partial data.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the row was made (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): How long the lookup took.

### Example input

```json
{ "query": "AI Act", "article": "50", "language": "EN", "asOf": "2026-11-05" }
```

## UK & Dutch Law Lookup API: article text by date, in force

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/national-law-lookup.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/national-law-lookup
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/national-law-lookup
Price: Apify Store $0.01 per article or act returned; HTTP API $0.005 per article or act returned
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/national-law-lookup, $0.005 per article or act returned (max 5 articles)

The text of a UK section or Dutch article as in force today (or on a date), whether it is in force and what changed it. Ask by citation: "Companies Act 2006 s 172", "BW 7:658", "artikel 13 Wet Vpb 1969". Official legislation.gov.uk and Dutch BWB data with a source link per row.

Example questions:

- What does article 13 of the Dutch Wet op de vennootschapsbelasting 1969 say as of 1 January 2025? Quote it and link the source.

### Input fields

- `query` (string, required): The act, optionally with the article. UK: a short title with a section ("Companies Act 2006 s 172", "section 172 of the Companies Act 2006"), a short name ("CA 2006", "DPA 2018", "UK GDPR", "PECR"; 35 common acts), a legislation.gov.uk path or URL ("ukpga/2006/46/section/172"), a chapter ("2006 c. 46") or an SI ("S.I. 2003/2426 reg 6"). NL: "BW 7:658", "artikel 13 Wet Vpb 1969", "Awb 8:1", "art. 310 Sr", an abbreviation (BW1-10, Sr, Sv, Rv, Awb, UAVG, Wft, Wwft, Woo ...), a citeertitel, a BWB id ("BWBR0002672"), a jci reference or a wetten.overheid.nl URL. Required. An unreadable citation fails in seconds, with examples, at no charge.
- `jurisdiction` (string): "UK" or "NL". Default empty = detected from the citation (paths, BWB ids, known names, Dutch or English words); set it when a bare name is ambiguous.
- `article` (string): Section, regulation or article number, optionally with a subsection or lid: "172", "172(1)", "7:658", "13 lid 2", "8:1"; several separated by commas (up to 5, e.g. "171, 172"). One row per article. Overrides an article in the query. Empty = the article in the query, or else one row for the whole act with its table of contents.
- `asOf` (string): YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2025-01-01": return the text as in force on that date (UK point-in-time version; NL consolidated version, newest correction). Empty = today.
- `language` (string): Optional, "EN" or "NL". UK texts are English and Dutch texts are Dutch: there is no official English translation of Dutch legislation, so EN for a Dutch act returns the Dutch text with a warning. Default empty = the source language.
- `maxTextChars` (integer): Cap on article_text, in characters, e.g. 30000 (default). Longer text is cut and flagged (article_text_truncated) with a warning.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query` (string | null): The query as given.
- `jurisdiction` (string): "UK" or "NL".
- `act_id` (string): Identifier of the act: legislation.gov.uk path ("ukpga/2006/46") or BWB id ("BWBR0005290"). Same role as celex in eu-law-lookup.
- `eli` (string | null): European Legislation Identifier URI (UK, e.g. http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/2006/46); null for NL.
- `title` (string | null): Short title or citeertitel, e.g. "Companies Act 2006", "Burgerlijk Wetboek Boek 7".
- `long_title` (string | null): Long title (UK) or intitule (NL).
- `act_type` (string | null): Type of act, e.g. "UK Public General Act", "UK Statutory Instrument", "Wet", "Algemene maatregel van bestuur".
- `act_type_code` (string | null): Source code for the type: legislation.gov.uk type (ukpga, uksi, asp...) or BWB soort (wet, AMvB, ministeriele-regeling...).
- `date_document` (string | null): UK: date of Royal Assent or making; NL: date of signature. YYYY-MM-DD.
- `date_publication` (string | null): NL: issue date of the original Staatsblad/Staatscourant; null when unknown and for UK.
- `official_publication` (string | null): Official reference: UK chapter or SI number ("2006 c. 46", "S.I. 2003/2426"), NL publication ("Stb. 1991, 600"). Same role as oj_reference in eu-law-lookup.
- `date_entry_into_force` (string | null): UK article rows: when the section came into force (from its commencement note); NL: when the regulation first entered into force. YYYY-MM-DD.
- `date_end_of_validity` (string | null): NL: last day of the last consolidated version when the regulation has lapsed (vervallen); null when open-ended and for UK.
- `in_force` (boolean | null): Whether the returned article (for NL act rows: the act) is in force on as_of (default today). UK act rows: null.
- `act_url` (string): Official page of the act (legislation.gov.uk id URI or wetten.overheid.nl).
- `language` (string): Language of the text: EN (UK) or NL (NL).
- `as_of` (string | null): The asOf date used (null = today).
- `latest_consolidated_version_date` (string | null): Date of the newest consolidated (revised) version the source holds; may be later than as_of.
- `text_version` (string | null): "consolidated" (revised / geconsolideerde tekst) or "original" (as enacted or made, UK only).
- `consolidated_version_date` (string | null): Date from which the version used applies, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `text_notice` (string | null): Licence attribution and the source's status note: revised texts are editorial consolidations; for NL the authentic text is the Staatsblad/Staatscourant publication.
- `source_url` (string): Page of the exact text version used (article-level when available).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `data_url` (string | null): The XML the text was read from. Same role as cellar_url in eu-law-lookup.
- `article` (string | null): The section, regulation or article returned, e.g. "172", "658", "8:1"; null for an act-level row.
- `paragraph` (string | null): The subsection (UK) or lid (NL) returned; null = whole article.
- `article_title` (string | null): Heading of the section or article (UK sections have one; most Dutch articles do not).
- `article_text` (string | null): Plain text, one line per subsection, paragraph or list item, numbering kept (UK "(1)", "(a)"; NL "1.", "a.").
- `article_text_truncated` (boolean | null): True when article_text was cut at maxTextChars.
- `article_amended_by` (array): Changes to this article: UK textual amendments shown with it (F-notes), NL the publication that last changed it. Items {source, date, change, url}.
- `pending_changes` (array): UK: changes legislation.gov.uk lists as not yet applied to this provision, {type, affected, source, url, in_force_date}. Always [] for NL.
- `articles_count` (integer | null): Act-level row: number of sections or articles (NL: not repealed).
- `table_of_contents` (array): Act-level row: [{article, title}] for up to 500 sections or articles, to pick one for a follow-up call.
- `warnings` (array): Caveats in plain words: not in force on asOf, repealed, newer version coming, fallbacks, truncation.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the row was made (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): How long the lookup took.

### Example input

```json
{ "query": "Wet op de vennootschapsbelasting 1969 artikel 13", "asOf": "2025-01-01" }
```

## Dutch Case Law API (Rechtspraak): court rulings by ECLI

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/dutch-case-law.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/dutch-case-law
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/dutch-case-law
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per decision returned; HTTP API $0.005 per court decision returned
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/dutch-case-law, $0.005 per court decision returned (max 25 ECLIs + 25 search results (maxResults))

Dutch court rulings (uitspraken) by ECLI or by keyword, court and date: case numbers, legal area, summary (inhoudsindicatie), appeal/cassation links, law references, full text on request. Hoge Raad (Supreme Court), Raad van State, appeal and district courts. Official Rechtspraak Open Data, sourced.

Example questions:

- Find Hoge Raad rulings on tenancy law (huurrecht) since 2024 and summarise what each one decided, with links.

### Input fields

- `ecli` (string): One or more Dutch ECLIs, separated by commas or spaces, e.g. "ECLI:NL:HR:2024:123" or "ECLI:NL:HR:2024:123, ECLI:NL:RVS:2024:1000" (max 100). Lower case and uitspraken.rechtspraak.nl links also work. One row per ECLI; an unknown ECLI fails at no charge. Empty = search with the fields below (both can be combined: ECLI rows come first).
- `query` (string): Words to find in the decision's title and summary (inhoudsindicatie), case-insensitive. Commas separate alternatives, words within one alternative must all appear: "huur, pacht" = huur OR pacht; "ontslag op staande voet" = all four words. Summaries are in Dutch, so use Dutch words. The official API has no full-text search: this filters the newest-updated decisions that match the other filters (up to 10,000 scanned). Empty = no keyword filter.
- `courts` (array): Court codes as used in the ECLI, e.g. ["HR"] for the Hoge Raad (Supreme Court); others: PHR (Procureur-Generaal/AG opinions), RVS (Raad van State), CRVB, CBB, GHAMS, GHARL, GHDHA, GHSHE (courts of appeal), RBAMS, RBDHA, RBROT, RBMNE ... (district courts). Full Dutch names also work. Empty = all courts.
