- `legalAreas` (array): Rechtsgebied names, e.g. ["Strafrecht"], ["Belastingrecht", "Arbeidsrecht"]; English also works: criminal, civil, administrative, tax, employment, immigration, insolvency, family, competition, environmental. A main area includes its sub-areas. Empty = all areas.
- `dateFrom` (string): Earliest decision date (uitspraakdatum), YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2024-01-01". Empty = no lower limit (to today if dateTo is empty).
- `dateTo` (string): Latest decision date, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2024-12-31". Empty = today when dateFrom is set, else no limit.
- `documentType` (string): "uitspraak" = court decisions only, "conclusie" = opinions of the Advocate-General at the Hoge Raad only. Empty = both.
- `maxResults` (integer): Most decisions to return from a search, most recently published or updated first, e.g. 20 (default). One charge per decision returned.
- `includeText` (boolean): true = add the full decision as plain text (section headings as '## ', numbered paragraphs kept), cut at maxTextChars. Default false: metadata and summary only (small rows). Same price. E.g. `true`.
- `maxTextChars` (integer): With includeText: cap on the text per decision in characters, e.g. 20000 (default). Longer text is cut and flagged (text_truncated, text_chars gives the full length).

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `ecli` (string): European Case Law Identifier of the decision, e.g. ECLI:NL:HR:2024:123.
- `title` (string | null): Rechtspraak's display title: ECLI, court, decision date and case numbers.
- `court` (string | null): Court (instantie) name, e.g. Hoge Raad, Raad van State, Rechtbank Amsterdam.
- `court_code` (string | null): Court code from the ECLI, e.g. HR, RVS, CRVB, GHAMS, RBAMS.
- `court_id` (string | null): The court's identifier URI in the Rechtspraak value list.
- `document_type` (string | null): "uitspraak" (decision) or "conclusie" (Advocate-General's opinion).
- `decision_date` (string | null): Date of the decision or opinion (uitspraakdatum), YYYY-MM-DD.
- `publication_date` (string | null): Date the text was published on rechtspraak.nl, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `modified` (string | null): Last change to the metadata or text, ISO 8601 (Rechtspraak local time).
- `case_numbers` (array): Case numbers (zaaknummers) as published, e.g. ["22/01066"].
- `seat` (string | null): Place of session (zittingsplaats), when given.
- `legal_areas` (array): Legal areas (rechtsgebieden), e.g. ["Strafrecht"].
- `procedures` (array): Procedure types, e.g. ["Cassatie"], ["Hoger beroep"].
- `language` (string | null): Language code of the metadata record (nl); English translations say so in the summary.
- `summary` (string | null): The court's own summary (inhoudsindicatie) as plain text; null when none.
- `relations` (array): Formal relations to other decisions: {ecli, relation (hogerBeroep, cassatie, conclusie, ...), direction (earlier = the other decision is from an earlier instance, later = a later one), outcome (e.g. bekrachtiging/bevestiging, vernietiging, contrair), label, url}.
- `references` (array): References to legislation and case law: {type (law, case_law, eu_law, local_regulation), label, identifier (BWB jci or ECLI), bwb_id, article, url}.
- `published_in` (array): Where the decision is published (vindplaatsen), e.g. ["Rechtspraak.nl", "NJ 2014/336"].
- `replaces` (array): Old identifiers (LJN) this ECLI replaces.
- `replaced_by` (string | null): ECLI that replaces this one, if it was withdrawn.
- `has_text` (boolean): Whether rechtspraak.nl publishes the decision text (false = metadata only).
- `text_chars` (integer | null): Length of the full plain text in characters (null without text).
- `text` (string | null): The decision as plain text (includeText only): '## ' section headings, numbering kept, footnotes at the end; cut at maxTextChars.
- `text_truncated` (boolean | null): True when text was cut at maxTextChars; null without includeText.
- `source_url` (string): The decision on uitspraken.rechtspraak.nl.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `data_url` (string): The official Open Data XML this row was read from.
- `warnings` (array): Caveats in plain words: text cut, metadata only, replaced ECLI, keyword scan limit.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the row was made (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): How long fetching this decision took.

### Example input

```json
{ "query": "huurrecht", "courts": ["HR"], "dateFrom": "2024-01-01", "maxResults": 20 }
```

## Federal Register & eCFR API: CFR text as of a date, changes

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/us-federal-rules.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/us-federal-rules
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/us-federal-rules
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per section, $0.002 per document; HTTP API $0.001 per unit: a CFR section with text = 5 units ($0.005), a Federal Register document = 2 ($0.002); rows without text are free
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/us-federal-rules, $0.001 per unit: a CFR section with text = 5 units ($0.005), a Federal Register document = 2 ($0.002); rows without text are free (max 10 CFR units or 50 documents)

Federal Register documents and Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR) text: a CFR section as in force today or on any date, its amendment history and the rules that changed it; what changed in a CFR part since a date; Federal Register search by agency or number. Official data, a source link per row.

Example questions:

- What changed in the Export Administration Regulations part 744 since August, and which Federal Register notices did it? Link the sources.

### Input fields

- `citation` (string): A CFR section, part or appendix: "21 CFR 101.9", "17 CFR 240.10b-5", "48 CFR 52.212-4", "15 CFR 744 Supplement No. 4", or an eCFR link ("https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-101.9"). A section or appendix returns one row: its text as in force on asOf, its amendment history and the Federal Register rules behind each change. A part ("15 CFR 744") returns its sections and appendices changed since the since date. Together with search, agency or documentType it instead limits Federal Register documents to that CFR part. Empty = no CFR lookup. An unreadable citation fails in seconds with examples, at no charge.
- `asOf` (string): YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2024-01-01": the CFR text in force on that date (eCFR history begins around January 2017). Empty = today (the eCFR's latest data, usually 1-2 days old).
- `since` (string): YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-11-01". With a part citation: list sections changed on or after this date (empty = the last 30 days). With a search: only documents published on or after this date (empty = any date). Ignored for a single section or a document number.
- `documentNumber` (string): One Federal Register document by its number, e.g. "2026-17231" (corrections look like "C1-2026-16628"). Returns its citation, type, agencies, dates, the CFR parts it affects and links. Empty = no document lookup. Takes precedence over every other field.
- `search` (string): Full-text search of Federal Register documents since 1994, newest first, e.g. "entity list". Combine with agency, documentType, since and citation. Empty = no word filter (agency or documentType alone also search).
- `agency` (string): Federal Register search by issuing agency: an acronym ("BIS", "FDA", "EPA", "SEC", "OFAC"), a name ("Bureau of Industry and Security") or a FederalRegister.gov slug ("industry-and-security-bureau"). Empty = all agencies. An unknown name fails with suggestions, at no charge.
- `documentType` (string): Federal Register search by type: RULE (final rules), PRORULE (proposed rules), NOTICE or PRESDOCU (presidential documents). Empty = all types. E.g. "RULE".
- `maxResults` (integer): Most rows to return: for a part citation the most recently changed units (max 25 per run, each with its text), for a search the newest documents (max 100). Default 20. One charge per row returned with an answer. E.g. 10.
- `maxTextChars` (integer): Cap on each section's text in characters, e.g. 20000 (default). Longer text is cut at a line end and flagged with text_truncated and a warning; source_url has the whole text.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `record_type` (string): "cfr_section" (a CFR section or appendix as of a date) or "fr_document" (a Federal Register document).
- `query` (string | null): The citation, document number or search as understood, e.g. "21 CFR 101.9".
- `citation` (string | null): cfr_section: the unit's CFR citation, e.g. "21 CFR 101.9". fr_document: the Federal Register citation (volume FR page), e.g. "91 FR 54658".
- `cfr_title` (integer): cfr_section: CFR title number (1-50), e.g. 21.
- `cfr_title_name` (string | null): cfr_section: name of the CFR title, e.g. "Food and Drugs".
- `part` (string | null): cfr_section: CFR part, e.g. "101".
- `subpart` (string | null): cfr_section: subpart letter, e.g. "A"; null when the part has none or for appendices.
- `section` (string | null): cfr_section: section number ("101.9") or appendix name ("Supplement No. 4 to Part 744").
- `unit_type` (string | null): cfr_section: "section" or "appendix".
- `heading` (string | null): cfr_section: the heading as printed, e.g. "§ 101.9 Nutrition labeling of food.".
- `as_of` (string | null): cfr_section: the date (YYYY-MM-DD) the text is in force for: asOf, capped at the eCFR's latest data.
- `text` (string | null): cfr_section: plain text as in force on as_of, one line per paragraph ("(a) ...", "(1) ..."), tables as "cell | cell" rows; cut at maxTextChars. Null when the unit was removed.
- `text_chars` (integer | null): cfr_section: length of text in characters (after any cut).
- `text_truncated` (boolean | null): cfr_section: true when text was cut at maxTextChars.
- `source_note` (string | null): cfr_section: the CFR source note with the Federal Register citation(s) that created the unit, e.g. "[58 FR 2175, Jan. 6, 1993]".
- `removed` (boolean | null): cfr_section: true when the unit was removed from the CFR on or before as_of.
- `latest_change_date` (string | null): cfr_section: date of the newest amendment on or before as_of (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `changed_since` (string | null): cfr_section from a part citation: the since date of the change window; null for a single-section lookup.
- `amendments` (array): cfr_section: amendment history from the eCFR versioner, newest first (max 50): {date, substantive, removed, fr_documents}. fr_documents lists final rules affecting this CFR part that took effect (or, failing that, were published) on that date: {document_number, citation, title, type, publication_date, effective_on, url}. They are the likely source of the change, matched by part and date (the Federal Register does not index by section). [] = looked up, none found; null = not looked up (only the 5 newest dates, or the dates inside the since window, are).
- `ecfr_up_to_date_as_of` (string | null): cfr_section: the date through which the eCFR title is current (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `source_url` (string | null): eCFR page of the unit as of as_of (cfr_section), or FederalRegister.gov page of the document (fr_document).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `api_url` (string | null): cfr_section: the eCFR versioner API call the text was read from.
- `document_number` (string | null): fr_document: Federal Register document number, e.g. "2026-17231".
- `title` (string | null): fr_document: document title.
- `type` (string | null): fr_document: "Rule", "Proposed Rule", "Notice" or "Presidential Document".
- `action` (string | null): fr_document: action line, e.g. "Final rule.".
- `abstract` (string | null): fr_document: the summary published with the document.
- `dates` (string | null): fr_document: the DATES paragraph as published, e.g. "This rule is effective August 21, 2026.".
- `agencies` (array): fr_document: issuing agencies as FederalRegister.gov names them, e.g. ["Commerce Department", "Industry and Security Bureau"].
- `publication_date` (string | null): fr_document: date published in the Federal Register (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `effective_on` (string | null): fr_document: effective date (YYYY-MM-DD); null when none is given (proposed rules, most notices).
- `comments_close_on` (string | null): fr_document: comment deadline (YYYY-MM-DD); null when not open for comment.
- `cfr_references` (array): fr_document: CFR parts the document affects, e.g. ["15 CFR 744"].
- `docket_ids` (array): fr_document: agency docket numbers.
- `regulation_id_numbers` (array): fr_document: Regulation Identifier Numbers (RIN), e.g. ["0694-AK49"].
- `start_page` (integer | null): fr_document: first Federal Register page.
- `end_page` (integer | null): fr_document: last Federal Register page.
- `significant` (boolean | null): fr_document: whether the rule is marked significant under EO 12866; null when not stated.
- `pdf_url` (string | null): fr_document: the official PDF on govinfo.gov (the legally authentic edition).
- `raw_text_url` (string | null): fr_document: full text as plain text on FederalRegister.gov.
- `warnings` (array): Caveats in plain words: text cut, date capped, more results than returned, part-level matching.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the row was made (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): How long the lookup took.

### Example input

```json
{ "citation": "21 CFR 101.9", "asOf": "2024-01-01" }
```

## Product Recall Check API: CPSC, NHTSA, FDA & EU Safety Gate

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/product-recalls.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/product-recalls
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/product-recalls
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per product checked; HTTP API $0.005 per product checked (every source answered)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/product-recalls, $0.005 per product checked (every source answered) (max 20 products)

Recalled yes/no, with each recall's date, hazard, remedy and official link, for a product name, brand, model, UPC/EAN or VIN. Checks US CPSC, NHTSA vehicle recalls, FDA enforcement reports (food, drugs, devices) and EU Safety Gate in one call. Lists every source checked.

Example questions:

- Before we list this used Peloton Bike+ and this 2012 Honda Accord for sale, check whether either has been recalled, for what hazard, and cite the source.

### Input fields

- `queries` (array, required): What to check, one per entry: a product name, brand or model ("Peloton Bike+"), a UPC/EAN barcode of 8-14 digits ("3418178586009"), a 17-character VIN ("1HGCP2F31CA000000") or a vehicle as year make model ("2012 Honda Accord"). Each entry gives one result row and at most one charge; repeats are checked once. 1-50 entries. Required.
- `maxMatches` (integer): How many recalls to list per query, newest first, e.g. 10 (default). match_count still gives the total found. Range 1-50; the price does not change.
- `sources` (array): Which sources to check, any of "cpsc", "nhtsa", "fda_food", "fda_drug", "fda_device", "eu_safety_gate", e.g. ["cpsc", "eu_safety_gate"]. Default (or empty) = all six. Each query only goes to the sources that fit it (VINs to NHTSA and EU Safety Gate). Same price for any number of sources.
- `euWeeks` (integer): How many of the latest weekly EU Safety Gate reports to search, e.g. 52 (default, about one year). Range 1-260 (five years); more weeks take longer. The US sources always cover their full history.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query` (string): The query as given (spaces tidied).
- `query_type` (string): How the query was read: text = product name, brand or model; upc = 8-14 digit barcode; vin = 17-character VIN (decoded with NHTSA vPIC); vehicle = year make model.
- `vehicle` (object | null): For vin and vehicle queries: {make, model, model_year} used for the NHTSA lookup; null otherwise.
- `recalled` (boolean | null): true = at least one recall or alert matched; false = no match in every source that applies; null = no match but a source could not be checked (see warnings).
- `match_count` (integer): Number of matching recalls found (only the newest maxMatches are in matches).
- `summary` (string): One sentence an agent can pass on: the newest match and its hazard, or 'No recall found' with the sources checked.
- `matches` (array): Matching recalls and alerts, newest first, at most maxMatches.
- `sources_checked` (array): Every source that applied to this query: {source, source_name, ok, matches, coverage}. ok false = not checked (see warnings). coverage says what was searched (e.g. the Safety Gate weeks).
- `warnings` (array): Sources that could not be checked (or NHTSA vPIC down for a VIN), in plain words. Rows with warnings are not charged.
- `input_error` (string | null): Why this query could not be checked, e.g. a VIN with a wrong check digit, with NHTSA vPIC's own error text and a valid example; null when the query was fine. Rows with an input_error are not charged.
- `source_url` (string | null): Official record of the newest match; null when nothing matched.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `attribution` (string): Source notices for the sources checked (CPSC credit, NHTSA, openFDA disclaimer, the EU Safety Gate acknowledgement).
- `checked_at` (string): When the check ran (ISO 8601, UTC).

### Example input

```json
{ "queries": ["Peloton Bike+", "3418178586009", "1HGCP2F31CA000000"], "maxMatches": 10 }
```

## HS Tariff Code & Duty Lookup API: US HTS and UK Tariff

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/tariff-lookup.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/tariff-lookup
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/tariff-lookup
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per lookup or search; HTTP API $0.005 per code lookup or code search (US or UK)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/tariff-lookup, $0.005 per code lookup or code search (US or UK) (max 1 code or 5 candidates)

Import duty for an HS-based tariff code, US Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) or UK commodity code: description hierarchy, general (MFN), special (preferential) and column 2 rates, US Chapter 99 references, UK VAT, source link. Or a product description in, 5 candidate codes out. No binding ruling.

Example questions:

- What US import duty applies to kids' bicycles (wheels under 63.5 cm) from Vietnam? Give the HTS code and cite the source.

### Input fields

- `code` (string): A US HTS code (8 or 10 digits, e.g. "8712.00.15" or "8712001510") or a UK commodity code (10 digits, e.g. "8712003010"). Dots and spaces are ignored. 4 or 6 digits (or a UK code that is not declarable) fail for free with a list of the codes under it. Empty = use `query` instead. Charged as one code-lookup.
- `query` (string): Plain product description, 2-200 characters, e.g. "bicycle" or "cotton t-shirt". Returns up to 5 candidate codes from the official tariff search (USITC or UK Trade Tariff), each with its rates. Candidates are not a classification: confirm them. Empty = use `code`. Charged as one code-search however many candidates come back.
- `market` (string): Which tariff to read: "US" (Harmonized Tariff Schedule, USITC) or "UK" (UK Global Tariff, HMRC; "GB" is the same). Empty = "US".
- `originCountry` (string): ISO 3166 alpha-2 code of the country the goods come from, e.g. "CN" or "DE". UK: preferential rates, additional duties and VAT are filtered to measures that apply to that country. US: preferential programs are filtered to ones named by that country code (plus USMCA for CA/MX), and column 2 and China Section 301 notes are added. Empty = all rates, unfiltered.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version, "1".
- `match_type` (string): "code" for a code lookup, "search_candidate" for a candidate returned by a description search.
- `query` (string | null): The product description searched for; null for a code lookup.
- `candidate_rank` (integer | null): 1-5 rank of a search candidate (US: ranked by Bosco Labs from the USITC hits; UK: the search's own relevance order); null for a code lookup.
- `market` (string): Importing market whose tariff was read.
- `code` (string): The commodity code, digits only (US 8 or 10, UK 10).
- `code_formatted` (string): The code as the source writes it (US 8712.00.15.10, UK 8712003010).
- `description` (string | null): Official description of this line, as published (often short, like "Other": read it with hierarchy).
- `hierarchy` (array): Official descriptions from the top (UK chapter, heading, ...; US heading level) down to this line: [{code, description}]. code is null for US sub-headers without a number.
- `declarable` (boolean | null): UK: true (only declarable codes are returned). US: null (not stated by the HTS data).
- `general_rate` (string | null): General / MFN duty rate as published: US column 1 General (e.g. "11%", "Free", "2.4¢/kg"); UK third-country duty for all origins (e.g. "14.00%", "£26.00 / 100 litre (hl)").
- `rate_line` (string | null): The line that carries general_rate (US 10-digit statistical lines inherit the rate of their 8-digit line).
- `column_2_rate` (string | null): US column 2 rate (goods of Cuba, North Korea, Belarus, Russia). null for UK.
- `special_rates_text` (string | null): US column 1 Special text as published, e.g. "Free (A+,AU,...) 5.5% (JP)". null for UK.
- `preferential_rates` (array): Preferential rates. US: [{rate, applies_to: [program codes]}] parsed from special_rates_text. UK: [{rate, applies_to: [area], measure_type, quota_order_number}] for tariff preferences and preferential quotas/suspensions (erga omnes and end-use suspensions are in temporary_reductions). Filtered when originCountry is given; UK without originCountry lists at most 10 (see preferential_rates_total).
- `preferential_rates_total` (integer): How many preferential rates apply before the 10-row cap (UK without originCountry); equals the list length otherwise.
- `additional_duties` (array): [{reference, type, rate, applies_to, additional_code, description}]. US: Chapter 99 references from footnotes and Chapter 99 lines whose text names this code (9903 additional duties; 9902 reductions are in temporary_reductions). UK: anti-dumping, countervailing, additional duties and excise measures, with additional codes (e.g. company-specific anti-dumping). rate null = depends on conditions; see source_url.
- `temporary_reductions` (array): [{reference, rate, description}]. US: HTS 9902 temporary duty reductions whose text names this code. UK: erga omnes and end-use suspensions and non-preferential quotas (reference = quota order number), the condition in description. Each applies only to the narrower goods or use it describes; check eligibility before using its rate.
- `vat` (array): UK VAT measures [{rate, additional_code, description}] (e.g. 20.00%, or 0.00% with additional code VATZ). Empty for US.
- `units` (array): Units of quantity: US units (e.g. "No.", "kg"); UK supplementary unit (e.g. "items (p/st)").
- `origin_country` (string | null): The originCountry used for filtering (ISO alpha-2), or null.
- `edition` (string | null): US HTS edition read (e.g. "2026 HTS Revision 22"); null for UK (the API serves today's tariff).
- `source_url` (string): Official page for this code (hts.usitc.gov search or trade-tariff.service.gov.uk commodity page).
- `provided_by` (string): "Bosco Labs (boscolabs.dev)".
- `api_url` (string): The official API call the data came from.
- `attribution` (string): Required source notice: USITC (U.S. Government work) or UK Open Government Licence v3.0 attribution.
- `warnings` (array): Limits that apply to this row, e.g. Chapter 99 measures not linked in the US data, UK import controls not listed, the candidate notice.
- `disclaimer` (string): Not a binding classification ruling; where to get one (CBP ruling, HMRC Advance Tariff Ruling).
- `as_of` (string): Date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) the tariff was read; rates are those in force at the source on that day.
- `retrieved_at` (string): ISO-8601 time of retrieval (UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): Seconds from start of the run to this row.

### Example input

```json
{ "code": "8712.00.15", "market": "US" }
```

## EU Tenders API (TED): public procurement & contract awards

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/eu-tenders.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/eu-tenders
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/eu-tenders
Price: Apify Store $0.002 per notice; HTTP API $0.002 per TED notice
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/eu-tenders, $0.002 per TED notice (max 200 notices (maxResults))

EU tenders and government procurement from TED, the EU's official tenders journal (EU/EEA, since 2016): open calls with deadlines, contract awards with winners and values. Filter by keyword, buyer country (e.g. Germany, Netherlands), CPV code, notice type, date, EUR value. No scraper to maintain.

Coverage: Every country that publishes on TED: the 27 EU member states, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, candidate countries and EU-funded procurement abroad; about 22,000 notices a week. History from November 2016 (complete from 2017). New notices are available the day they are published.

Example questions:

- Find open IT tenders above 1 million euros in Germany and the Netherlands from the last two weeks and list their deadlines.
- Which companies won construction contracts from Polish buyers last month, and for how much?
- Alert me to new cloud hosting tenders in the Nordics every morning.

### Input fields

- `keywords` (string): Full-text search over the whole notice, in any language; a notice matches when it contains all words, e.g. "cloud hosting". Empty = no keyword filter.
- `countries` (array): Buyer countries as ISO 3166 alpha-2 (DE, FR, NL, PL, ...) or alpha-3 (DEU) codes, e.g. ["DE", "NL"]. Alpha-3 works for any country, e.g. UKR. Empty = all countries.
- `cpvCodes` (array): Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code prefixes as digit strings; a prefix matches every code below it, e.g. ["72"] = IT services, "45" = construction work, "3312" = medical equipment, "72212000" = one specific code. Empty = all sectors.
- `noticeTypes` (array): Kinds of notices: contract_notice (open call for tenders), contract_award (who won, for how much), prior_information, direct_award_preannouncement, contract_modification, market_consultation. Default ["contract_notice"]. Pass [] for all kinds.
- `publishedFrom` (string): Earliest publication date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-10-01". The TED API covers notices from November 2016. Empty = 7 days before `publishedTo`.
- `publishedTo` (string): Latest publication date, YYYY-MM-DD. Empty = today. E.g. "2026-03-31".
- `minValueEur` (integer): Minimum total notice value in EUR, e.g. 1000000 (estimated value for calls, awarded value for awards). When set, notices stated in other currencies (e.g. PLN, SEK) and notices without a value are left out, as TED does not convert currencies. Empty = no minimum.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum notices, newest first, e.g. 100. Default 50. You pay per notice delivered.
- `onlyNewSinceLastRun` (boolean): true = skip (and don't charge for) notices an earlier run with the same filters already delivered. For scheduled runs. Default false. Remembered in a named key-value store in your account. E.g. `true` for a daily scheduled run.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `notice_id` (string): TED publication number, e.g. 760925-2026. Unique per notice.
- `notice_type` (string | null): contract_notice, contract_award, prior_information, direct_award_preannouncement, contract_modification or market_consultation (from TED's form type).
- `ted_notice_type` (string | null): TED's detailed notice type code, e.g. cn-standard, can-standard, pin-only, can-modif.
- `published` (string | null): Publication date in the Official Journal S (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `deadline` (string | null): Deadline for receipt of tenders (earliest over all lots), ISO date or date-time with UTC offset. Null when the notice has none (e.g. award notices).
- `title` (string | null): Notice title, English when TED provides it (TED's 'Country – CPV – title' form), else the original language.
- `title_language` (string | null): ISO 639 language code of title, e.g. eng.
- `description` (string | null): Short description of the procurement (max. 500 characters), English if available, else the original language. E-mail addresses and phone numbers are removed. Null for legacy (pre-eForms) notices.
- `description_language` (string | null): ISO 639 language code of description, e.g. deu.
- `buyer_name` (string | null): Name of the (first) buyer: the contracting authority or entity.
- `buyer_country` (string | null): Country of the buyer, ISO 3166 alpha-3 (e.g. DEU), as published by TED.
- `buyer_city` (string | null): City of the buyer.
- `cpv_codes` (array): All CPV codes of the notice (8 digits, no check digit), duplicates removed.
- `main_cpv` (string | null): Main CPV code of the procedure (eForms notices only).
- `estimated_value` (number | null): Estimated value of the procedure, excl. VAT, in currency. Not converted.
- `awarded_value` (number | null): Total value of the contracts awarded in this notice, excl. VAT, in currency (award notices).
- `currency` (string | null): ISO 4217 currency of awarded_value, or of estimated_value when there is no awarded value.
- `winner_names` (array | null): Names of the winning tenderers (award notices; usually companies).
- `procedure_type` (string | null): Procedure type as coded by TED, e.g. open, restricted. Null when not given.
- `lots_count` (integer | null): Number of lots (eForms notices only).
- `ted_url` (string): Notice page on ted.europa.eu.
- `source_url` (string): The notice page on ted.europa.eu (official XML: same path with /xml).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the notice was fetched from the TED API.

### Example input

```json
{
  "keywords": "software",
  "countries": ["DE", "NL", "FR"],
  "cpvCodes": ["72", "48"],
  "noticeTypes": ["contract_notice", "contract_award"],
  "publishedFrom": "2026-10-01",
  "minValueEur": 100000,
  "maxResults": 200
}
```

## Pentagon / DoD Contract Awards API: winners, amounts, tickers

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/dod-contract-awards.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/dod-contract-awards
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/dod-contract-awards
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per award row; HTTP API $0.005 per award row (USAspending history)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/dod-contract-awards, $0.005 per award row (USAspending history) (max 100 awards (maxResults))

Pentagon/DoD contract awards of $7.5M+ the same evening they are announced, plus USAspending.gov history since FY2008 (any federal agency). Winner, amount, service, NAICS/PSC, matched to a US stock ticker with SEC shares outstanding. Filter by date, agency, amount, company, ticker.

Coverage: Same evening: the Pentagon's daily contract list (weekdays, rows in by about 7 p.m. New York). History: the USAspending.gov API from 2007-10-01, for the Department of Defense or any other federal agency. DoD contract actions reach USAspending up to 90 days after signing, so the default window is the last 135 days.

Example questions:

- Which Kratos contracts did the Pentagon award in 2019, and how large were they?
- Who won the largest Navy shipbuilding contracts (NAICS 336611) in 2025?
- Show Department of Homeland Security contracts over $10 million signed in the first half of 2026.

### Input fields

- `source` (string): "both" (default) = the Pentagon's same-evening contract list (published around 5 p.m. New York on the signing day, face values, DoD only) plus the USAspending history (obligations, ~3 months behind for DoD). "dailyList" = only the same-evening list rows. "history" = only USAspending. The list has no NAICS/PSC codes, so it is skipped when naicsCodes or pscCodes are set, and when agencies excludes the Department of Defense.
- `dateFrom` (string): Earliest action (signing) date, or announcement date for same-evening list rows, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2019-01-01". History from 2007-10-01 (FY2008). Empty = 135 days before `dateTo`, because DoD data is published up to 90 days late (about 105 days observed).
- `dateTo` (string): Latest action (signing) date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2019-12-31". Empty = today. The last ~3 months of DoD data are incomplete.
- `agencies` (array): Top-tier awarding agency names as USAspending spells them, e.g. ["Department of Defense"], ["Department of Homeland Security"], ["National Aeronautics and Space Administration"]. Default ["Department of Defense"]. Pass [] for ALL federal agencies.
- `minAmountUsd` (integer): Minimum summed obligations per award and day, in USD, e.g. 1000000. Default 7500000, the DoD's public announcement threshold (the daily 5 p.m. contracts list). 0 = every award-day except net de-obligations (negative sums).
- `recipients` (array): Winning company search terms, matched by USAspending against recipient and parent names, e.g. ["kratos", "huntington ingalls"]. Empty = all recipients.
- `tickers` (array): Only awards matched to these US-listed tickers (NYSE, Nasdaq, CBOE), e.g. ["LMT", "KTOS", "AVAV"]. Turns ticker matching on. Empty = no ticker filter.
- `naicsCodes` (array): NAICS industry codes, 2 to 6 digits, e.g. ["336414"] (guided missiles and space vehicles) or ["3364"]. Empty = all.
- `pscCodes` (array): Product and Service Codes, e.g. ["1410"] (guided missiles), ["R425"] (engineering support). Empty = all.
- `matchTickers` (boolean): true (default) = match the recipient or its parent company to a US-listed ticker by exact cleaned name (SEC company list) and add the SEC-reported shares outstanding. Unmatched awards are still returned, with ticker = null. E.g. `false` to skip the ticker match.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum award rows, newest signing dates first, then largest amounts, e.g. 20. Default 100. Each row is one charged event.
- `onlyNewSinceLastRun` (boolean): true = skip (and don't charge for) award-days (including old-dated actions the DoD publishes late) an earlier run with the same filters already delivered. For scheduled runs. Default false. Remembered in a named key-value store in your account. E.g. `true` for a daily scheduled run.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `source` (string): Where the row comes from: "usaspending" (obligation records, ~3 months late for DoD) or "dod_daily_list" (the Pentagon's same-evening contract list, parsed by AI with checks). The two are separate records of an award and are never summed or deduped.
- `award_id` (string | null): Contract PIID (USAspending 'Award ID'); for daily-list rows the contract number in the text, null when none is stated.
- `parent_award_id` (string | null): PIID of the parent IDV (IDIQ, BPA, GSA schedule) for task and delivery orders; null for standalone contracts.
- `award_key` (string): USAspending generated_internal_id: unique award key (PIID + agency + parent IDV).
- `action_date` (string): Signing (action) date, YYYY-MM-DD; for daily-list rows the announcement date.
- `amount_usd` (number): USAspending rows: obligated amount in USD, that day's actions on this award summed (modifications can be negative). Daily-list rows: the amount as stated (see amount_basis); for a multiple-award contract the full shared ceiling on every awardee's row (see shared_award).
- `is_ceiling` (boolean): True when amount_usd is a ceiling, not money committed (amount_basis is "ceiling"): an IDIQ maximum or a multiple-award ceiling. Kept for compatibility; use amount_basis and shared_award. Only daily-list rows can be true.
- `contract_number` (string | null): Contract number (PIID) as stated: for USAspending rows the same as award_id; for daily-list rows the number in the announcement paragraph, null when that paragraph states none.
- `award_kind` (string | null): What kind of award the row is. Daily list: from the announcement wording ("has been awarded a ... contract" = new_contract, "modification (P00012) to previously awarded contract" = modification, "exercises an option" = option_exercise, "task order", "delivery order" or an order under an ordering agreement, "multiple award" or "will compete for each order" = multiple_award_idiq, "single award" = single_award_idiq; an IDIQ that says neither is new_contract), kept only when such a keyword is in the paragraph. USAspending: award type A BPA CALL = bpa_call, B PURCHASE ORDER = new_contract, C DELIVERY ORDER = delivery_order (FPDS files task orders as delivery orders), D DEFINITIVE CONTRACT = new_contract; a day without the base award is option_exercise (action type G) or modification. Null when unknown.
- `pricing_type` (string | null): Contract pricing from the announcement wording ("firm-fixed-price", "cost-plus-fixed-fee", ...; hybrid = two or more named). Daily-list rows only; null for USAspending rows (the transaction search does not return it) and when the text names none.
- `amount_basis` (string | null): What amount_usd measures: ceiling (a maximum or multiple-award ceiling, not money committed; shared when shared_award is true), face_value (a definitive contract's or order's value), modification_value (the value of a modification), obligated (money obligated: every USAspending row), estimated. Null when the text does not say.
- `obligated_at_award_usd` (number | null): Daily list: the amount the announcement says is obligated at the time of award (0 for "no funds are obligated"), only when that figure is in a sentence about obligation; else null. USAspending: the obligated amount (same as amount_usd).
- `shared_award` (boolean | null): True when several companies share this one amount (a multiple-award contract: every awardee gets a row with the full ceiling). Never sum amount_usd over such rows: count each award_group_id once. False for USAspending rows; null for daily-list days read before schema 2.
- `awardees_count` (integer | null): Number of companies sharing this award_group_id (1 = not shared).
- `award_group_id` (string | null): Stable id shared by all rows of one award: daily list = one announcement paragraph and amount; USAspending = one award and signing day. To total money without double counting, take amount_usd once per award_group_id.
- `co_awardees` (array | null): The other companies in the same award_group_id (at most 20); empty when not shared.
- `completion_date` (string | null): Estimated completion date stated in the announcement, YYYY-MM-DD (a month alone: its last day); null when not stated and for USAspending rows.
- `classification_evidence` (string | null): The words that support award_kind, pricing_type and amount_basis, e.g. "multiple award; firm-fixed-price; maximum" (daily list) or "award type DELIVERY ORDER" (USAspending).
- `action_count` (integer): Number of contract actions summed into this row.
- `modification_numbers` (array): Modification numbers of those actions ('0' = the base award).
- `new_award` (boolean): True when the day includes the base award (modification 0), false for modifications only.
- `award_type` (string | null): DEFINITIVE CONTRACT, DELIVERY ORDER, PURCHASE ORDER or BPA CALL.
- `awarding_agency` (string | null): Top-tier awarding agency, e.g. Department of Defense.
- `awarding_sub_agency` (string | null): Awarding sub-agency, e.g. Department of the Navy, Department of the Army, Department of the Air Force, Defense Logistics Agency, Missile Defense Agency.
- `recipient_name` (string | null): Contractor (recipient) name as reported.
- `recipient_uei` (string | null): Recipient Unique Entity ID (SAM.gov).
- `parent_name` (string | null): Parent company name from the USAspending award record.
- `parent_uei` (string | null): Parent company UEI.
- `recipient_city` (string | null): Recipient city.
- `recipient_state` (string | null): Recipient state code (daily-list rows: the state as written, e.g. Virginia).
- `recipient_country` (string | null): Recipient country.
- `performance_state` (string | null): Place of performance state code.
- `performance_country` (string | null): Place of performance country.
- `naics_code` (string | null): NAICS industry code.
- `naics_description` (string | null): NAICS description.
- `psc_code` (string | null): Product and Service Code.
- `psc_description` (string | null): PSC description.
- `description` (string | null): Description of the day's largest action (max 300 characters).
- `ticker` (string | null): US-listed ticker (NYSE, Nasdaq, CBOE) of the recipient or its parent, by exact cleaned-name match; null when not matched.
- `matched_on` (string | null): Which name matched the ticker: the recipient itself or its parent company.
- `sec_cik` (integer | null): SEC Central Index Key of the matched company.
- `sec_company_name` (string | null): Company name in SEC's ticker list.
- `exchange` (string | null): Exchange of the ticker in SEC's list.
- `shares_outstanding` (integer | null): Shares outstanding from the SEC cover page (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding), the count of the action date (latest on or before it, else the earliest). Multiply by your own price for a market cap.
- `shares_as_of` (string | null): Date of that share count, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `usaspending_url` (string): Award page on USAspending.gov.
- `source_url` (string | null): USAspending API record of the award; for daily-list rows the war.gov article, null when the e-mail did not link it.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `data_lag_note` (string): Reporting lag of the source: DoD actions appear up to 90 days after signing.
- `retrieved_at` (string): UTC time the row was built.

### Example input

```json
{
  "dateFrom": "2019-01-01",
  "dateTo": "2019-12-31",
  "tickers": ["KTOS"],
  "maxResults": 1000
}
```

## US Federal Awards API: contracts & grants, all agencies

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/us-federal-awards.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/us-federal-awards
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/us-federal-awards
Price: Apify Store $0.004 per award row; HTTP API $0.004 per award row
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/us-federal-awards, $0.004 per award row (max 100 awards (maxResults))

US federal contract, grant and loan awards from every agency (USAspending.gov): winner, UEI, parent company, stock ticker, agency, amounts, dates, NAICS/PSC/assistance listing, place of performance and a source link. Filter by company, ticker, agency, keyword, state, date.

Example questions:

- Which federal contracts did Palantir win this quarter?
- Largest NASA contracts last month
- Grants to universities in Texas for AI this year

### Input fields

- `recipients` (array): Winning organisations, as name text or 12-character SAM UEI, e.g. ["palantir"], ["university of texas"] or ["FSY4LVSBGWB7"]. USAspending matches the text against recipient and parent company names and UEIs. Empty (default) = all recipients.
- `tickers` (array): Only awards whose recipient or its parent company matches these US-listed tickers (NYSE, Nasdaq, CBOE; exact cleaned SEC company name), e.g. ["PLTR"] or ["LMT", "BAH"]. Subsidiaries are found through their parent company. Empty (default) = no ticker filter; every row still gets a ticker when its name matches.
- `agencies` (array): Awarding agencies by abbreviation, name or toptier code, e.g. ["NASA"], ["Department of Energy"], ["097"] (DoD). A name that is not a top-tier agency is searched as a sub-agency, e.g. ["Defense Logistics Agency"]. Empty (default) = all federal agencies.
- `awardTypes` (array): Which awards: "contracts" (USAspending codes A-D: BPA calls, purchase orders, delivery orders, definitive contracts), "grants" (02-05: block, formula, project grants, cooperative agreements), "loans" (07, 08), "direct_payments" (06, 10), "other" (09, 11: insurance, other assistance). E.g. ["grants"]. Default ["contracts"].
- `keywords` (array): Full-text search over award descriptions and other text fields, e.g. ["artificial intelligence"] or ["cybersecurity"]. Several keywords = any of them. Empty (default) = no keyword filter.
- `naicsCodes` (array): NAICS industry codes, 2 to 6 digits, e.g. ["541512"] (computer systems design) or ["3364"]. Contracts only. Empty (default) = all.
- `pscCodes` (array): Product and Service Codes, e.g. ["DA01"] (IT software development) or ["AR"] (space R&D). Contracts only. Empty (default) = all.
- `cfdaNumbers` (array): Assistance listing (CFDA) numbers as NN.NNN, e.g. ["47.070"] (NSF computer and information science) or ["93.855"] (NIH allergy and infectious diseases). Financial assistance only. Empty (default) = all.
- `placeOfPerformanceStates` (array): Two-letter US state or territory codes where the work is done, e.g. ["TX"] or ["VA", "MD", "DC"]. Empty (default) = anywhere, including abroad.
- `dateFrom` (string): Earliest action date (signing date of the award or of a modification), YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-07-01". Searchable from 2007-10-01. Empty (default) = 30 days before dateTo. DoD contracts appear up to 90 days late.
- `dateTo` (string): Latest action date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-09-30". Empty (default) = today.
- `minAmount` (integer): Only awards whose total obligated amount (all actions since signing) is at least this many US dollars, e.g. 1000000. Empty or 0 (default) = no minimum.
- `sortBy` (string): "amount" (default) = awards ordered by their largest action (obligation) in the date window, largest first; that action is the one shown. "date" = ordered by their latest action in the window, newest first. Loans-only searches rank by loan face value.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum award rows, one per award, e.g. 20. Default 20, maximum 1000. Each row is one charged event.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `award_id` (string | null): Award identifier as USAspending shows it: contract PIID, or FAIN/URI for financial assistance.
- `award_key` (string): USAspending generated_internal_id: the unique award key, also used in source_url.
- `award_type_group` (string | null): contracts, grants, loans, direct_payments or other (from the USAspending award type code).
- `award_type` (string | null): Award type as USAspending describes it, e.g. DEFINITIVE CONTRACT, DELIVERY ORDER, PROJECT GRANT (B), COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT (B).
- `award_type_code` (string | null): USAspending award type code, e.g. D (definitive contract), C (delivery order), 04 (project grant), 05 (cooperative agreement), 07 (direct loan).
- `parent_award_id` (string | null): PIID of the parent IDV (IDIQ, BPA, GSA schedule) for task and delivery orders; null otherwise.
- `recipient_name` (string | null): Recipient (winner) name as published by USAspending.
- `recipient_uei` (string | null): Recipient's SAM.gov Unique Entity ID (12 characters).
- `parent_name` (string | null): Parent company of the recipient, from the USAspending award record.
- `parent_uei` (string | null): Parent company's UEI.
- `recipient_city` (string | null): Recipient's city.
- `recipient_state` (string | null): Recipient's US state code.
- `recipient_country` (string | null): Recipient's country.
- `ticker` (string | null): US stock ticker (NYSE/Nasdaq/CBOE) when the recipient or parent name exactly matches an SEC-listed company after cleaning; null otherwise. Derived by Bosco Labs, not by USAspending.
- `matched_on` (string | null): "recipient" or "parent": which name matched the ticker; null when no ticker.
- `awarding_agency` (string | null): Top-tier awarding agency, e.g. National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
- `awarding_sub_agency` (string | null): Awarding sub-agency, e.g. Department of the Navy, National Institutes of Health.
- `funding_agency` (string | null): Top-tier funding agency (can differ from the awarding agency).
- `action_date` (string | null): Date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the award's action shown in this row: its largest action in the date window (sortBy amount) or its latest (sortBy date).
- `action_amount_usd` (number | null): Federal obligation of that action in USD (negative = de-obligation; 0 for administrative modifications and loans).
- `is_admin_change` (boolean | null): True for a $0 action: an administrative change to an existing award, not new money. Null for loans.
- `modification_number` (string | null): Modification number of that action ("0" or empty = the base award).
- `total_obligated_usd` (number | null): Total obligated on the award so far, all actions since signing, in USD.
- `total_value_usd` (number | null): Contracts: potential total value including all options (base_and_all_options), USD. Loans: loan face value. Null for other assistance.
- `award_date_signed` (string | null): Date the award was first signed (base award), YYYY-MM-DD. Earlier than dateFrom = the row is a modification of an older award.
- `start_date` (string | null): Period of performance start, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `end_date` (string | null): Period of performance current end, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `description` (string | null): Award description, cut at 300 characters.
- `naics_code` (string | null): NAICS industry code (contracts).
- `naics_description` (string | null): NAICS industry title.
- `psc_code` (string | null): Product and Service Code (contracts).
- `psc_description` (string | null): Product and Service Code title.
- `cfda_number` (string | null): Assistance listing (CFDA) number (financial assistance), e.g. 47.070.
- `cfda_title` (string | null): Assistance listing title.
- `performance_city` (string | null): Place of performance city.
- `performance_state` (string | null): Place of performance US state code.
- `performance_country` (string | null): Place of performance country.
- `source_url` (string): The award's page on usaspending.gov (the source to cite).
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `api_url` (string): The award record in the USAspending API (JSON).
- `retrieved_at` (string): When this row was retrieved, ISO-8601 UTC.

### Example input

```json
{
  "agencies": ["NASA"],
  "awardTypes": ["contracts"],
  "dateFrom": "2026-10-01",
  "dateTo": "2026-10-31",
  "maxResults": 20
}
```

## ECB Rates & Euro Inflation API: policy rates, FX, €STR, HICP

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/eu-rates-inflation.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/eu-rates-inflation
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/eu-rates-inflation
Price: Apify Store $0.002 per series returned; HTTP API $0.002 per series returned (catalogue free)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/eu-rates-inflation, $0.002 per series returned (catalogue free) (max 20 series)

Latest value, previous value, change and recent history of ECB policy rates, euro reference FX rates, €STR, euro-area and national bond yields, and Eurostat HICP inflation. Ask by plain name (ecb_deposit_rate, eur_fx:USD, hicp:NL), no SDMX keys. Official data, a source link per series.

Example questions:

- What's the ECB deposit rate now, when did it last change, and how does euro-area inflation compare? Cite the source.

### Input fields

- `series` (array): Which series to fetch, by plain name (case-insensitive), up to 20 per run, e.g. ["ecb_deposit_rate", "eur_fx:USD", "hicp:EA"]. Names: ecb_deposit_rate, ecb_main_refi_rate, ecb_marginal_lending_rate (one observation per rate change), estr (€STR), eur_fx:<CUR> (ECB reference rate, CUR per 1 EUR, e.g. eur_fx:GBP), euro_area_yield_curve:<maturity> (AAA spot yield, e.g. 10Y, 3M, 1Y6M; add :all for all government bonds), gov_bond_10y:<country> (monthly average 10-year yield, about 6 weeks behind, e.g. gov_bond_10y:IT), hicp:<geo>[:<variant>] (Eurostat inflation; geo EA, EU or NL, DE, ...; variant annual (default), monthly, index, core, energy, food, services, goods, or an ECOICOP 2 code like CP01). An unknown name fails at once with suggestions and costs nothing. Empty (with no rawSeriesKey) = list the catalogue for free.
- `last` (integer): How many of the newest observations to return per series, e.g. 12 (the last 12 months of a monthly series). Empty = 12, or with dateFrom every observation in the window (up to 1000). latest_value, previous_value and change are always filled. The price is the same for any number.
- `dateFrom` (string): First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-01-01". For monthly series the month holding the date counts. Empty = no lower bound (only `last` limits).
- `dateTo` (string): Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-03-15". With last = 1 you get the value on that date or the last one before it (weekends and holidays have no FX value). Empty = up to the latest published value.
- `frequency` (string): Only where the source has it: eur_fx daily (default), monthly or annual averages; policy rates daily (rate on every day) instead of the default one-row-per-change. Other series keep their own frequency and say so in `warnings`. Empty = each series' default.
- `rawSeriesKey` (array): Optional full ECB Data Portal series keys (dataflow + key, every dimension filled, no wildcards), e.g. ["EXR.M.CHF.EUR.SP00.E"]. Same output and price as named series. Empty = none.
- `mode` (string): "series" (default) fetches the series above. "catalogue" returns one row per supported name pattern with its source dataset, key template, frequencies, unit and an example, free of charge.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version, "1".
- `series` (string): The series as requested, normalised (e.g. eur_fx:USD, hicp:NL:core), or the raw ECB key.
- `title` (string | null): The series title exactly as the source states it (ECB TITLE; Eurostat dataset, category, area and unit labels). null on error rows.
- `description` (string): What the series is and how to read it, in plain words (written by Bosco Labs).
- `source` (string): Publisher of the values.
- `dataset` (string): Source dataset: ECB dataflow (FM, EST, EXR, YC, IRS, ...) or Eurostat dataset code (prc_hicp_minr).
- `series_key` (string): Exact series identifier at the source: ECB dataflow.key (e.g. EXR.D.USD.EUR.SP00.A) or Eurostat dataset/freq.unit.coicop18.geo.
- `frequency` (string | null): changes (one observation per policy-rate change), daily, monthly, quarterly or annual.
- `unit` (string | null): Unit of the values, e.g. percent per annum, USD per 1 EUR, annual rate of change, %.
- `latest_date` (string | null): Date of the newest observation: YYYY-MM-DD (daily, change dates), YYYY-MM (monthly), YYYY (annual). For policy rates: the day the current rate took effect.
- `latest_value` (number | null): Newest value, unmodified from the source.
- `previous_date` (string | null): Date of the observation before the newest one (for policy rates: the previous change).
- `previous_value` (number | null): Value of that previous observation, unmodified.
- `change` (number | null): latest_value - previous_value, computed by Bosco Labs (exact decimal difference); not an official ECB or Eurostat figure.
- `observations` (array): The newest `last` observations, oldest first, each {date, value, status}. status is the source's observation flag, null when normal (ECB: P provisional, E estimated; Eurostat: e estimated, p provisional, b break in series).
- `observation_count` (integer): Number of entries in observations.
- `source_url` (string | null): Human-readable page of the series: ECB Data Portal series page or Eurostat data browser table.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `api_url` (string | null): The exact API request the values came from (re-run it to verify).
- `attribution` (string): Required source credit: names the source, says the values are unmodified and available free of charge from it, and marks `change` as computed by Bosco Labs. Keep it when you republish the values.
- `warnings` (array): Caveats in plain words, e.g. a requested frequency the series doesn't have, or a window cut to the newest 1000 observations.
- `error` (string | null): Why this series has no data (unknown currency, area or category, empty date window, source down), with valid examples. Rows with an error are not charged.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the data was fetched (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): How long fetching all series took.

### Example input

```json
{ "series": ["ecb_deposit_rate", "eur_fx:USD", "hicp:EA"] }
```

## ClinicalTrials.gov API: trial search & NCT dossier

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/clinical-trials.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/clinical-trials
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/clinical-trials
Price: Apify Store $0.004 per trial; HTTP API $0.004 per trial
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/clinical-trials, $0.004 per trial (max 100 trials (maxResults) or 100 NCT numbers)

Clinical trials as compact JSON rows: status, phase, sponsor, conditions, interventions, enrollment, start and primary completion dates, countries, outcomes and results. Look up NCT numbers or search by condition, drug, sponsor, phase, status, country and dates. Sourced, no contact data.

Example questions:

- What is the status and primary completion date of NCT05813925? Cite the ClinicalTrials.gov record.

### Input fields

- `nctIds` (array): ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers to look up, NCT + 8 digits, e.g. ["NCT05813925"]. Up to 100, in one API call; one row per trial found, in the order given. When set, all search filters below are ignored. Empty = search mode.
- `condition` (string): Condition or disease to search for, e.g. "obesity" or "non-small cell lung cancer". Matches ClinicalTrials.gov's condition field including its synonyms; supports OR/AND, e.g. "obesity OR overweight". Empty = any condition.
- `intervention` (string): Drug, biologic, device or procedure name, e.g. "semaglutide" or "semaglutide OR tirzepatide". Use molecule or brand names; a drug class like "GLP-1" only matches trials that write it. Empty = any intervention.
- `sponsor` (string): Lead sponsor organisation, e.g. "Novo Nordisk" (matches "Novo Nordisk A/S"). Searches the lead sponsor only, not collaborators. Empty = any sponsor.
- `phase` (array): Trial phases to include, any of EARLY_PHASE1, PHASE1, PHASE2, PHASE3, PHASE4, NA, e.g. ["PHASE3"]. A phase 2/3 trial matches both PHASE2 and PHASE3. Empty = all phases (observational studies have none).
- `status` (array): Overall recruitment status of the trial, e.g. ["RECRUITING", "NOT_YET_RECRUITING"]. UNKNOWN = status not verified for over 2 years. Empty = any status.
- `locationCountries` (array): Trials with at least one site in any of these countries, e.g. ["Germany", "DK"] or ["Europe"]. Accepts country names as ClinicalTrials.gov writes them ("United States", "South Korea", "Czechia"), common ISO alpha-2 codes, and the regions "Europe" (45 European countries incl. UK, Switzerland, Norway, Ukraine) and "EU" (27 member states). Empty = anywhere.
- `startDateFrom` (string): Earliest trial start date (actual or planned), YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY, e.g. "2025-01-01". Inclusive. Empty = no lower bound.
- `startDateTo` (string): Latest trial start date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2025-12-31". Inclusive. Empty = no upper bound (includes planned future starts).
- `primaryCompletionFrom` (string): Earliest primary completion date (actual or estimated: when the primary endpoint data are complete, the usual read-out catalyst), YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-01-01". Empty = no lower bound.
- `primaryCompletionTo` (string): Latest primary completion date, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-12-31". Empty = no upper bound.
- `hasResults` (boolean): true = only trials with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; false = only trials without. Leave empty (omit) for both. E.g. `true`.
- `maxResults` (integer): Maximum number of trials (rows) to return in search mode, e.g. 20. Default 20, maximum 500. Each row is one charged `trial` event, so this also caps the cost. Ranked by relevance when a condition or intervention is given, else newest start date first.
- `detail` (string): "summary" (default): the compact dossier. "full" also fills eligibility (criteria up to 4,000 characters, sex, ages), arms (up to 20), secondary outcomes (up to 15) and sites (facility, city, country, status; up to 100). Same price.

### Output fields

- `nct_id` (string | null): ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, e.g. NCT05813925.
- `title` (string | null): Brief title.
- `acronym` (string | null): Study acronym, e.g. REDEFINE 5.
- `status` (string | null): Overall recruitment status, e.g. RECRUITING, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, COMPLETED, TERMINATED, UNKNOWN.
- `phases` (array | null): Phases, e.g. ["PHASE3"] or ["PHASE2", "PHASE3"] for a phase 2/3 trial; empty for observational studies.
- `study_type` (string | null): INTERVENTIONAL, OBSERVATIONAL or EXPANDED_ACCESS.
- `conditions` (array | null): Conditions or diseases studied, as registered.
- `interventions` (array | null): Interventions: type (DRUG, BIOLOGICAL, DEVICE, PROCEDURE, BEHAVIORAL, ...) and name.
- `sponsor` (string | null): Lead sponsor organisation; null when the record lists a private individual as sponsor (class INDIV).
- `sponsor_class` (string | null): Lead sponsor class: INDUSTRY, NIH, FED, OTHER_GOV, NETWORK, OTHER (e.g. universities), ...
- `collaborators` (array | null): Collaborating organisations (individuals, class INDIV, left out).
- `enrollment_count` (integer | null): Number of participants (actual or planned, see enrollment_type).
- `enrollment_type` (string | null): ACTUAL or ESTIMATED.
- `start_date` (string | null): Study start date, ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is registered).
- `start_date_type` (string | null): ACTUAL or ESTIMATED; null when not stated.
- `primary_completion_date` (string | null): Primary completion date (last participant's primary endpoint data collected), ISO 8601, may be YYYY-MM.
- `primary_completion_date_type` (string | null): ACTUAL or ESTIMATED.
- `completion_date` (string | null): Study completion date, ISO 8601, may be YYYY-MM.
- `completion_date_type` (string | null): ACTUAL or ESTIMATED.
- `last_update_posted` (string | null): Date the record was last updated on ClinicalTrials.gov (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `countries` (array | null): Countries with at least one listed site, sorted.
- `site_count` (integer | null): Number of sites (locations) listed in the record.
- `primary_outcomes` (array | null): Primary outcome measures (up to 5; see primary_outcomes_total).
- `primary_outcomes_total` (integer | null): Number of primary outcomes registered.
- `has_results` (boolean | null): true if results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
- `results_first_posted` (string | null): Date results were first posted (YYYY-MM-DD), null if none.
- `brief_summary` (string | null): Brief summary, up to 1,000 characters (cut texts end with [truncated]); contact details removed.
- `eligibility` (object | null): detail=full only (null in summary): eligibility criteria.
- `arms` (array | null): detail=full only (null in summary): arms/groups, up to 20.
- `secondary_outcomes` (array | null): detail=full only (null in summary): secondary outcome measures, up to 15.
- `sites` (array | null): detail=full only (null in summary): study sites, up to 100. Organisation-level only: no contact persons, emails or phones.
- `source_url` (string | null): The trial's page on ClinicalTrials.gov.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `data_processed_at` (string | null): When ClinicalTrials.gov last processed (posted) its dataset, from its /api/v2/version endpoint (dataTimestamp, no time zone given); null if that endpoint was unavailable.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When this Actor retrieved the record (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `attribution` (string): Required credit: source ClinicalTrials.gov, processing and retrieval dates, and the modifications made.
- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.

### Example input

```json
{ "nctIds": ["NCT05813925", "NCT04368728"] }
```

## Drug Safety API: FDA adverse events, label, recalls, EMA status

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/drug-safety.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/drug-safety
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/drug-safety
Price: Apify Store $0.02 per dossier or $0.004 per single-section query; HTTP API $0.004 per sub-query; a full dossier = 5 units ($0.02); partial answers are free
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/drug-safety, $0.004 per sub-query; a full dossier = 5 units ($0.02); partial answers are free (max 1 drug)

Drug safety dossier for one drug name as one sourced JSON row: FDA adverse events (top FAERS reaction counts), boxed warning, indications, US recalls and shortages (openFDA), EU authorisation, EPAR and EU shortages (EMA). Dossier (default) $0.02 = 5 queries; one section $0.004. Not medical advice.

Example questions:

- Does semaglutide have a boxed warning, what are its most reported adverse reactions, and is it authorised in the EU? Cite the sources.

### Input fields

- `drug` (string, required): One drug: generic name, active ingredient or brand, e.g. "semaglutide", "metformin" or "Ozempic". Case does not matter. Brand names are resolved to the active ingredient for FAERS, recalls, shortages and EMA. An unknown or misspelled name fails in seconds with close names to try (nothing charged). Required.
- `mode` (string): "dossier" (default) fills all five sections in one call and costs $0.02 (one `dossier` event; on the API 5 drug-queries of $0.004). The other values fill one section only and cost one `drug-query` event ($0.004): "label", "adverse_events_top", "recalls", "shortages" or "eu_status". Sections not asked for are null. Empty = dossier.
- `maxItems` (integer): Cap on each list in the row: top FAERS reactions, recalls (newest first), US shortage records, EU products and EU shortages, e.g. 10. Default 10, maximum 50. Totals are always reported in full. Does not change the price.

### Output fields

- `query` (string): The drug name as given (whitespace normalised).
- `mode` (string): dossier, label, adverse_events_top, recalls, shortages or eu_status.
- `drug` (object): How the name was resolved.
- `label` (object | null): FDA label (openFDA drug/label): the newest label for the drug, prescription labels first. null when not asked for, when no FDA label exists (see warnings) or when openFDA failed.
- `adverse_events` (object | null): FAERS adverse event reports (openFDA drug/event) as COUNTS only, never individual case records. Reports that list the drug as suspect or concomitant; voluntary, unverified, not incidence, causality not established. null when not asked for or openFDA failed.
- `recalls` (object | null): US drug recalls (openFDA drug/enforcement, FDA enforcement reports since 2004) whose generic name or product description names search_term; newest first. Includes compounded products. null when not asked for or openFDA failed.
- `shortages` (object | null): US drug shortages (openFDA drug/shortages, FDA Drug Shortage list), one record per package; current first, then newest. null when not asked for or openFDA failed.
- `eu_status` (object | null): EU status from the European Medicines Agency's medicines and shortages data files (centrally authorised human medicines only; nationally authorised products are not listed). null when not asked for or EMA failed.
- `failed_sections` (array): Sections asked for whose source failed (null in the row, reason in warnings), e.g. ["eu_status"]. Not empty = partial answer, which is not charged; run again for the full one. [] when complete.
- `warnings` (array): Why a section is null or partial, e.g. "EMA: ... unavailable" or "label: no FDA label found ..."; [] when all fine.
- `notice` (string): Not medical advice, and how to read FAERS counts.
- `attribution` (string): Credits FDA/openFDA and acknowledges EMA as the source (with access month), plus Bosco Labs' changes. Keep it with any copy.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the sources were queried, ISO 8601 UTC.
- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version, "1".
- `provided_by` (string): "Bosco Labs (boscolabs.dev)".

### Example input

```json
{ "drug": "semaglutide" }
```

## Dutch Address Lookup API: BAG postcode, geocode & building data

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/dutch-address-lookup.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/dutch-address-lookup
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/dutch-address-lookup
Price: Apify Store $0.002 per resolved address; HTTP API $0.002 per address resolved (unresolved inputs are free)
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/dutch-address-lookup, $0.002 per address resolved (unresolved inputs are free) (max 50 addresses/BAG ids or 1 postcode (100 addresses))

Validates and geocodes Dutch addresses against the official BAG register (via PDOK): postcode, BAG ids, WGS84 + RD coordinates, construction year, use, floor area and building status. Free text, postcode + house number (or range) or BAG ids; up to 100 per run. Unmatched inputs are free.

Example questions:

- Is 'Damrak 1 Amsterdam' a valid address? Give me its postcode, building year, use and floor area, with the source.

### Input fields

- `addresses` (array): Dutch addresses to check and geocode, one per line, as people write them: street + house number (+ letter or addition) + city, and/or postcode + house number, e.g. "Damrak 1 Amsterdam", "Dam 5B Amsterdam", "Damrak 18-1 Amsterdam", "Coolsingel 40, 3011AD Rotterdam", "1012LG 1". Up to 100 (together with bagIds); repeats are looked up once. One output row per address. Empty = use postcode or bagIds.
- `postcode` (string): A Dutch postcode, 4 digits + 2 letters, e.g. "1012JS" or "1012 JS". Alone it lists every address in that postcode (one row each, up to 100); with houseNumber it returns that address, with houseNumber + houseNumberTo every address in that range. Empty = not used.
- `houseNumber` (integer): House number within `postcode`, e.g. 1. Only used with postcode. Empty = all numbers in the postcode.
- `houseNumberTo` (integer): Last house number of a range starting at houseNumber, inclusive, e.g. 20 for 1-20. Needs postcode and houseNumber. Empty = only houseNumber.
- `houseNumberAddition` (string): House letter and/or addition for a single houseNumber, e.g. "B" (5B), "1" (18-1), "H" (8-H), "A2" (1A-2). Empty = all units at that number (one row each).
- `bagIds` (array): 16-digit BAG identifiers: nummeraanduiding (address, e.g. "0363200012113669"), verblijfsobject (unit, "0363010012111931"), ligplaats/standplaats (berth/pitch) or pand (building, "0363100012185508": building details only, no address). Up to 100 together with addresses. Empty = not used.
- `include` (array): Which sections to fill: any of "address" (street, postcode, city, municipality, province), "building" (construction year, use purposes, floor area, status, units in the building), "coordinates" (WGS84 + RD New), e.g. ["address", "coordinates"]. BAG ids are always returned. Default (or empty) = all three. Without "building" the run is faster; the price is the same.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `input` (string): The input as given: a free-text address, 'POSTCODE number(-to) addition' for postcode queries, or a BAG id.
- `input_type` (string): Which input this row answers: address (free text), postcode, or bag_id.
- `resolved` (boolean): true = one BAG address (or, for a pand id, one building) was found; only these rows are charged.
- `match_quality` (string): exact: every part of the input agrees with the BAG; probable: one address fits but part of the input differs or is missing (see warnings); ambiguous: several addresses fit (see candidates); not_found: no BAG address fits; invalid_input: not a valid BAG id; source_error: PDOK did not answer.
- `match_score` (number | null): PDOK Locatieserver relevance score for free-text matches (relative within one query, higher is better); null for postcode and BAG id lookups.
- `address` (object | null): The normalised BAG address. null when not resolved or 'address' is not in include.
- `bag_ids` (object): BAG identifiers of the address. Always present; values null when not resolved.
- `coordinates` (object | null): Point of the address (centroid of the unit). null when not resolved or 'coordinates' not in include.
- `building` (object | null): The BAG object and the building(s) it lies in. null when not resolved, 'building' not in include, or the BAG OGC API failed (see warnings).
- `candidates` (array): For ambiguous or not_found rows: up to 3 nearest BAG addresses (display_name, postcode, nummeraanduiding_id, score). Re-run with one of them, or its id in bagIds. Empty when resolved.
- `warnings` (array): Caveats and failures in plain words an agent can relay; the rest of the row is still valid.
- `source_url` (string | null): PDOK record the address (or, for a pand id, the building) was read from; null when not resolved.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the row was made (ISO 8601, UTC).

### Example input

```json
{ "addresses": ["Damrak 1 Amsterdam", "Coolsingel 40, 3011AD Rotterdam", "1012LG 1", "Damrak 18-1 Amsterdam"] }
```

## Weather Forecast API: hourly + daily by city or lat/lon

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/weather-forecast.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/weather-forecast
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/weather-forecast
Price: Apify Store $0.0015 per location forecast

Weather forecast for up to 50 places or coordinates, up to 10 days: hourly temperature, rain, wind, gusts, clouds and humidity plus a daily summary in local time. Source MET Norway (CC BY 4.0), cached per its terms. Unknown places are free.

Example questions:

- Will it rain in Amsterdam tomorrow afternoon?
- Wind speed forecast for these 5 wind farm coordinates, next 48 hours.

### Input fields

- `locations` (array, required): Places to forecast, one per line: a town or city name, optionally with a country or region after a comma ("Amsterdam", "Paris, FR", "Portland, Oregon"), or coordinates as "lat,lon" in decimal degrees, latitude first ("52.3676,4.9041"; rounded to 4 decimals). Place names come from a built-in list of towns of 15,000+ people and capitals; for anything else (a farm, a venue, a wind turbine) give coordinates. Up to 50; repeats are forecast once. One output row per location. Required.
- `hours` (integer): How far ahead to forecast, counted from the current hour, e.g. 48 for today and tomorrow. Max 240 (10 days; MET Norway's forecast ends after about 9.5). Steps are hourly for the first ~2.5 days, then every 6 hours. Default (or empty) = 48.
- `timezone` (string): IANA timezone for output times and daily summaries, e.g. "Europe/Amsterdam", "America/New_York", "UTC". Empty (default) = the place's own timezone for place names, UTC for coordinates.
- `summary` (boolean): true (default) = a daily summary for every day in `hours` plus only the next 12 hourly steps (about 7 KB per location). false = the daily summary plus every forecast step in `hours` (about 18 KB per location for 48 hours, 33 KB for 240). The price is the same.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `input` (string): The location as given.
- `resolved` (boolean): true = a forecast was returned; only these rows are charged.
- `status` (string): ok: forecast returned; not_found: place name not in the built-in list (give 'lat,lon'); invalid_input: coordinates out of range; source_error: MET Norway did not answer.
- `name` (string | null): Matched place as 'name, region, country code', e.g. 'Rotterdam, South Holland, NL'; null for coordinate input.
- `country_code` (string | null): ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the matched place; null for coordinate input.
- `latitude` (number | null): Latitude used, decimal degrees, rounded to 4 decimals.
- `longitude` (number | null): Longitude used, decimal degrees, rounded to 4 decimals.
- `elevation_m` (number | null): Ground height used for the temperature, metres above sea level (MET Norway's, or the place's from GeoNames).
- `timezone` (string | null): IANA timezone of the output times and daily summaries.
- `updated_at` (string | null): When MET Norway's forecast model data were last updated (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `fetched_at` (string | null): When this forecast was fetched from MET Norway (ISO 8601, UTC); may be earlier than the run, because MET's terms require reusing a response until it expires.
- `hours` (integer): Hours ahead covered (the input `hours`); 0 when not resolved.
- `units` (object): Unit of each value field in timeseries and daily.
- `timeseries` (array): Forecast steps in time order: the next 12 hourly steps when summary=true, every step within `hours` when false. Empty when not resolved.
- `daily` (array): One summary per local calendar day within `hours`, derived from the steps. Empty when not resolved.
- `warnings` (array): Plain-language notes: ambiguous place names (with alternatives), UTC default for coordinates, why a location failed.
- `source_url` (string | null): The MET Norway Locationforecast request the forecast comes from; null when not resolved.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `place_source_url` (string | null): GeoNames record of the matched place; null for coordinate input.
- `attribution` (string): Required credit: 'Data from MET Norway (CC BY 4.0)'.
- `attribution_details` (string): Licence link, the note that daily values are derived (not MET Norway's responsibility), and GeoNames credit when a place name was used.
- `retrieved_at` (string): When the row was made (ISO 8601, UTC).

### Example input

```json
{ "locations": ["Rotterdam", "Paris, FR", "Portland, Oregon", "52.3676,4.9041"], "hours": 48 }
```

## Package Vulnerability Check API: CVEs, CISA KEV, safe upgrade

Docs: https://boscolabs.dev/package-vulns.html
Apify Store: https://apify.com/bosco_labs/package-vulns
MCP: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=bosco_labs/package-vulns
Price: Apify Store $0.005 per answer; HTTP API $0.005 per package version or CVE answered
API: POST https://api.boscolabs.dev/v1/package-vulns, $0.005 per package version or CVE answered (max 1 check)

Known vulnerabilities in a package version (npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist) or one CVE/GHSA id: severity, CVSS, fixed versions, CISA KEV exploited status and the lowest safe upgrade; for a CVE also the affected packages. From OSV.dev and CISA, a source link per advisory.

Example questions:

- Before I bump lodash in package.json: is 4.17.15 vulnerable, is anything exploited, and what is the lowest safe version? Cite the advisories.

### Input fields

- `ecosystem` (string): Package registry of `name`, e.g. "npm". One of npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist (also accepted: pip, cargo, rust, golang, composer, gem; any case). Needed with `name`; ignored when `vulnerabilityId` is set. No default.
- `name` (string): Package name exactly as in its registry, e.g. "lodash", "requests", "org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core" (Maven = group:artifact) or "github.com/gin-gonic/gin" (Go module path). When OSV has no advisory, the name (and version) is checked in the registry index; an unknown package fails free of charge. Ignored when `vulnerabilityId` is set.
- `version` (string): Exact version to check, e.g. "4.17.15" (Go: "v1.9.0"). OSV.dev decides whether it falls in an affected range. With a version you also get `safe_version`: the lowest fixed version above it with no known vulnerability. Empty = every advisory for the package at any version (the 40 most severe are listed, no safe_version).
- `vulnerabilityId` (string): One vulnerability id instead of a package, e.g. "CVE-2021-44228" or "GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q" (PYSEC-, GO-, RUSTSEC-, MAL- and OSV- ids work too). Returns the affected packages and version ranges, CISA KEV status, the FIRST EPSS score and NVD's CVSS. When set, the package fields are ignored. Empty = package mode.

### Output fields

- `schema_version` (string): Output schema version.
- `query_type` (string): "package" (ecosystem + name [+ version]) or "vulnerability" (one CVE/GHSA id).
- `ecosystem` (string | null): Ecosystem as OSV names it (npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, NuGet, RubyGems, Packagist); null in vulnerability mode.
- `name` (string | null): Package name as given; null in vulnerability mode.
- `version` (string | null): Version checked; null = all versions (or vulnerability mode).
- `vulnerability_id` (string | null): The CVE/GHSA id asked for, normalised (e.g. CVE-2021-44228); null in package mode.
- `summary` (string): One sentence an agent can pass on: count, max severity, CISA KEV status and the safe version (package), or severity, KEV and affected packages (id).
- `vulnerability_count` (integer | null): Package mode: number of distinct known vulnerabilities (duplicates across databases merged), even when `vulnerabilities` lists only the 40 most severe; 0 = none known (the package was found in its registry, or see warnings). Null in vulnerability mode.
- `known_exploited` (boolean | null): True when any listed vulnerability is in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; false when none is; null when the catalog could not be loaded (see warnings).
- `max_severity` (string | null): Highest severity among the vulnerabilities: CRITICAL, HIGH, MODERATE or LOW (GitHub's label, else from the CVSS v3 score); null when unknown or none.
- `safe_version` (string | null): Package mode with a version: the lowest fixed version above it that OSV reports as having no known vulnerability (the version itself if it is clean). Null without a version, when none was found, or in vulnerability mode.
- `safe_version_note` (string | null): How safe_version was found, or why there is none (e.g. no fix published).
- `epss` (object | null): Vulnerability mode: FIRST EPSS {cve, score (0-1 probability of exploitation activity in the next 30 days), percentile, date, source_url}; null otherwise or when unavailable.
- `nvd` (object | null): Vulnerability mode: NVD record {cve, cvss_score, cvss_severity, cvss_vector, cvss_version, cwe_ids, published, last_modified, vuln_status, description, source_url}; descriptions over 1,000 characters are shortened and marked as shortened by Bosco Labs; null otherwise or when NVD did not answer.
- `vulnerabilities` (array): Known vulnerabilities, most severe first (known exploited, then severity, then CVSS), at most 40; vulnerability mode: one item.
- `source_url` (string): OSV.dev page for the package or the vulnerability id.
- `provided_by` (string): Who compiled this row; cite together with source_url.
- `attribution` (string): Licence and source notices for the data in this row (GitHub Advisory Database CC BY 4.0, CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS, NVD notice, MITRE CVE terms, deps.dev). Keep it when you republish.
- `warnings` (array): Optional sources that failed (KEV, EPSS, NVD, registry existence check), advisories omitted for licence reasons, or a capped list, in plain words.
- `checked_at` (string): When the check ran (ISO 8601, UTC).
- `duration_seconds` (number): Time the check took.

### Example input

```json
{ "ecosystem": "PyPI", "name": "requests", "version": "2.32.5" }
```
